planetary.title: Jupiter Meaning
planetary.overview: Jupiter describes expansion, confidence, opportunity, faith, generosity, learning, teaching, and the way a person grows beyond the familiar. It shows where life tends to open doors, where wisdom is developed, and where excess can become the shadow of abundance.
planetary.cycle: Jupiter spends about one year in each sign, with some variation due to retrograde motion. Its sign describes the style of growth and belief; its house shows where opportunity, learning, and expansion are most likely to gather.

signs.body: Jupiter in Aries grows through courage, initiative, risk, and self-trust. Opportunity opens when the person is willing to begin before every condition is perfect.
Jupiter in Taurus grows through steadiness, resources, embodiment, and the patient building of value. Opportunity opens through consistency and respect for what is tangible.
Jupiter in Gemini grows through curiosity, language, learning, and connection. Opportunity opens through conversation, adaptability, and the willingness to explore many angles.
Jupiter in Cancer grows through care, belonging, home, protection, and emotional wisdom. Opportunity opens through nurturing what matters and creating a safe base.
Jupiter in Leo grows through creativity, confidence, generosity, and visible self-expression. Opportunity opens when the person shares their gifts without apologizing for being seen.
Jupiter in Virgo grows through service, craft, health, refinement, and practical improvement. Opportunity opens when usefulness becomes devotion rather than perfectionism.
Jupiter in Libra grows through partnership, fairness, art, diplomacy, and social intelligence. Opportunity opens through cooperation, balance, and wise relationship choices.
Jupiter in Scorpio grows through depth, trust, intimacy, shared resources, and the courage to face what is hidden. Opportunity opens through emotional honesty and transformation.
Jupiter in Sagittarius grows through travel, study, faith, teaching, and the search for truth. Opportunity opens when the person follows meaning and lets experience become wisdom.
Jupiter in Capricorn grows through discipline, structure, responsibility, and long-range ambition. Opportunity opens when optimism is paired with patience and a real plan.
Jupiter in Aquarius grows through community, innovation, friendship, systems thinking, and future-oriented ideals. Opportunity opens when individual vision serves a wider field.
Jupiter in Pisces grows through compassion, imagination, spiritual openness, art, and trust in what cannot be measured. Opportunity opens through empathy and inspired surrender with boundaries.

planetary.title: Mars Meaning
planetary.overview: Mars describes action, desire, anger, courage, conflict, heat, pursuit, boundaries, and the way a person uses force. It shows how effort is mobilized, how a person fights for what matters, and where raw energy needs direction.
planetary.cycle: Mars usually spends about six to seven weeks in a sign, though retrograde cycles can keep it in one sign for several months. Its sign describes action style and conflict style; its house shows where drive, friction, and initiative concentrate.

signs.body: Mars in Aries acts quickly, directly, and with strong initiative. This placement has clean ignition, but needs a worthy outlet so courage does not become needless conflict.
Mars in Taurus acts slowly but persistently. This placement builds momentum through endurance, but can become immovable when anger has nowhere honest to go.
Mars in Gemini acts through words, ideas, movement, and quick decisions. This placement is mentally sharp and versatile, but needs focus so energy does not scatter.
Mars in Cancer acts protectively and emotionally. This placement fights for home, family, and safety, but must watch indirect anger when needs are not named.
Mars in Leo acts with pride, warmth, creativity, and dramatic force. This placement needs a stage for courage and a purpose that lets effort feel personal.
Mars in Virgo acts through precision, improvement, service, and practical skill. This placement is effective when focused on useful work, but can turn heat into criticism.
Mars in Libra acts through strategy, negotiation, aesthetics, and the pursuit of fairness. This placement fights best when it knows what it wants and stops outsourcing the decision.
Mars in Scorpio acts with depth, intensity, patience, and controlled force. This placement can endure pressure and move with precision, but must watch control as a defense.
Mars in Sagittarius acts through conviction, movement, risk, and the pursuit of truth. This placement needs a horizon, but must make sure belief is embodied in action.
Mars in Capricorn acts with discipline, strategy, endurance, and respect for results. This placement can build real power through patience and directed effort.
Mars in Aquarius acts through principle, innovation, independence, and group-minded change. This placement needs a cause and the freedom to move differently.
Mars in Pisces acts through intuition, compassion, imagination, and subtle timing. This placement needs spiritual or creative purpose, plus boundaries strong enough to keep energy from leaking.

planetary.title: Mercury Meaning
planetary.overview: Mercury describes thought, speech, learning, translation, commerce, movement, humor, and the way a person makes connections between ideas. It shows how information is gathered, sorted, questioned, explained, and exchanged.
planetary.cycle: Mercury usually spends about two to four weeks in a sign, though retrograde cycles can extend its stay. Its sign describes mental style and communication; its house shows where the mind stays busy and where messages need to move.

signs.body: Mercury in Aries thinks quickly, speaks directly, and prefers decisive language. This placement learns by acting and may need to slow down long enough to hear the reply.
Mercury in Taurus thinks carefully, speaks plainly, and trusts what can be tested. This placement needs time to decide, but once the mind is made up it tends to hold steady.
Mercury in Gemini is curious, agile, verbal, and quick to connect ideas. This placement learns through variety, conversation, comparison, and mental movement.
Mercury in Cancer thinks through feeling, memory, and emotional context. Communication is intuitive and protective, and words land best when safety is present.
Mercury in Leo communicates with warmth, confidence, creativity, and dramatic presence. This placement speaks best when the message has heart and personal meaning.
Mercury in Virgo analyzes, edits, improves, and notices what others miss. This placement communicates with precision and is strongest when its discernment serves repair rather than worry.
Mercury in Libra thinks relationally and weighs multiple sides before speaking. This placement is skilled at mediation, diplomacy, aesthetics, and fair-minded conversation.
Mercury in Scorpio investigates beneath the surface and prefers meaningful conversation over empty noise. This placement notices subtext and can speak with penetrating honesty.
Mercury in Sagittarius thinks broadly, speaks candidly, and looks for meaning behind the facts. This placement needs truth, perspective, and room for big questions.
Mercury in Capricorn thinks strategically, practically, and with respect for consequences. This placement communicates best through structure, planning, and clear purpose.
Mercury in Aquarius thinks independently, experimentally, and collectively. This placement is drawn to systems, future possibilities, unusual ideas, and social patterns.
Mercury in Pisces thinks through image, feeling, symbol, and intuition. This placement communicates with imagination and empathy, but needs grounding when details matter.

planetary.title: Moon Meaning
planetary.overview: The Moon describes emotional needs, instinctive reactions, memory, body rhythms, caretaking patterns, and what helps a person feel safe enough to respond rather than defend. It shows the private self: how feelings move, how comfort is sought, and what kind of environment supports steadiness.
planetary.cycle: The Moon travels through the zodiac in about 27.3 days and changes signs roughly every two to two and a half days. Its sign describes emotional style; its house shows where the person seeks safety, familiarity, and nourishment.

signs.body: Moon in Aries feels quickly and responds directly. Emotional safety comes through autonomy, honest action, and the freedom to move instead of waiting for permission.
Moon in Taurus seeks emotional steadiness through comfort, touch, routine, and reliable surroundings. Feelings settle when life feels simple, embodied, and materially secure.
Moon in Gemini processes feelings through language, movement, curiosity, and mental variety. Emotional regulation often comes from naming the feeling and talking it through.
Moon in Cancer is deeply responsive, protective, and tied to home, memory, and belonging. Emotional safety comes through care, privacy, and trusted bonds.
Moon in Leo needs warmth, affection, play, and heartfelt recognition. Feelings want expression, and emotional safety grows when joy and loyalty are present.
Moon in Virgo processes emotions through order, usefulness, observation, and practical care. Safety comes from rhythm, repair, and knowing what can be done next.
Moon in Libra seeks emotional balance through harmony, fairness, beauty, and relational attunement. Safety grows when conflict can be addressed without losing respect.
Moon in Scorpio feels intensely and needs emotional honesty, privacy, and trust. Safety comes from depth, loyalty, and the freedom to name what is usually hidden.
Moon in Sagittarius needs freedom, movement, humor, meaning, and room to breathe. Emotional safety grows when life still feels open and the story can keep expanding.
Moon in Capricorn seeks emotional safety through competence, structure, responsibility, and self-command. Feelings may be private, but they are not absent.
Moon in Aquarius needs space, perspective, friendship, and respect for individuality. Emotional safety grows when feelings can be understood without being crowded.

Moon in Pisces feels through empathy, imagination, atmosphere, and spiritual sensitivity. Safety comes through gentleness, creative release, and boundaries that keep compassion from becoming overwhelm.

planetary.title: Neptune Meaning
planetary.overview: Neptune is a modern interpretive planet associated with dreams, imagination, spirituality, compassion, dissolution, idealization, confusion, and the softening of boundaries. It does not replace traditional rulership logic, but it can describe where certainty blurs and longing becomes powerful.
planetary.cycle: Neptune takes about 165 years to complete the zodiac and spends roughly 14 years in each sign. Its sign is generational; its house and aspects show where inspiration, sensitivity, projection, disillusionment, and spiritual or creative longing gather.

signs.body: Neptune in Aries describes a generation seeking inspiration through independence, action, and spiritual courage. The dream is personal freedom; the risk is confusing impulse with calling.
Neptune in Taurus describes a generation seeking inspiration through nature, the body, art, value, and the material world. The dream is sacred simplicity; the risk is glamorizing security.
Neptune in Gemini describes a generation seeking inspiration through language, media, thought, and exchange. The dream is imaginative connection; the risk is confusion through too many voices.
Neptune in Cancer describes a generation seeking inspiration through home, ancestry, care, and emotional belonging. The dream is spiritual refuge; the risk is idealizing the past.

Neptune in Leo describes a generation seeking inspiration through creativity, performance, romance, and personal radiance. The dream is inspired self-expression; the risk is confusing attention with love.

Neptune in Virgo describes a generation seeking inspiration through service, healing, craft, and practical devotion. The dream is meaningful usefulness; the risk is trying to perfect what needs compassion.
Neptune in Libra describes a generation seeking inspiration through partnership, beauty, peace, and justice. The dream is ideal relationship; the risk is seeing harmony where truth has been avoided.
Neptune in Scorpio describes a generation seeking inspiration through depth, intimacy, mystery, psychology, and hidden power. The dream is total transformation; the risk is glamorizing intensity.

Neptune in Sagittarius describes a generation seeking inspiration through belief, travel, philosophy, and spiritual exploration. The dream is ultimate meaning; the risk is mistaking certainty for wisdom.

Neptune in Capricorn describes a generation seeking inspiration through structure, ambition, institutions, and public purpose. The dream is meaningful authority; the risk is disillusionment with systems.

Neptune in Aquarius describes a generation seeking inspiration through technology, community, social ideals, and collective imagination. The dream is a better future; the risk is idealizing the group.
Neptune in Pisces describes a generation seeking inspiration through compassion, art, spirituality, and collective feeling. The dream is unity; the risk is losing boundaries in the longing to merge.

planetary.title: Pluto Meaning
planetary.overview: Pluto is a modern interpretive planet associated with power, depth, compulsion, exposure, crisis, shadow material, transformation, and rebirth. It does not replace traditional rulership logic, but it can describe where hidden forces intensify and where a person is asked to change at the root.
planetary.cycle: Pluto takes about 248 years to complete the zodiac and spends a variable amount of time in each sign because of its elliptical orbit. Its sign is generational; its house and aspects show where power dynamics, deep endings, repair, and rebirth tend to concentrate.

signs.body: Pluto in Aries describes a generation transforming identity, courage, conflict, and the right to act. Power is confronted through independence and raw initiative.
Pluto in Taurus describes a generation transforming money, land, food, bodies, values, and survival. Power is confronted through attachment, possession, and material security.
Pluto in Gemini describes a generation transforming language, media, education, movement, and information. Power is confronted through ideas and the control of narrative.
Pluto in Cancer describes a generation transforming home, family, ancestry, belonging, and emotional inheritance. Power is confronted through memory and protection.
Pluto in Leo describes a generation transforming creativity, leadership, fame, pleasure, and personal expression. Power is confronted through visibility and the need to be special.
Pluto in Virgo describes a generation transforming labor, health, service, systems, and methods of repair. Power is confronted through usefulness, efficiency, and bodily maintenance.
Pluto in Libra describes a generation transforming partnership, law, beauty, justice, and social contracts. Power is confronted through relationship and the demand for balance.
Pluto in Scorpio describes a generation transforming intimacy, shared resources, taboo, psychology, and hidden power. Power is confronted through emotional truth and deep release.
Pluto in Sagittarius describes a generation transforming belief, education, travel, law, and global worldview. Power is confronted through truth claims and the meaning systems people live by.
Pluto in Capricorn describes a generation transforming institutions, authority, career, government, and social hierarchy. Power is confronted through structure and accountability.
Pluto in Aquarius describes a generation transforming technology, networks, community, social ideals, and collective power. Power is confronted through systems of belonging and exclusion.
Pluto in Pisces describes a generation transforming spirituality, art, compassion, escapism, and collective grief. Power is confronted through what dissolves, heals, or overwhelms.

planetary.title: Saturn Meaning
planetary.overview: Saturn describes structure, limits, discipline, responsibility, time, mastery, consequences, and the work of becoming reliable. It shows where life asks for maturity, where fear can harden into defense, and where sustained effort can become earned authority.
planetary.cycle: Saturn spends about two and a half to three years in each sign, with variation due to retrograde motion. Its sign describes the style of discipline and testing; its house shows where effort, delay, responsibility, and mastery concentrate.

signs.body: Saturn in Aries learns maturity through courage, self-command, and responsible action. The work is to lead without impulsiveness and assert the self without turning every move into a fight.
Saturn in Taurus learns maturity through resources, stability, patience, and self-worth. The work is to build security without becoming trapped by fear of loss.
Saturn in Gemini learns maturity through speech, learning, listening, and mental discipline. The work is to trust the mind while taking communication seriously.
Saturn in Cancer learns maturity through care, family, emotional boundaries, and the creation of safety. The work is to protect without closing the heart.
Saturn in Leo learns maturity through creativity, visibility, confidence, and the right use of pride. The work is to be seen without making recognition the measure of worth.
Saturn in Virgo learns maturity through service, health, craft, and daily discipline. The work is to refine without turning improvement into self-harm.
Saturn in Libra learns maturity through partnership, fairness, commitment, and balanced judgment. The work is to build relationships that are honest, reciprocal, and structurally sound.
Saturn in Scorpio learns maturity through trust, shared resources, intimacy, endings, and emotional honesty. The work is to face depth without using control as armor.
Saturn in Sagittarius learns maturity through belief, study, truth, and lived wisdom. The work is to test convictions against reality and embody the philosophy being taught.
Saturn in Capricorn learns maturity through discipline, structure, leadership, and long-range responsibility. The work is to build with integrity rather than proving worth through achievement alone.
Saturn in Aquarius learns maturity through community, systems, boundaries, and social responsibility. The work is to serve the collective without hiding behind detachment.
Saturn in Pisces learns maturity through compassion, faith, imagination, and spiritual boundaries. The work is to give form to sensitivity without drifting away from reality.

planetary.title: Sun Meaning
planetary.overview: The Sun describes core identity, vitality, creative force, visibility, and the part of the chart that wants to live with purpose. It shows what gives a person energy, what they are learning to embody, and where life asks them to act from the center rather than from imitation or approval-seeking.
planetary.cycle: The Sun moves through the zodiac once each year, spending about one month in each sign. Its sign describes the style of identity and vitality; its house shows the life area where that identity seeks expression.

signs.body: Sun in Aries expresses identity through courage, immediacy, initiative, and the willingness to begin. This placement needs movement, challenge, and room to act directly.
Sun in Taurus expresses identity through steadiness, embodiment, loyalty, and the building of lasting value. This placement needs stability, beauty, and a life that can be trusted by the senses.
Sun in Gemini expresses identity through curiosity, language, movement, and connection. This placement needs variety, conversation, learning, and room to keep asking better questions.
Sun in Cancer expresses identity through care, protection, memory, and emotional intelligence. This placement needs belonging, privacy, and a life rooted in what feels safe and meaningful.
Sun in Leo expresses identity through creativity, warmth, visibility, and personal radiance. This placement needs joy, self-expression, and permission to be seen without performing for approval.

Sun in Virgo expresses identity through discernment, craft, service, repair, and attention to what can be improved. This placement needs useful work and a way to serve without reducing the self to flaws.
Sun in Libra expresses identity through relationship, balance, beauty, fairness, and social awareness. This placement needs reciprocity and the courage to choose without disappearing into compromise.

Sun in Scorpio expresses identity through depth, emotional honesty, trust, and transformation. This placement needs real intimacy, privacy, and the strength to release control when truth is asking to surface.
Sun in Sagittarius expresses identity through meaning, movement, candor, learning, and the search for a wider horizon. This placement needs freedom, truth, and experience that becomes wisdom.
Sun in Capricorn expresses identity through discipline, responsibility, structure, and earned authority. This placement needs goals that matter and a path where effort can become legacy.

Sun in Aquarius expresses identity through originality, perspective, community, and future-minded change. This placement needs room to be different while staying connected to something larger than the self.

Sun in Pisces expresses identity through empathy, imagination, spiritual sensitivity, and porous awareness. This placement needs compassion, creative space, and boundaries strong enough to protect openness.

planetary.title: Uranus Meaning
planetary.overview: Uranus is a modern interpretive planet associated with disruption, liberation, invention, awakening, instability, and the refusal to keep living inside a pattern that has gone stale. It does not replace traditional rulership logic, but it can describe the flavor of sudden change and individuation.
planetary.cycle: Uranus takes about 84 years to complete the zodiac and spends roughly seven years in each sign. Its sign is often generational; its house and aspects show where the person experiences surprise, freedom, reinvention, and breaks from convention.

signs.body: Uranus in Aries describes a generation that disrupts through courage, independence, and bold action. Innovation comes through refusal to wait for permission.
Uranus in Taurus describes disruption around money, land, food, bodies, values, and material security. Innovation comes through changing what stability means.
Uranus in Gemini describes disruption through language, media, education, mobility, and information systems. Innovation comes through new ways of thinking and connecting.
Uranus in Cancer describes disruption around home, family, belonging, and emotional inheritance. Innovation comes through redefining protection and private life.
Uranus in Leo describes disruption through creativity, performance, leadership, and personal expression. Innovation comes through new ways of being seen.
Uranus in Virgo describes disruption around work, health, service, systems, and daily process. Innovation comes through better methods and practical reform.
Uranus in Libra describes disruption around partnership, justice, aesthetics, and social agreements. Innovation comes through changing how people relate and negotiate.
Uranus in Scorpio describes disruption around intimacy, shared resources, power, psychology, and taboo material. Innovation comes through confronting what was hidden.
Uranus in Sagittarius describes disruption around belief, travel, education, law, publishing, and global perspective. Innovation comes through challenging inherited truths.
Uranus in Capricorn describes disruption around institutions, authority, career, government, and long-standing structures. Innovation comes through rebuilding systems.
Uranus in Aquarius describes disruption around networks, technology, community, social ideals, and collective futures. Innovation comes through new forms of belonging.
Uranus in Pisces describes disruption around spirituality, compassion, art, dreams, and collective sensitivity. Innovation comes through awakening what had been submerged.

planetary.title: Venus Meaning
planetary.overview: Venus describes attraction, affection, pleasure, beauty, social ease, values, money, taste, and the way a person gives and receives sweetness. It shows what feels desirable, what feels worth protecting, and how harmony is created or avoided.
planetary.cycle: Venus usually spends about three to five weeks in a sign, though retrograde cycles can extend the stay. Its sign describes love style, values, and aesthetic preference; its house shows where connection, pleasure, and value-seeking become most visible.

signs.body: Venus in Aries loves directly, boldly, and with appetite for pursuit. This placement needs aliveness, honesty, and the freedom to want what it wants without over-explaining desire.
Venus in Taurus loves through steadiness, touch, loyalty, pleasure, and material care. This placement needs consistency and a love that can be felt in the body.
Venus in Gemini loves through conversation, curiosity, wit, and mental connection. This placement needs variety, laughter, and a partner who keeps the mind awake.
Venus in Cancer loves protectively, tenderly, and through emotional memory. This placement needs trust, care, and a bond that feels like a safe place to land.
Venus in Leo loves warmly, generously, creatively, and with a need for visible affection. This placement needs admiration, play, loyalty, and romance with heart.
Venus in Virgo loves through service, attention, repair, and thoughtful detail. This placement needs sincerity and may show devotion by noticing what would make life easier.
Venus in Libra loves through reciprocity, beauty, fairness, and partnership. This placement needs mutuality and can create harmony without losing the ability to choose.
Venus in Scorpio loves intensely, privately, and with a need for emotional truth. This placement needs trust, depth, and relationships that can hold real vulnerability.
Venus in Sagittarius loves through honesty, adventure, humor, and shared meaning. This placement needs freedom and a bond that makes life feel wider.
Venus in Capricorn loves seriously, loyally, and through commitment that proves itself over time. This placement needs reliability, maturity, and shared long-term values.
Venus in Aquarius loves through friendship, ideals, freedom, and respect for difference. This placement needs space inside connection and a bond that can hold individuality.
Venus in Pisces loves compassionately, imaginatively, and with great emotional openness. This placement needs tenderness, inspiration, and boundaries that keep devotion from becoming self-loss.

points.orbit: Approximately 9 years through the zodiac; roughly 9 months per sign.
points.core: The disowned, uncompromising self. Black Moon Lilith marks raw instinct that refuses to be tamed, shamed, or controlled, and the place where autonomy and unfiltered truth are reclaimed.
points.note: Read psychologically around autonomy and refusal to comply, not as fate or as a lurid archetype.
points.policy: Modern point; secondary weighting only. Not used in dignity, sect, or time-lord logic, and never treated as a primary chart ruler. Weight up only when it aspects a personal planet or angle, or sits on an angle.

points.orbit: Approximately 50 years, between Saturn and Uranus; time per sign is uneven, roughly 2 to 8 years.
points.core: The deep, lasting wound and the path through it. Chiron marks where a person may feel broken, not enough, or too much, and where working honestly with that wound can become medicine they later offer others.
points.keyTransit: The Chiron return near age 50 brings the core wound back for confrontation, integration, and a more conscious relationship with the old pattern.
points.policy: Modern point; secondary weighting only. Not used in dignity, sect, or time-lord logic, and never treated as a primary chart ruler. Weight up only when it aspects a personal planet or angle, or sits on an angle.

points.orbit: Calculated intersection of the Moon's orbit with the ecliptic; always opposite the South Node.
points.core: Growth direction, unfamiliar medicine, the qualities and life field that ask for conscious development.
points.keyTransit: Nodal returns, nodal reversals, eclipses, and transiting nodes to angles or personal planets can mark developmental thresholds and important meetings, choices, or releases.
points.policy: Lunar node; calculated point, not a planet. Use as a developmental axis and timing factor. Do not use for dignity, sect, rulership, or planetary condition.

pointPlacements.tldr: Lilith in the 1st house: your raw, untamed self shows openly
pointPlacements.body: Lilith in the 1st house: your raw, untamed self shows openly. Where you refuse to be tamed and reclaim your right to take up space. Watch: defiance that pushes people away. You are uncompromising about who you are; you refuse to be told how to be, and it shows on sight. Strongly colors the whole personality; intense drives that often sit hidden in the unconscious. The work is to understand and own the energy rather than be unconsciously run by it.
pointPlacements.business: A magnetic, undeniable presence when owned.
pointPlacements.shadow: A confrontational identity, or hiding the raw self behind a guarded front.

pointPlacements.body: Lilith in the 10th house: the untamed in public life. Where you reclaim power and visibility outside the rules. Watch: a reputation built on defiance, or being cast as the villain. You refuse to be controlled in public life; raw ambition that will not play the expected role. Needs unconventional, self-directed work and resists rigid authority; may go marginal or self-employed. Originality is an asset in creative fields, a liability in rigid ones.
pointPlacements.business: Authority claimed on your own terms, often as an outsider.
pointPlacements.shadow: Self-sabotage of reputation, or a combative public face.

pointPlacements.tldr: Lilith in the 11th house: the outsider in the group
pointPlacements.body: Lilith in the 11th house: the outsider in the group. Where you reclaim belonging on your own terms and disrupt the collective. Watch: alienating the people who would have you. You refuse to belong to the group on its terms; raw nonconformity in community and friendship. Idealistic and highly selective about friends and groups; risks over-demanding others and feeling betrayed. Wants to make a unique contribution, but needs realism so perfectionism doesn't deliver nothing.

angles.tldr: Aquarius rising: independent, observant, and built slightly outside the expected pattern.
angles.body: With Aquarius rising, you meet life through perspective, originality, and an instinct for the collective field. Your path asks you to stay true to your difference without using detachment as a wall.

angles.body: With Aries rising, the first move is action. You tend to meet the world directly, respond quickly, and learn by entering the situation rather than waiting until every variable is settled.
angles.approach: Initiates fast, leads with instinct, and prefers momentum over prolonged deliberation.

modifiers.summary: Safety and ethics policy for any addiction-pattern or recovery-support content in the knowledge base.
modifiers.body: Addiction-related astrology content is sensitive, optional, and non-clinical. It must be framed as pattern awareness with constructive support, never as diagnosis, inevitability, shame, or medical guidance.
modifiers.definition: A review policy governing how addiction-support interpretations can be authored, reviewed, and surfaced.
appUsage: Require human review before changing any addiction-support status beyond DRAFT.
Keep this content behind an app-level sensitive-content toggle unless a separate product decision says otherwise.
If a user signals active struggle, crisis, or risk, prioritize support options over astrological interpretation.
Use region-appropriate support resources and avoid categorical promises about outcomes.
modifiers.note: Imported from the project support bundle. Source files were not copied into the repository.

principles: Descriptive, not deterministic. A chart never causes, predicts, or excuses addiction.
Never diagnostic. This content is not medical or clinical advice and does not replace care.
Recovery-oriented. Difficulty is workable; the chart is a mirror for awareness, paired always with action and support.
Agency first. The person, not the planets, is the author of change.
prohibitedFramings: Any 'your chart dooms you to addiction' or inevitable framing.
Romanticizing, glamorizing, or normalizing substance use or any addictive behavior.
Using astrology to delay, substitute for, or argue against professional treatment.
Dwelling on or sensationalizing overdose losses or specific named tragedies.
Clinical or diagnostic claims about a person's mind, body, or substance use.
requiredFramings: Pair every pattern with a constructive channel and a pointer toward real support.
State plainly that recovery is possible and help exists.
Keep the energy workable, not a sentence.

safety.activeStruggle: If a user signals active struggle, crisis, or risk, the product leads with support options, not an astrological explanation. Astrology never rationalizes or replaces care.
safety.resources: Surface region-appropriate support. For US users, an example is the SAMHSA National Helpline, 1-800-662-4357 (free, confidential, 24/7). Do not make categorical promises about confidentiality or outcomes; let users choose.
safety.doNot: Do not provide instructions, dosing, sourcing, or any how-to relating to substances.

classes.reviewGate: All addiction/recovery content stays DRAFT until reviewed against this policy. This policy needs human sign-off before any such content ships READY.

signatures.constructiveChannel: Neptune's higher octave: creativity, music and art, meditation, spiritual practice, service, time near water or rest. Feed the longing for transcendence through inspiration, not anesthesia.
signatures.support: Pair self-reflection with grounding routines and, where needed, professional or peer support.

signatures.pattern: Hard aspects to Neptune can intensify fogginess, self-deception, and the pull to escape pain rather than face it.

signatures.support: These are good moments to lean on guidance rather than decide or 'sign on the dotted line' alone.

signatures.pattern: Neptune emphasis in the 8th (shared depths, loss, vulnerability) or 12th (the hidden, solitude) can make anesthesia tempting where the material is painful.

signatures.support: Spiritual or psychological guidance noticeably lowers the pull toward avoidance and self-destructive habit here.

signatures.constructiveChannel: Identify the actual need under the urge, and meet it directly: rest, connection, creative expression, being heard.

signatures.pattern: Pluto themes can show up as compulsion, obsession, or the use of control to manage what feels overwhelming.
signatures.constructiveChannel: Self-awareness is the lever. Naming the darker pattern honestly is what loosens its grip and opens transformation.

signatures.constructiveChannel: The growth direction is the opposite: come back into the body, build routine, focus on the here and now, be of service, value the small concrete details.

Transiting Uranus to natal Pluto can break a compulsive grip. Self-awareness becomes the key to leaving self-defeating behavior behind.

being heard by a trusted person

modifiers.definition: A planet's house position sets how strongly and quickly it acts. Angular planets are loud and active; cadent planets are quiet and slow.

angular.effect: Strong, prominent, fast to manifest. Events 'happen'.

cadent.effect: Weaker, more mental or transitional, slow to externalize.

modifiers.appUsage: Weight a placement or transit UP when the planet is angular, DOWN when cadent. An angular transit is a headline; a cadent one is background. Combine with dignity: angular + dignified is the strongest signal, cadent + debilitated the weakest.
modifiers.summary: Angularity weights how strongly and quickly a planet acts by house position.

modifiers.summary: Aspect cycle language reads each aspect as a phase in an unfolding planetary relationship rather than a fixed good-or-bad verdict.
modifiers.body: An aspect is not a fixed verdict. It is a phase in the ongoing cycle between two planets, from conjunction as the seed of a new cycle, through opposition as full visibility, and back to the next conjunction. The same angle can mean different things depending on whether it is waxing or waning.
modifiers.definition: A process-oriented aspect method that reads planetary aspects as cycle phases, with waxing aspects building outward and waning aspects distributing, questioning, integrating, and releasing.
appUsage: Layer this onto existing transit, natal, synastry, and composite aspect interpretations.
Use waxing or waning phase to refine the task of the aspect without replacing the base meaning.
For user-facing copy, translate waxing contacts as building, developing, acting, and testing form.
Translate waning contacts as sharing, integrating, questioning, completing, and releasing.
Do not turn aspect type alone into a fixed positive or negative verdict.
modifiers.note: Imported from approved project aspect-cycle material. Source files were not copied into the repository.

classes.coreReframe: An aspect is not a fixed good-or-bad verdict. It is a phase in the ongoing cycle of relationship between two planets, from conjunction as the seed of a new cycle through opposition as full visibility and back to the next conjunction. The same angle can mean different things depending on where it falls in that cycle.

hemicycles.waxing: From conjunction to opposition. Energy builds outward: instinctive, action-driven, developing the impulse. The question is: how do I grow and build this?
hemicycles.waning: From opposition back to conjunction. Energy is shared and released: conscious, meaning-driven, distributing and releasing what was realized. The question is: what does this mean, and what do I release?
hemicycles.howToTell: Compare the two planets. If the faster planet is 0 to 180 degrees ahead of the slower one, moving toward the opposition, the aspect is waxing. From 180 back toward 360, it is waning.

classes.vocabularyNote: In the waning half of the cycle, release and releasing are accurate terms, as in the lunar cycle's waning phases.

majorAspects.plainTranslation: Conjunction, 0 degrees: the seed of a new cycle. The two energies fuse into a single fresh impulse, instinctive and not yet conscious. A beginning full of potential that you act on before you fully understand it.

majorAspects.waning: Share and release what you have already developed.
majorAspects.plainTranslation: Sextile, 60 degrees: an opening that asks for effort. The two energies can cooperate, but not on their own; you have to take the opportunity.

majorAspects.waxing: Crisis in action: building structure against resistance, the hard push to make something real.
majorAspects.waning: Crisis in consciousness: questioning whether what you built still has meaning, and releasing what is outgrown.
majorAspects.plainTranslation: Square, 90 degrees: a crisis and turning point that demands action. The same 90 degrees points in different directions depending on whether it is waxing or waning.

majorAspects.waxing: The impulse finds its first comfortable form.
majorAspects.waning: Sharing and releasing what was realized, with a risk of coasting.
majorAspects.plainTranslation: Trine, 120 degrees: ease and natural flow; the energies cooperate without friction. The gift is fluency; the trap is taking it for granted.

Opposition, 180 degrees: the peak of the cycle. The two energies face each other and become fully conscious, often through other people or outside events. Fulfillment, or a confrontation that forces clarity.

minorAspects.plainTranslation: Quintile, 72 degrees: the creative, individual stamp; the unique style someone brings to something.
Septile, about 51 degrees: an inspired thread; a sense of being moved by something beyond ordinary logic.
Novile, 40 degrees: gestation; something developing privately before it is ready to show.

examples.plainTranslation: A waxing Mars-Saturn square is a crisis of action: pushing drive against hard limits and building discipline the hard way. A waning Mars-Saturn square is a crisis of consciousness: questioning whether the structure that was built still serves, and beginning to release it. Same 90 degrees, different tasks.

The conjunction is a fresh, instinctive urge to grow, fused with identity and acted on before it is understood. The opposition is that same growth made visible and tested through circumstances or other people, where it can finally be seen more objectively.
The opening is there for graceful, warm communication, but it stays potential until used. Unlike a trine, it will not flow on its own.

classes.integration: A lens layered on the existing aspect corpora: transit, synastry, and composite. It does not replace them; it adds the waxing or waning distinction and the phase reading. It is consistent with progressed lunation cycle logic, where the same cycle is applied to the Sun and Moon.

prohibitions: Do not use aspect type alone as a fixed good-or-bad verdict.
Do not let waxing or waning phase override the planet pair, aspect type, house context, dignity, sect, or timing testimony.
Do not apply same-moment aspect exclusions to transit-to-natal lookup.
weighting: Use aspect-cycle phase as a refinement layer after the base interpretation is selected.
Waxing aspects emphasize development, action, outward growth, and form-building.
Waning aspects emphasize integration, distribution, meaning, completion, and release.
Oppositions describe peak visibility and full awareness in the cycle.
Conjunctions describe cycle beginnings and fused potential.

modifiers.summary: Aspect lookup must choose the correct regime first: same-moment pairs are canonicalized and have 11 impossible inner-planet aspects; transit-to-natal aspects are ordered and have no impossible exclusions.
modifiers.body: Use this policy to prevent two different aspect regimes from being mixed. Same-moment aspects measure both bodies at one instant, so Sun, Mercury, and Venus elongation limits make 11 combinations impossible. Transit-to-natal aspects measure a moving transiting body against a fixed natal point, so every ordered planet-aspect-planet combination can occur and must not be filtered by same-moment exclusions.
modifiers.definition: Lookup and validity policy for same-moment aspect files versus transit-to-natal aspect lookups.
appUsage: Pick the regime before lookup.
For same-moment aspects, canonicalize the pair using canonical_order, then skip file reads for impossible combinations.
For transit-to-natal aspects, preserve order as transiting planet -> natal point and do not apply impossible exclusions.
Do not treat missing Moon aspects as elongation exclusions; the Moon has no elongation cap in this policy.
Do not create reverse-order same-moment files. Reverse spellings are aliases of canonical keys.
modifiers.note: Normalized from approved project aspect policy JSON. Source file was not copied into the repository.

classes.dedupRule: Every same-moment pair is stored and looked up under canonical_order. The reverse spelling (e.g. mercury_sun) is an ALIAS of the canonical key (sun_mercury), never a separate file. Resolve order before lookup.

same_moment.rationale: Both bodies are measured at one instant, so inner-planet elongation caps the maximum separation. The combinations below cannot occur. The app must NOT request or expect a file for them.
same_moment.moon_rule: The Moon has NO elongation limit. All five aspects to all nine other bodies are valid. A missing Moon file is a gap to fill, not an exclusion.

applies_to: daily check-in: transiting planet -> natal planet
transit_to_natal.rationale: Bodies are not co-measured. A transiting planet sweeps the entire zodiac against a fixed natal point, so it can form ANY of the five aspects to ANY natal point. The same_moment impossibilities DO NOT apply here. Do not filter transit-to-natal lookups through the impossible set.

classes.lookupContract: Pick the regime first. For same_moment: canonicalize the pair, then if (pair, aspect) is in impossible -> return no-match WITHOUT a file read. For transit_to_natal: keep order (transiting, natal), never apply the impossible set.
classes.fileNameStyle: Repository transit aspect files use hyphenated canonical same-moment ids: planet-aspect-planet. App lookup keys may use underscores internally, but must map to this file naming convention.

prohibitions: Do not apply same-moment elongation exclusions to transit-to-natal readings.
Do not request same-moment files for impossible Sun-Mercury, Sun-Venus, or Mercury-Venus aspects listed in this policy.
Do not create reverse-order duplicate same-moment files.
Do not exclude Moon aspects under the elongation rule.
weighting: This policy controls lookup validity, not interpretation weight.
Same-moment aspect files in data/transits are canonical pair files, not ordered transit-to-natal files.
Transit-to-natal interpretation support should be handled by ordered lookup logic or a separate ordered corpus if authored later.

modifiers.definition: The master weighting rule. Benefics improve what they touch (bonification); malefics harm what they touch (maltreatment). This decides whether a given meaning resolves well or badly.

bonification.effect: A planet or point a benefic conjoins or aspects (especially by trine or sextile, in tight orb) is helped, protected, and its outcomes improved.
bonification.strength: The in-sect benefic (Jupiter by day, Venus by night) bonifies most strongly.

maltreatment.effect: A planet or point a malefic conjoins, squares, or opposes (in tight orb) is harmed and its outcomes worsened.
maltreatment.strength: The out-of-sect malefic (Saturn by night, Mars by day) maltreats most harshly; a dignified or in-sect malefic does far less damage.

modifiers.overcoming: The planet in the earlier zodiacal degree holds the superior position and dominates the relationship, especially across a square.
modifiers.appUsage: After reading a transit, scan for a benefic or malefic also aspecting the same point. Benefic present -> weight the outcome UP. Malefic present -> weight it DOWN, more so if out of sect. This converts a neutral meaning into a good or bad day.
modifiers.summary: Benefic and malefic contacts weight whether an indication resolves more easily or more harshly.
modifiers.body: The master weighting rule. Benefics improve what they touch (bonification); malefics harm what they touch (maltreatment). This decides whether a given meaning resolves well or badly.

modifiers.definition: The chart ruler (lord of the Ascendant, lord of the chart) is the planet that rules the rising sign. It is the most personal significator of the native: the steering planet of the whole life. Where it sits and how well it is conditioned describes the direction and quality of the life.

determination.rule: Take the rising sign and find its traditional domicile ruler (use dignity.domicile). That planet is the chart ruler.
determination.modernCoRuler: For Scorpio, Aquarius, and Pisces a modern co-ruler may be read only as a secondary modern lens. The traditional ruler stays primary and is the one used for naming, weighting, dignity, sect, and time-lord logic.

surfacePolicy.default: Default chart-ruler text names the traditional ruler as the chart ruler.
surfacePolicy.modernLens: Modern co-rulers may appear in an explicitly labeled modern lens field or view. Phrase them as modern lenses, not replacements.
surfacePolicy.doNotSurfaceAsRuler: Do not describe Pluto, Uranus, or Neptune as the chart ruler. For Scorpio, say Mars is the traditional ruler and Pluto is the modern lens. For Aquarius, say Saturn is the traditional ruler and Uranus is the modern lens. For Pisces, say Jupiter is the traditional ruler and Neptune is the modern lens.

howToRead: The rising sign sets the style; its ruler is the agent that carries that style into the world.
The HOUSE the chart ruler occupies shows where the life is steered, where the main story unfolds.
The SIGN it occupies shows the manner in which the life is pursued.
Its dignity (use the dignity scoring) shows how effectively the native pursues their direction: a debilitated chart ruler means a harder, more obstructed path.
Its sect status (in/out of sect) and solar phase (combust, cazimi, under the beams) further weight how cleanly it operates.
Aspects to the chart ruler are the main forces helping or blocking the life direction.
modifiers.appUsage: Rank transits to the chart ruler among the most personally significant in any day, alongside transits to the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant. A transit to the chart ruler speaks to the whole life-direction, not one lane; weight it up across all three lanes (business, creative, self).
modifiers.summary: The chart ruler is the ruler of the rising sign and describes the steering planet of the life.
modifiers.body: The chart ruler (lord of the Ascendant, lord of the chart) is the planet that rules the rising sign. It is the most personal significator of the native: the steering planet of the whole life. Where it sits and how well it is conditioned describes the direction and quality of the life.

modifiers.summary: The chart speaks most clearly about the shape of the story, less clearly about the choices made within it, and least clearly about the exact scenes through which it unfolds.
modifiers.body: Use this stance to keep readings descriptive rather than deterministic. The chart can describe themes, arcs, pressures, patterns, and timing windows with meaningful confidence. It cannot honestly guarantee exact scenes, fixed outcomes, or the user's choices.
modifiers.definition: A graded-clarity policy for astrological interpretation: read the arc with confidence, hold the choices as open, and treat exact events as too contingent to promise.
appUsage: Use this as an ethics anchor for chart, transit, progression, synastry, and timing features.
Describe the arc and active pattern clearly.
Frame choices as open and user-led.
Do not sell exact scenes, outcomes, dates, jobs, relationships, or decisions as fixed.
When the app gives examples, label them as possible expressions of a pattern rather than guaranteed events.
modifiers.note: Original project stance. Added as policy material; no external source file was copied into the repository.

classes.anchor: The chart speaks most clearly about the shape of the story, less clearly about the choices made within it, and least clearly about the exact scenes through which it unfolds.

layers.name: The shape of the story
layers.plainTranslation: Your nature, your themes, the arc you're living. This is where the chart is loudest. Read it.

layers.name: The choices made within it
layers.plainTranslation: The choices you make inside that shape. The chart hints; it doesn't decide. This part is on you.

layers.name: The exact scenes
layers.plainTranslation: The job, the date, the timing. The chart can't call these. Too many hands on them, yours most of all.

principles: Read the arc with confidence. Hold the choices as open. Treat the scenes as un-callable.
The further you push toward naming exact events, the less the chart can honestly say.
It's for understanding the shape you're in, not fortune-telling. Direction, not scenes.
Nothing here is fixed. The chart isn't a verdict. You're still the one driving.
classes.useInProduct: Anchors the descriptive-not-deterministic stance in the ethics policies. Read the arc with confidence, the choices as open, the events as un-callable. Never sell a scene as fixed.

prohibitions: Do not frame astrology as a verdict.
Do not present exact life scenes as guaranteed.
Do not remove user agency from timing or compatibility features.
Do not treat examples as predictions.
weighting: Arc-level interpretation can be stated with the most confidence.
Choice-level interpretation should be framed as available paths and pressures.
Event-level interpretation should be framed as possible expressions only when multiple indicators repeat.
Exact dates and exact outcomes require the strongest caution language.

modifiers.summary: Chiron cycle milestones describe recurring wound-and-repair themes, culminating in the Chiron return around age 50-51.
modifiers.body: Use Chiron cycle milestones as a modern secondary timing layer. The cycle can describe when an old wound becomes visible, when the person meets helpers or mirrors, and when the same theme returns with more consciousness. It is not a traditional timing factor and should not override planets, houses, rulers, sect, dignity, or time-lord logic.
modifiers.definition: Chiron has an uneven orbit of about 50 years. Its squares, opposition, trines, sextiles, and return can arrive at different ages depending on natal placement, so exact degree calculation matters more than age estimates.
appUsage: Label this as a modern Chiron life-cycle layer, not a traditional timing doctrine.
Use exact transit-to-natal Chiron contacts rather than age alone whenever possible.
Read the natal Chiron sign, house, and close aspects before giving a cycle example.
Surface examples as possible life areas for reflection, not as fixed events.
Weight up when Chiron contacts the Sun, Moon, Ascendant, MC, Venus, Mars, chart ruler, or a strongly activated house.
modifiers.note: Distilled from approved project Chiron source material. Source files were not copied into the repository.

cycleFacts.period: about 50 years, with uneven time in signs
cycleFacts.ageCaution: Early cycle contacts vary widely by natal Chiron position; calculate exact contacts before showing timing.
cycleFacts.coreTheme: The same sore place returns at different maturity levels: first as something that happens to the person, later as something they can name, work with, and sometimes help others understand.

milestones.plainTranslation: Early opportunity to notice a healing thread, often before the person has language for it. Interests, helpers, or subtle clues can appear and make sense later.
examples: a child developing an unusual interest that later becomes meaningful
a supportive teacher, friend, or healer appearing early
a first hint of the gift wrapped inside the sore place

milestones.plainTranslation: The first sharp activation of the wound. Depending on age, the person may experience it as something done by others before they understand the pattern.
examples: feeling singled out around identity, body, voice, belonging, family, or competence
a painful experience that repeats the original wound theme
a sudden awareness that there is more going on beneath the visible life

milestones.plainTranslation: A more supportive opening in the cycle. The person may meet helpers, mentors, teachers, or friends who give language and tools for the wound.
examples: finding a mentor who names the pattern
discovering therapy, healing work, art, teaching, or advocacy as a path
realizing the wound can become skill rather than only pain

milestones.plainTranslation: The wound becomes visible across the room. The person can begin to understand how the old hurt has shaped choices, relationships, and identity.
examples: seeing the shadow pattern clearly for the first time
a relationship, teacher, client, or crisis mirroring the wound back
realizing that the old defense is no longer protecting the life being built

milestones.plainTranslation: Another healing opening, often close enough to the Uranus midlife cycle to accelerate growth. People or circumstances can help the person move closer to purpose.
examples: meeting a guide, practitioner, peer group, or community that speeds integration
turning personal healing into study, service, or creative work
choosing a path that feels more honest than the inherited one

milestones.plainTranslation: Unhealed material demands attention again. If it overlaps the Uranus opposition, the experience can feel intense because healing and freedom are asking for change at the same time.
examples: old pain showing up through relationship, body, work, family, or purpose questions
a need to stop betraying the self to meet an expected life script
a turning point where the person chooses repair over repetition

milestones.plainTranslation: A later opportunity to practice the healing with more awareness. The person often has better tools, clearer boundaries, and more capacity to choose support.
examples: creative work gaining depth from lived experience
finding people who support growth instead of repeating the wound
using hard-won insight to help someone else without rescuing them

milestones.plainTranslation: The Chiron return brings the original wound theme back for integration. The question is no longer only what hurt; it is what the person now knows, teaches, protects, repairs, or refuses to keep repeating.
examples: a long-running identity, relationship, family, body, or purpose wound becoming impossible to ignore
choosing therapy, mentorship, teaching, advocacy, caregiving, art, or spiritual practice with more maturity
turning the old sore place into a boundary, vocation, or medicine for others

examplePatternsByHouse.1: Identity, body, visibility, autonomy, and the fear of unintentionally hurting others through self-assertion.
examplePatternsByHouse.2: Body comfort, money, food, possessions, self-worth, and learning to treat human needs without shame.
examplePatternsByHouse.3: Voice, learning, language, siblings, school, daily movement, and the wound of not being understood.
examplePatternsByHouse.4: Family, parents, home, belonging, emotional safety, and the habit of seeking unavailable people as a substitute for the old unmet need.
examplePatternsByHouse.5: Creativity, joy, romance, children, performance, and the fear that self-expression will be mocked or rejected.
examplePatternsByHouse.6: Work, health, service, routines, usefulness, and the pressure to fix what hurts through control or over-functioning.
examplePatternsByHouse.7: Partnership, projection, abandonment, repair through reciprocity, and learning not to make another person the whole medicine.
examplePatternsByHouse.8: Trust, intimacy, shared resources, grief, dependency, and the courage to face what the person would rather keep buried.
examplePatternsByHouse.9: Faith, education, worldview, teachers, belonging to a larger meaning system, and healing the wound around belief.
examplePatternsByHouse.10: Authority, career, reputation, legacy, public competence, and the fear of being exposed as not enough.
examplePatternsByHouse.11: Friendship, community, future, group belonging, exclusion, and learning to contribute without losing individuality.
examplePatternsByHouse.12: Solitude, hidden pain, dreams, retreat, old endings, and healing what was carried silently or unconsciously.

prohibitions: Do not call Chiron a planet or a traditional timing factor.
Do not use Chiron to diagnose trauma, illness, or psychological pathology.
Do not frame the wound as permanent damage or fate.
Do not tell users they must become healers, teachers, or spiritual practitioners because of Chiron.
weighting: Exact transit-to-natal Chiron contacts are stronger than age estimates.
Contacts to Sun, Moon, Ascendant, MC, Venus, Mars, chart ruler, or angular houses increase relevance.
Repeated testimony from the natal Chiron placement, current transits, progressions, returns, or activated houses is required before naming concrete examples.
Use as optional modern-points content and keep it hidden unless the user enables Chiron or asks for healing/shadow material.

modifiers.summary: A composite chart describes the relationship as its own entity, including its shared purpose, emotional climate, communication pattern, affection style, conflict style, growth path, limits, instability, fog, intensity, and visible style.
modifiers.body: Use the composite chart after each natal chart and the synastry contacts. Synastry describes how two people activate each other; the composite describes the bond as a third pattern with its own center of gravity. Read it as a relationship climate, not as proof that a relationship should continue, end, or become permanent.
modifiers.definition: The composite chart is a relationship chart created from the midpoint structure of two natal charts. It is used to describe the shared field of the relationship rather than either person alone.
appUsage: Read order: each natal relationship pattern, synastry contacts and overlays, then composite chart.
Use Composite Sun, Moon, Ascendant, Venus, Mars, and Saturn as the core relationship layer before outer-planet details.
Do not use a composite chart as a verdict. Present strengths, pressure points, and choices.
Weight hard Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto contacts carefully because they can describe real strain, instability, fog, or power dynamics.
For relationship summaries, prefer concrete language: purpose, daily emotional climate, communication, affection, conflict, commitment, and repair.
modifiers.note: Expanded from approved project composite, relationship, marquee, and relationship-method source material. Source files were not copied into the repository.

readingOrder: Read each natal chart first to understand the people in the relationship.
Read synastry next to identify activation, attraction, friction, and house overlays.
Read the composite chart last to describe the shared relationship pattern.
Separate chemistry from durability, and separate intensity from health.

coreFactors.sun: Purpose, identity, vitality, and the central reason the relationship organizes around.
coreFactors.moon: Daily emotional climate, comfort needs, instinctive reactions, and how safe the relationship feels from the inside.
coreFactors.ascendant: The relationship's visible style, first impression, and automatic way of meeting the world as a pair.
coreFactors.mercury: Communication style, mental rhythm, problem-solving, and how the relationship talks itself through experience.
coreFactors.venus: Affection, pleasure, ease, social grace, attraction, and what makes the relationship feel worth choosing.
coreFactors.mars: Desire, conflict, action, sexual heat, initiative, anger, and how the relationship pushes or fights.
coreFactors.jupiter: Growth, generosity, humor, opportunity, shared faith, and where the relationship can become larger than either person alone.
coreFactors.saturn: Commitment, duty, structure, delay, fear, restraint, endurance, and the tests the relationship must handle honestly.
coreFactors.uranus: Change, freedom, disruption, novelty, unconventional rhythm, and whether the relationship can tolerate instability.
coreFactors.neptune: Compassion, imagination, idealization, spiritual longing, confusion, secrecy, sacrifice, and the need for realism.
coreFactors.pluto: Intensity, transformation, compulsion, control, survival material, power exchange, and deep psychological pressure.

houseMeanings.1: The relationship becomes highly visible and identity-forming. Watch for losing individual identity inside the bond.
houseMeanings.2: Shared values, money, assets, self-worth, and material security become central. Misaligned values can become stubborn conflict.
houseMeanings.3: Communication, mental rapport, daily exchange, siblings, neighbors, and movement become central. Emotional depth may need conscious effort.
houseMeanings.4: Home, family, roots, privacy, memory, and emotional foundation become central. Comfort helps, but staleness or subjectivity can creep in.
houseMeanings.5: Romance, fun, creativity, children, play, pleasure, and self-expression become central. Durability needs support from Saturn or committed houses.
houseMeanings.6: Daily work, service, health, maintenance, labor, and unequal effort become central. Resentment grows if one person carries too much.
houseMeanings.7: Partnership, equality, fairness, commitment, negotiation, and mutual recognition become central. This can support romantic or professional partnership.
houseMeanings.8: Intimacy, shared resources, debt, trust, transformation, crisis, and power dynamics become central. Watch control, domination, and emotional extremes.
houseMeanings.9: Beliefs, travel, learning, teaching, publishing, exploration, and shared worldview become central. The bond needs enough room to breathe.
houseMeanings.10: Career, reputation, visibility, status, goals, and public contribution become central. Emotional openness may need extra attention.
houseMeanings.11: Friendship, community, networks, shared dreams, groups, and future-building become central. A friendship base strengthens the bond.
houseMeanings.12: Hidden material, secrecy, sacrifice, subconscious patterns, retreat, and karmic-feeling unfinished business become central. Reality-checking is essential.

aspectPrinciples.conjunction: Fuses the two functions and makes that theme loud in the relationship. It can create unity or enmeshment depending on the planets involved.
aspectPrinciples.sextile: Offers cooperation and opportunity. It helps, but the relationship still has to use the opening.
aspectPrinciples.trine: Creates ease and flow. It can soften conflict, but may also become passive if the relationship avoids needed work.
aspectPrinciples.square: Creates friction, pressure, and repeated activation. It demands skill, repair, and honesty rather than avoidance.
aspectPrinciples.opposition: Creates polarity and projection. The relationship must learn to hold both ends instead of making one person carry the uncomfortable side.

aspectCautions.sunMercury: Composite Sun and Mercury are usually conjunction-only for major-aspect use because they stay close by astronomical relationship.
aspectCautions.sunVenus: Composite Sun and Venus are usually conjunction-only for major-aspect use because they stay close by astronomical relationship.
aspectCautions.hardSunMoon: Core purpose and emotional needs can pull against each other; the relationship needs balance between want and need.
aspectCautions.hardSunMars: High drive can become argument or combativeness without constructive outlets.
aspectCautions.hardSunSaturn: The bond can feel heavy, limiting, dutiful, or afraid to move. Durability is not automatically health.
aspectCautions.hardSunUranus: Instability and constant change can make the bond hard to ground.
aspectCautions.hardSunNeptune: Idealization, secrecy, rescue patterns, or unclear reality can distort the relationship.
aspectCautions.hardSunPluto: Power struggles, obsession, manipulation, or consuming intensity can dominate unless transformed consciously.
aspectCautions.hardMoonSaturn: Emotional safety may feel restricted by duty, fear, or withholding.
aspectCautions.hardMoonNeptune: Emotional fog, projection, or fantasy can make it difficult to tell what is actually happening.
aspectCautions.hardVenusSaturn: Affection can feel withheld, delayed, conditional, or burdened by responsibility.
aspectCautions.hardVenusUranus: Attraction can be exciting but inconsistent, with freedom needs disrupting closeness.
aspectCautions.hardVenusNeptune: Romance can slide into illusion, deception, or saving fantasies if not grounded.
aspectCautions.hardMarsSaturn: One part of the relationship pushes while another blocks, creating frustration unless effort is structured.
aspectCautions.hardMarsNeptune: Action can scatter, anger can go indirect, and desire can blur without clear agreements.
aspectCautions.hardPlutoPersonal: Contacts from Pluto to Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, or Mars intensify the bond but require strong boundaries around control and compulsion.

classes.ascendantUse: Composite Ascendant describes how the relationship appears and reacts as a pair. Read the sign for style, the ruler for direction, and aspects to the Ascendant for how easily the relationship can inhabit that style.
classes.ethicalBoundary: Composite charts should never be used to justify staying in harmful dynamics. Intensity, karma language, or endurance indicators do not equal health.

sun.1: Composite Sun in the 1st: the relationship is its own strong, visible, self-defined entity. Gift: a clear, confident identity as a couple. Watch: so focused on itself it turns insular.
sun.2: Composite Sun in the 2nd: centers on building security, resources, and shared values. Gift: it makes something tangible and stable. Watch: money and possessions standing in for emotional connection.
sun.3: Composite Sun in the 3rd: lives through communication, learning, and daily exchange. Gift: you genuinely talk and think together. Watch: staying mental and busy, light on depth.
sun.4: Composite Sun in the 4th: about home, family, and a private emotional base. Gift: deep roots and belonging. Watch: turning so inward it withdraws from the world.
sun.5: Composite Sun in the 5th: about romance, creativity, play, and joy. Gift: it stays fun, expressive, and alive. Watch: trouble shifting from playmate to life-partner mode.
sun.6: Composite Sun in the 6th: runs on shared work, routine, health, and being useful to each other. Gift: a functional, supportive daily life. Watch: it becomes a to-do list and loses romance.
sun.7: Composite Sun in the 7th: centrally about partnership - being a committed couple is the point. Gift: a strong sense of 'we'. Watch: losing individual identity inside the union.
sun.8: Composite Sun in the 8th: about intimacy, depth, shared resources, and transformation. Gift: it changes you both at the core. Watch: power struggles and intensity that overwhelms.
sun.9: Composite Sun in the 9th: about growth, adventure, study, and expanding horizons. Gift: you make each other bigger. Watch: drifting if the shared adventure stalls.
sun.10: Composite Sun in the 10th: a public-facing relationship - visible, ambitious, seen as a couple. Gift: shared purpose and standing. Watch: image and achievement crowding out private warmth.
sun.11: Composite Sun in the 11th: friendship-based, social, and future-facing. Gift: genuine companionship and shared goals. Watch: feeling more like friends than lovers.
sun.12: Composite Sun in the 12th: a private, hidden, or spiritual core - much of it lives behind closed doors. Gift: a soulful, intimate undertone. Watch: secrecy, escapism, or a bond that hides from daylight.

moon.1: Composite Moon in the 1st: the relationship wears its feelings openly - emotion shapes its whole identity. Gift: warmth and emotional honesty. Watch: moods running the relationship.
moon.2: Composite Moon in the 2nd: emotional security comes through stability, money, and comfort. Gift: a grounded, safe feeling. Watch: leaning on material security to feel loved.
moon.3: Composite Moon in the 3rd: feels close through talking and daily contact. Gift: emotional communication. Watch: needing constant contact to feel secure.
moon.4: Composite Moon in the 4th: the emotional heart is home and family - its most natural placement. Gift: deep belonging and nurturing. Watch: over-attachment and withdrawing into the nest.
moon.5: Composite Moon in the 5th: emotions flow through romance, play, and creativity. Gift: affectionate, fun, expressive. Watch: emotional drama and needing constant romance.
moon.6: Composite Moon in the 6th: you feel close through caretaking and daily routines. Gift: nurturing through small acts. Watch: worry, fussing, and love that turns into chores.
moon.7: Composite Moon in the 7th: emotional security comes from the partnership itself. Gift: feeling met and paired. Watch: emotional dependency on the relationship for stability.
moon.8: Composite Moon in the 8th: emotions run deep, intimate, and intense. Gift: deep, almost bottomless emotional bonding. Watch: jealousy, possessiveness, and emotional power plays.
moon.9: Composite Moon in the 9th: feels good when it's growing, exploring, or learning together. Gift: optimism and shared adventure. Watch: restlessness and needing constant novelty.
moon.10: Composite Moon in the 10th: emotions are tied to the relationship's public life and direction. Gift: a shared sense of purpose. Watch: feelings managed for appearances; private warmth neglected.
moon.11: Composite Moon in the 11th: emotional closeness comes through friendship and shared hopes. Gift: easy companionship. Watch: feeling like friends more than intimate partners.
moon.12: Composite Moon in the 12th: the emotional life is private, deep, and partly unconscious. Gift: a soulful, intuitive bond. Watch: hidden feelings, secrets, and emotional escapism.

mercury.1: Communication defines you; you talk constantly, and people know you for the rapport. Keep it open.
mercury.2: You talk about money and values, and those practical conversations bond you. Plan the resources together.
mercury.3: Heavy on talk, ideas, daily back-and-forth - you think alike here. Keep the dialogue lively.
mercury.4: You communicate about home and roots; the private conversations matter most. Keep them honest.
mercury.5: Playful, creative communication; you joke and make things together. Keep it light and expressive.
mercury.6: You talk about work and routines - practical, useful exchange. Don't let the talk slide into nagging.
mercury.7: Communication centers on the partnership; you negotiate and discuss your way through. Keep it fair and clear.
mercury.8: Deep, probing conversations; you discuss the hidden stuff honestly. It's intense. Don't tip into interrogation.
mercury.9: You talk about beliefs and big ideas; learning bonds you. Keep exploring together.
mercury.10: You communicate about goals and status; the professional talk matters here. Stay aligned on the ambition.
mercury.11: You talk as friends and allies; shared ideas hold the wider circle together. Keep planning.
mercury.12: Private, often unspoken communication; you sense each other. Watch for what's left unsaid. Voice it.

venus.1: Composite Venus in the 1st: the relationship radiates warmth and attraction - it looks and feels loving. Gift: charm and easy affection. Watch: prioritizing how it looks over how it works.
venus.2: Composite Venus in the 2nd: love is expressed through comfort, gifts, security, and shared pleasures. Gift: a stable, sensual bond. Watch: love measured in money and things.
venus.3: Composite Venus in the 3rd: affection flows through words, wit, and everyday sweetness. Gift: loving communication. Watch: charm that stays light and avoids deeper feeling.
venus.4: Composite Venus in the 4th: love centers on home - a warm, beautiful, comforting private life. Gift: domestic harmony. Watch: coziness that avoids the hard conversations.
venus.5: Composite Venus in the 5th: love is romantic, playful, and creative - one of the warmest placements. Gift: lasting romance and fun. Watch: needing the honeymoon feeling to last forever.
venus.6: Composite Venus in the 6th: affection shows up through care, service, and daily kindness. Gift: love in the small acts. Watch: love reduced to usefulness.
venus.7: Composite Venus in the 7th: love and partnership beautifully aligned - a natural couple. Gift: harmony and genuine partnership. Watch: avoiding conflict to preserve the harmony.
venus.8: Composite Venus in the 8th: love is deep and intense - bonded through vulnerability, sometimes money or sex. Gift: deep, intimate closeness. Watch: possessiveness and jealousy.
venus.9: Composite Venus in the 9th: love grows through adventure, learning, and shared beliefs. Gift: an expansive, exciting bond. Watch: love cooling when the adventure pauses.
venus.10: Composite Venus in the 10th: affection is visible and often tied to status or public life. Gift: a couple others admire. Watch: image standing in for intimacy.
venus.11: Composite Venus in the 11th: love is friendly, easygoing, and socially connected. Gift: genuine liking and companionship. Watch: more friendship than passion.
venus.12: Composite Venus in the 12th: love is tender, private, and easy to idealize - sometimes secret. Gift: a soulful, compassionate bond. Watch: loving the fantasy, or hiding the love.

mars.1: Composite Mars in the 1st: the relationship is energetic, assertive, and forceful - it acts boldly. Gift: drive and presence. Watch: aggression and conflict spilling into its identity.
mars.2: Composite Mars in the 2nd: energy goes into building security and earning. Gift: you work hard for what you want. Watch: fights about money and possessions.
mars.3: Composite Mars in the 3rd: the drive shows up in communication - lively, direct, sometimes combative. Gift: passionate exchange. Watch: arguments and sharp words.
mars.4: Composite Mars in the 4th: energy and friction center on home and family. Gift: you build and defend your domestic life fiercely. Watch: tension and conflict in the private space.
mars.5: Composite Mars in the 5th: drive goes into romance, sex, and creative play. Gift: strong physical chemistry and fun. Watch: competitiveness and drama in the romance.
mars.6: Composite Mars in the 6th: energy goes into work, routines, and getting things done. Gift: a productive, capable team. Watch: bickering over chores and daily friction.
mars.7: Composite Mars in the 7th: the drive is aimed at the partnership - passionate, and prone to open conflict. Gift: you fight for the relationship. Watch: the relationship as a battleground.
mars.8: Composite Mars in the 8th: powerful sexual and emotional intensity - deep drive, deep heat. Gift: passion and transformative energy. Watch: power struggles and jealousy.
mars.9: Composite Mars in the 9th: energy goes into adventure, growth, and shared causes. Gift: you pursue big things together. Watch: clashing beliefs and restless conflict.
mars.10: Composite Mars in the 10th: drive aimed at ambition, status, and public goals. Gift: a couple that achieves. Watch: competition between you, or fighting in public view.
mars.11: Composite Mars in the 11th: energy goes into shared goals, friends, and causes. Gift: you mobilize toward the future together. Watch: friction within the wider social circle.
mars.12: Composite Mars in the 12th: the drive runs hidden - passion and anger both work below the surface. Gift: quiet, private intensity. Watch: passive conflict and buried resentment.

jupiter.1: Optimism and confidence are visible; you expand each other, and the couple feels lucky. Don't overpromise.
jupiter.2: Growth ties to money and resources; you prosper together. Watch the overspending.
jupiter.3: Ideas and learning expand; you grow through talking. Keep exploring - and don't exaggerate.
jupiter.4: Home and family expand; you build abundance at the base. Don't overextend the household.
jupiter.5: Fun, romance, creativity flourish; you enjoy life together, generously. Don't overdo it.
jupiter.6: Work and routine improve; you grow through service. Watch the urge to take on too much.
jupiter.7: The partnership itself expands; it's generous and warm, a lucky relationship. Keep it real.
jupiter.8: Shared resources and intimacy grow; you transform abundantly. Watch the excess and the risk.
jupiter.9: Beliefs, travel, and growth flourish; you expand each other's world. It's a strong, adventurous bond.
jupiter.10: Public success and reputation grow; you achieve together. Keep the ambition grounded.
jupiter.11: Friendships and hopes expand; you grow through community. It's a generous social bond.
