northNode.plainMeaning: Growth direction, unfamiliar medicine, and the qualities the user is learning to embody.
useWhen: natal North Node sign or house
transiting planet conjunct natal North Node
transiting North Node conjunct a natal planet or angle
synastry contacts to the North Node
northNode.userLanguage: This is not automatically comfortable, but it points toward the version of you that is becoming more alive.

southNode.plainMeaning: Familiar pattern, default instinct, old competence, inherited habit, or a place where the user can over-rely on what already works.
useWhen: natal South Node sign or house
transiting planet conjunct natal South Node
transiting South Node conjunct a natal planet or angle
synastry contacts to the South Node
southNode.userLanguage: This can feel easy because it is known. Known is not the same as good for you forever.

nodalReturn.plainMeaning: A developmental checkpoint when the transiting nodes return to the natal nodal axis.
examples: A relationship, path, study, relocation, job, or identity pattern returns with new meaning.
The user may notice the same theme from the previous nodal cycle, but with more choice available.
Important people can enter or leave as the old pattern and new direction become visible.
nodalReturn.readingRule: Read the natal node sign/house first, then check which planets or angles are contacted by the return chart, eclipses, and current transits.

nodalReversal.cycle: about 9.3 years after each nodal return
nodalReversal.plainMeaning: A midpoint check when transiting North Node contacts natal South Node and transiting South Node contacts natal North Node.
examples: The user may be pulled strongly toward a familiar pattern so they can see whether it still serves them.
A person or opportunity can feel compelling because it activates both comfort and growth tension.
The cycle can ask for integration rather than a simple move forward.
nodalReversal.readingRule: Watch for reversals in relationship, work, home, belief, or identity patterns connected to the natal nodal houses.

eclipseSeason.cycle: twice yearly eclipse seasons near the nodal axis
eclipseSeason.plainMeaning: A period when the Sun, Moon, and nodes align, intensifying the house/sign axis being activated.
examples: A choice, release, beginning, ending, or revelation clusters around the eclipse house axis.
Events can feel larger than ordinary lunations when the eclipse tightly contacts natal planets or angles.
The effect is strongest when the eclipse repeats an already active transit, progression, return, or profection theme.
eclipseSeason.readingRule: Name the axis, exact natal contacts, and whether the eclipse leans North Node growth or South Node release. Do not recommend elaborate ritual work during eclipses.

ascendantDescendant.northNodeOnAscendant: A visibility and self-direction threshold. The user may feel more ready to initiate, be seen, or move independently, while partnership demands still require balance.
ascendantDescendant.northNodeOnDescendant: A relationship and client threshold. Important helpers, partners, agreements, or dependencies can become central, and the user may need to stop doing everything alone.
examples: choice between self-direction and partnership responsibility

mcIc.northNodeOnMc: A public-role threshold. Career growth, recognition, promotion, or a visible responsibility can increase while home/family needs ask for conscious care.
mcIc.northNodeOnIc: A home and roots threshold. Relocation, family support, private life, or emotional foundations can become more important while career assumptions are reviewed.

sun.northNode: Identity, confidence, leadership, and direction get a forward pull. Beneficial people or opportunities may appear when other indicators agree.
sun.southNode: A familiar identity pattern or old role may be ready for release, especially if it has limited vitality.

moon.northNode: Emotional growth, family support, public response, or caretaking themes become more active.
moon.southNode: Old family patterns, emotional defaults, or care dynamics may need release or more conscious handling.
examples: support from a woman or caretaker

mercury.northNode: Messages, study, travel logistics, paperwork, youth topics, or negotiations can open movement.
mercury.southNode: Old communication loops, unclear agreements, or logistical mistakes may need correction.

venus.northNode: Relationships, money, pleasure, beauty, children, celebration, or social support can become joining points.
venus.southNode: Old attachment patterns, overspending, comfort-seeking, or relational nostalgia may need clarity.

mars.northNode: Action, courage, enterprise, and direct initiative can move quickly when aimed well.
mars.southNode: Haste, conflict, careless risk, mechanical trouble, or reactive anger may need restraint.

jupiter.northNode: Growth through teachers, law, travel, publishing, finances, education, or honorable support can expand.
jupiter.southNode: Overconfidence, excess, risky speculation, or a belief pattern may need correction.

saturn.northNode: Durable commitments, professional progress, accountability, and long-term structures can form.
saturn.southNode: Delay, authority pressure, duty, coldness, or a familiar fear pattern may need mature handling.

uranus.northNode: Sudden openings, liberation, unusual meetings, innovation, or reputation shifts can move the user forward.
uranus.southNode: Disruption, rebellion, scandal risk, or unstable choices can repeat an old pattern if not handled consciously.

neptune.northNode: Compassion, creativity, spirituality, and surrender can open when boundaries are also present.
neptune.southNode: Confusion, deception, avoidance, leakage, theft, or substance-related themes need grounded care.

pluto.northNode: Deep psychological work, power reclamation, and restructuring can become unavoidable and transformative.
pluto.southNode: Control, crisis bonding, compulsion, or power struggle can pull the user back into familiar intensity.

synastry.northNodeContacts: A partner's planet on the user's North Node can feel activating, growth-oriented, and sometimes uncomfortable. It should be described as developmental pressure, not proof the relationship must last.
synastry.southNodeContacts: A partner's planet on the user's South Node can feel immediate and familiar. It can show recognition and ease, but also regression or a pull back into known patterns.
synastry.saturnNodeContacts: Saturn-node contacts can feel weighty, serious, binding, or consequential. Use safety-first language and do not frame heaviness as obligation.
synastry.policy: Nodal synastry shows dynamics and developmental pressure, not certainty.

displayPolicy.chartDisplay: Show lunar nodes in the main chart by default as calculated points, visually separate from planets.
displayPolicy.interpretationWeight: Do not let nodes outrank Sun, Moon, Ascendant, chart ruler, or repeated house/ruler themes unless the nodes are angular, tightly aspected, eclipsed, or repeated across techniques.
displayPolicy.unknownBirthTime: Node sign can usually be shown without birth time, but house and angle contacts require accurate birth time.

Nodal return and reversal are life-cycle context, not standalone event guarantees.

modifiers.summary: Nodal Return and Nodal Reversal are developmental checkpoints in the lunar node cycle, asking whether the person is moving toward growth or repeating the familiar pattern.
modifiers.body: Use Nodal Return and Nodal Reversal as node-axis timing context. The return reactivates the natal North/South Node storyline; the reversal brings the transiting North Node to the natal South Node and can make familiar patterns especially compelling. Read the natal node sign and house axis first, then check eclipses, progressions, return charts, and close planet or angle contacts.
modifiers.definition: The lunar nodes regress through the zodiac and return to the natal nodal axis about every 18.6 years. The reversal occurs around the halfway point of that cycle.
appUsage: Use exact node position for timing; ages are approximate.
Read North Node and South Node together as one axis.
Weight up if an eclipse, angle, Sun, Moon, chart ruler, Venus, Mars, or Saturn is involved.
Do not describe nodal cycles as fixed outcomes.

cycleFacts.regression: The lunar nodes move backward through the zodiac at about 1.5 deg/year.
cycleFacts.returnPeriod: The North Node returns to its natal place every ~18.6 years, so returns land near ages 18-19, 37, 56, and 74-75.
cycleFacts.metonic: A related 19-year eclipse return (Metonic) repeats an eclipse on nearly the same day and degree.

milestones.plainTranslation: The axis of your life direction re-activates: North Node (where you're growing toward) against South Node (where you've come from). A checkpoint on direction, often landing alongside the launch or redirection of a whole life chapter.
milestones.guidance: Reassess whether you're moving toward growth or sliding back into the familiar.

milestones.plainTranslation: Nodal reversal: the transiting nodes sit opposite your natal axis (the transiting North Node on your natal South Node). The familiar past pulls hard. A halfway course-check.
milestones.guidance: Notice the pull backward and choose your direction consciously.

relationshipToEclipses.metonicCycle: A related 19-year eclipse return (Metonic) repeats an eclipse on nearly the same day and degree.
relationshipToEclipses.rule: Eclipse contacts are strongest when they fall near the natal nodal axis, angles, Sun, Moon, chart ruler, Venus, Mars, or Saturn and repeat another active timing theme.

prohibitions: Do not call nodal return a guaranteed turning point without supporting testimony.

Repeated node contacts across synastry, progressions, returns, and transits increase relevance.
Nodes describe developmental pressure and timing, not fixed outcome.

modifiers.body: Use these examples as interpretive labels when natal promise, progressions, returns, activated house rulers, and transits repeat the same theme. A single transit can describe pressure, mood, or opportunity; it should not be promoted into a concrete event unless other timing layers agree.
modifiers.definition: A predictive example pattern is a cluster of repeated indicators that points toward a life area becoming active enough to describe in plain language, such as relationship definition, career consequence, home movement, health maintenance, legal process, travel logistics, financial restructuring, or public visibility.
appUsage: Surface these examples as possibilities, not verdicts.
Require repeated testimony before naming a concrete event category.
Prefer plain language: relationship definition, career pressure, home change, health maintenance, financial responsibility, legal paperwork, travel logistics, public visibility.
When the topic is sensitive, name the life area and recommend practical support rather than dramatizing the symbol.
Use planet examples to clarify the flavor of the event, and house examples to clarify the life area.
modifiers.note: Distilled from approved predictive, transit, spiritual astrology, and Saturn cycle reference material. Source files were not copied into the repository.

timingPrinciples.innerAndOuter: Slow planets describe the larger life phase. Faster planets can time the moment when the larger phase becomes visible through a conversation, decision, message, appointment, meeting, conflict, or public announcement.
timingPrinciples.threePassTransit: When a slow planet makes three contacts, read the first pass as the issue appearing, the retrograde pass as review or complication, and the final pass as decision, integration, or consequence.
timingPrinciples.storedActivation: A station, close outer-planet contact, return chart angle, or progressed contact can store pressure. A later fast trigger may coincide with the visible event.
timingPrinciples.eventDefinition: An event can be external, internal, relational, bodily, legal, financial, or psychological. The app should not assume that a transit must produce an obvious outer incident.
timingPrinciples.multipleIndicators: For a major event label, look for the same planet pair, house topic, ruler, angle, or return-chart emphasis repeating at least three times.

sun.plainFocus: Visibility, identity, vitality, leaders, authority figures, recognition, central decisions, and personal direction.
examples: A public role, title, or reputation question comes into focus.
A leader, parent, manager, or authority figure becomes part of the story.
A decision about direction, confidence, or personal visibility can no longer stay vague.

moon.plainFocus: Home, family, emotional safety, body rhythms, care, movement, memory, and the immediate lived environment.
examples: A home, family, caregiving, or domestic matter needs attention.
The body or emotional system responds before the mind has a full explanation.
A short-term timing trigger brings a larger pattern into the day-to-day.

mercury.plainFocus: Messages, paperwork, travel logistics, siblings, study, schedules, devices, agreements, and news.
examples: A document, text, call, email, application, contract, or announcement becomes the trigger point.
Travel, commuting, school, scheduling, or device issues need practical handling.
The event becomes known through a message, meeting, report, or conversation.

venus.plainFocus: Relationships, money, ease, pleasure, value, aesthetics, gifts, social repair, and attraction.
examples: A relationship softens, defines itself, asks for repair, or reveals the true state of affection.
A financial offer, purchase, gift, payment, pricing issue, or spending pattern becomes visible.
A choice about comfort, beauty, desire, or worth carries more weight than usual.

mars.plainFocus: Action, urgency, conflict, heat, inflammation, effort, competition, enterprise, tools, and accidents caused by haste.
examples: A dispute, deadline, confrontation, repair, athletic push, or risky action forces movement.
The body needs caution around speed, inflammation, sharp tools, machinery, driving, or overexertion.
A business launch, bold ask, or competitive effort can move quickly if the aim is clean.

jupiter.plainFocus: Growth, protection, opportunity, teachers, law, publishing, travel, education, faith, and social support.
examples: A legal, academic, publishing, travel, teaching, or certification matter expands.
Support can come through mentors, allies, institutions, or a door opening at the right time.
A joyful life event can become more likely when relationship, family, or 5th-house testimony agrees.

saturn.plainFocus: Time, limits, duty, authority, work, age, health maintenance, delay, structure, accountability, and consequence.
examples: A job, commitment, debt, family duty, legal responsibility, or long-term obligation has to be handled seriously.
The body may ask for maintenance, pacing, treatment, rest, or a more realistic workload.
An authority figure, institution, boss, parent, mentor, or inner critic becomes part of the test.

uranus.plainFocus: Disruption, freedom, shock, innovation, breaks in routine, technology, nervous-system charge, and sudden reversals.
examples: A sudden change, cancellation, breakthrough, relocation impulse, technical disruption, or independence issue changes the plan.
The user may need more freedom or flexibility than the current structure allows.
If accident signatures repeat elsewhere, haste and electrical or mechanical risks deserve extra caution.

neptune.plainFocus: Confusion, surrender, uncertainty, porous boundaries, spirituality, art, secrecy, fog, fatigue, and quiet erosion.
examples: A situation becomes unclear, idealized, hidden, delayed, or hard to define.
Work, health, relationship, or money boundaries may blur unless the user asks direct questions.
Creative, spiritual, and compassionate openings are stronger when practical safeguards are present.

pluto.plainFocus: Power, pressure, control, exposure, obsession, survival patterns, buried material, and deep restructuring.
examples: A control dynamic, power struggle, financial entanglement, intense attachment, or hidden issue surfaces.
A role, relationship, habit, or system may need deep restructuring rather than cosmetic adjustment.
When practical indicators agree, the event can involve institutions, shared resources, therapy, investigation, or crisis management.

firstReturn: Changing jobs because the old path was built around other people's expectations.
Defining a relationship instead of letting ambiguity carry the weight.

prohibitions: Do not predict a specific event from one transit.
Do not use these examples to diagnose health conditions.
Do not present legal, pregnancy, custody, safety, financial, or relationship outcomes as guaranteed.
Do not use fear-based language to force urgency.
Do not expose source names or book titles in user-facing text.
weighting: Use examples only when repeated testimony supports them.
Angular contacts and activated rulers carry more weight than background aspects.
Progressions describe the life chapter; transits describe timing pressure.
Return charts describe the field for the year, month, or planetary cycle.
Fast planets can time the day, message, meeting, or decision only when a larger pattern is already active.
The same planet pair repeating across natal, progressed, return, and transit layers should be weighted up.

modifiers.summary: The progressed lunation cycle describes a roughly 29-30 year life-phase rhythm formed by the progressed Moon and progressed Sun.
modifiers.body: Use this as a slow life-cycle layer, not a daily transit. The phase describes where the person is in a long arc of endings, beginnings, risk, visibility, sharing, revision, and release.
modifiers.definition: A progressed lunation phase is measured by the angular separation between the progressed Moon and progressed Sun, mapped as an eight-phase cycle across the chart angles.
appUsage: Use as a life-phase feature with multi-year timing, not a daily notification trigger.
Calculate the phase from progressed Moon to progressed Sun separation; do not infer it from age alone.
Anchor interpretive framing to the IC, Descendant, MC, and Ascendant wave described in the framework.
Pair with Saturn Return when timing overlaps: progressed lunation describes what is ripening emotionally, while Saturn Return asks what structure can hold it.
Keep language non-fatalistic. A phase describes developmental weather, not a guaranteed event.
modifiers.note: Voiced from project-authored progressed lunation notes. Source file was not copied into the repository.

framework.anchor: The cycle is anchored to the IC, not 0 Aries. The eight phases map onto the chart's four angles as a wave: New Moon at the IC (bottom), First Quarter at the Descendant, Full Moon at the MC (top), Last Quarter at the Ascendant.
framework.houseProgression: New Moon = 4th, Crescent = 5th-6th, First Quarter = 7th-8th, Gibbous = 9th, Full Moon = 10th, Disseminating = 11th-12th, Last Quarter = 1st-3rd, Balsamic = end of the 3rd into a new cycle.

cycleFacts.rate: Progressed Moon moves about 13 degrees/year, progressed Sun about 1 degree/year; the Sun-Moon separation opens and closes over the full cycle.
cycleFacts.timing: Where you start depends on your natal lunar phase. Born near a New Moon, you hit your progressed New Moon in your mid-to-late twenties. Born near the Balsamic phase, you hit it early in life.
cycleFacts.note: This slow rhythm frames even long outer-planet transits. The progressed New Moon can land like an ending-and-renewal, close in feel to a heavy Pluto transit.

classes.relatedCycles: Pairs with saturn_return.json: the progressed lunar return (what makes you happy) often precedes the Saturn return's call to build on it.

phases.name: Progressed New Moon
phases.plainTranslation: Beginning and ending in the same breath. Something is over - a chapter, a job, an identity - and it can hurt. A seed goes in, but it is underground. You cannot see the new direction yet. The pull is home, roots, the quiet core.
phases.guidance: Do not force a direction. Let it stay murky. Go home, regroup, let the new self form before you name it.

phases.name: Progressed Crescent
phases.plainTranslation: Time to move, even blind. The dream needs first steps. Everything is new and the learning curve is steep - new job, new role, new person, all unfamiliar.
phases.guidance: Start anyway. Take the risk, then do the boring work. Take help. Stop overthinking it.

phases.name: Progressed First Quarter
phases.plainTranslation: A clean break. Independence, sometimes forced, usually through a test. Now you face other people - partners, rivals, the crowd. Weddings and divorces both cluster here.
phases.guidance: Take the risk. Pull in your allies. Face the judgment instead of dodging it.

phases.name: Progressed Gibbous
phases.plainTranslation: Everything grows - ambition, stakes, feelings, problems. Your horizons widen. You reach higher, climbing toward a peak. The trap is overdoing it: overwork, overspend, burn out.
phases.guidance: Invest hard, watch the excess. You are building toward delivery, not there yet.

phases.name: Progressed Full Moon
phases.plainTranslation: The peak. Climax or anti-climax - a win or a letdown, and both go public. Maximum visibility, maximum clarity. Separation runs strong: distance from home, the urge to shed the old.
phases.guidance: See it clearly. Take the result, spend the energy, set new targets once it settles.

phases.name: Progressed Disseminating
phases.plainTranslation: The turn toward home. Share what you got - teach it, give it back, fold it into the group. You find your people and your niche. Or you sit with a loss and work through it.
phases.guidance: Spread the harvest. Build the network. Carry the lesson into ordinary life. Do not slide into hiding.

phases.name: Progressed Last Quarter
phases.plainTranslation: A wake-up call. Back from the crowd to yourself. Hard questions: who am I, what do I want, what is still undone. The fear points forward - that you left it too late.
phases.guidance: Cut the distractions. Focus. Do the undone thing while there's time.

phases.name: Progressed Balsamic
phases.plainTranslation: The world gets quieter and more concentrated. Supports fall away, dreams get shelved, energy dips. It is the release, the closing, the last word. It can also be a late harvest - the reward you waited years for, landing now.
phases.guidance: Let go of what is holding you back. Say the unsaid. Find closure. Protect the small new seed. Rest, and get support if you are running on empty.

prohibitions: Do not use progressed lunation phase as a deterministic prediction of events.
Do not describe the Balsamic phase as failure, disappearance, or doom.
Do not use age alone when calculated progressions are available.
Do not collapse progressed lunation into ordinary New Moon or Full Moon ritual content.
weighting: Exact progressed Sun-Moon separation determines the phase.
Phase changes are multi-year thresholds and deserve stronger weight near phase boundaries.
Angular phases are louder: New Moon near IC, First Quarter near Descendant, Full Moon near MC, Last Quarter near Ascendant.
Natal lunar phase changes when a person reaches each progressed phase; personalize timing from the natal chart.

orbs.phaseRanges: Use the eight 45-degree phase bands supplied in classes.phases.degreeRange.
orbs.thresholdWindow: Give extra interpretive weight when the progressed Sun-Moon separation is within about 2 degrees of a phase boundary.

modifiers.definition: A planet receives another when the second sits in a sign or degree the first rules by dignity. Mutual reception is when each occupies the other's dignity; the two then cooperate and can act almost as if joined.
appUsage: If two planets in a HARD aspect are in mutual reception, weight the difficulty DOWN: they find a way to work together despite the angle.
Reception strengthens a soft aspect and rescues a hard one; absence of reception leaves a hard aspect at full force.
Reception by major dignity (domicile, exaltation) is strong; by minor dignity (triplicity, bounds, decan) is weaker.
modifiers.note: Use the dignity tables to detect reception: planet A in a sign ruled by B, and B in a sign ruled by A.
modifiers.summary: Reception describes whether planets can cooperate through dignity, especially across difficult aspects.
modifiers.body: A planet receives another when the second sits in a sign or degree the first rules by dignity. Mutual reception is when each occupies the other's dignity; the two then cooperate and can act almost as if joined.

modifiers.summary: Planet-specific retrograde metadata and plain-language meanings for planets that station retrograde.
modifiers.body: Retrograde interpretation should stay planet-specific and should distinguish a natal retrograde signature from a temporary transit retrograde period.
modifiers.definition: A retrograde is apparent backward motion from the observer perspective, used symbolically as review, return, delay, reversal, or internalization depending on planet and context.
appUsage: Do not mark the Sun or Moon retrograde.
Use planet-specific meanings instead of one generic retrograde paragraph.
For daily transit UI, show pre-shadow and post-shadow only when the app has reliable date data.
modifiers.note: Imported from the project policy bundle; source file was not copied into the repo.

modifiers.definition: A planet that appears to move backward through the zodiac. Its themes turn inward, repeat, and revisit rather than advance.
modifiers.appUsage: When a transiting planet is retrograde, frame its lane as review/revisit/delay rather than new initiation. When stationing, treat its theme as intensified and unavoidable for those days.

retrograde.effect: Internalized, delayed, or reconsidered expression of the planet. Good for redoing, auditing, and returning; poor for launching.

station.effect: Near the turn between retrograde and direct, the planet is nearly motionless and its significations are concentrated and emphasized.

modifiers.summary: Retrograde motion turns a planet back through revision, delay, return, and reworking.
modifiers.body: A planet that appears to move backward through the zodiac. Its themes turn inward, repeat, and revisit rather than advance.

modifiers.summary: Traditional rulership remains primary; modern co-rulership is treated as an explicit secondary lens.
modifiers.body: When naming a chart ruler or sign ruler, use the traditional ruler. Modern planets may inform interpretation only when clearly framed as a modern lens.
modifiers.definition: A normalized table of traditional rulership and modern co-rulership relationships.
appUsage: Use Mars for Scorpio, Saturn for Aquarius, and Jupiter for Pisces in ruler text.
Surface Pluto, Uranus, and Neptune only inside an explicitly labeled modern lens.
Do not let modern co-rulers alter dignity, sect, or time-lord logic.
