modifiers.summary: Saturn Return marks the renewal of the natal Saturn cycle, asking the person to upgrade their relationship with maturity, responsibility, structure, limits, authority, and long-term work.
modifiers.body: A Saturn Return occurs when transiting Saturn returns to the natal degree of Saturn. It is not automatically punishment or a fixed outcome. It is a life-cycle threshold where earlier models of responsibility, authority, discipline, fear, work, and commitment are tested against the life the person is actually building.
modifiers.definition: A Saturn Return is the conjunction of transiting Saturn to natal Saturn, beginning a new approximately 29.5-year Saturn cycle.
appUsage: Use Saturn Return as a life-cycle feature, not as a daily transit blip.
Compute exact timing from transiting Saturn to natal Saturn. Do not rely on age alone.
Use age bands only as rough guidance: first return around 29-30, second around 58-60, third around 87-89.
Weight the natal Saturn sign, house, dignity, sect, retrograde condition, and natal aspects to Saturn as the core interpretive structure.
If Saturn stations within about 1-2 degrees of natal Saturn, treat the return period as louder and longer.
Do not frame Saturn Return as guaranteed crisis. Frame it as a maturity checkpoint where avoided structures become harder to ignore.
modifiers.note: Synthesized from approved project Saturn Return reference PDFs. Source files were not copied into the repository.

coreMeaning.saturnFunction: Saturn describes maturity, structure, discipline, limits, authority, responsibility, work, time, consequence, and the ability to build something durable.
coreMeaning.returnFunction: A return brings the planet's natal imprint back to full activation. For Saturn, the question is how the person has been using or avoiding Saturn's themes, and what must mature now.
coreMeaning.upgradeFrame: The return asks the person to stop living only from inherited models of authority and responsibility and to build a Saturn pattern that belongs to their own life.

waxingSquareOne.meaning: Early encounter with limits, rules, effort, authority, and consequences.

firstOpposition.meaning: Limits and authority become visible through confrontation. The person begins to see where external rules and inner resistance meet.

waningSquareOne.meaning: Pressure to test inherited expectations against adult choices. Early responsibility patterns begin to strain.

firstReturn.meaning: The first full audit of maturity, work, authority, commitment, and life structure.

waxingSquareTwo.meaning: Friction around how the post-return structure is actually working.

secondOpposition.meaning: Mid-cycle visibility. Weak spots in discipline, commitment, authority, and long-term direction become harder to deny.

waningSquareTwo.meaning: A later pressure point that asks what needs to be revised before the second return.

secondReturn.meaning: A threshold of elderhood, legacy, usefulness, wisdom, age, bodily reality, and what the person is ready to contribute next.

thirdReturn.meaning: A late-life threshold around completion, wisdom, embodiment of experience, and the final shape of Saturn's work.

first.theme: Leaving inherited Saturn behind and building an adult structure that fits the person's real life.
questions: Which rules did I inherit but never choose?
Where am I avoiding the work that would make me more free?
Where does fear pretend to be maturity?
What structure would let my life hold more truth?

second.theme: Reviewing the life built after the first return and choosing what wisdom, authority, and legacy become now.
questions: What have I built that still matters?
What does age make more honest?
Where am I confusing usefulness with overwork?
What can I now teach, model, or pass on?
commonPressurePoints: simplifying life around what remains true

third.theme: Late-life integration of Saturn's full arc: time, limits, wisdom, completion, and the durable shape of the life.
questions: What is complete enough to release?
What still asks for dignity, structure, or care?

feltTone: A sense that the old way of doing adulthood no longer works.
Pressure to get realistic about time, energy, money, commitment, health, work, or family obligations.
A confrontation with consequences: not as punishment, but as information about what the current structure is producing.
A louder inner judge or critic, especially where the person learned harsh models of authority.
A desire to stop pretending and build something that can last.
A feeling of being asked to choose between staying loyal to inherited expectations and becoming accountable to the life that is actually true now.
outerExamples: A job path, degree, business, or career identity stops feeling sustainable and demands a serious decision.
A relationship can no longer stay vague; commitment, boundaries, repair, or ending must be discussed honestly.
Family expectations become impossible to carry without resentment, forcing adult boundaries.
Money patterns become concrete: debt, unstable income, undercharging, overspending, or lack of planning needs structure.
The body makes the cost of stress, overwork, avoidance, or neglect harder to ignore.
A long-term project asks for discipline, repetition, and patience instead of inspiration alone.
Authority issues surface through bosses, parents, institutions, clients, mentors, legal systems, or the person's own inner authority.
The person realizes they have been rebelling against authority in a way that still lets authority define the shape of their life.
The person has to decide whether the thing they are working so hard for is actually worth the cost.
The person begins building a structure that looks boring from the outside but finally gives their life enough support to grow.
innerExamples: Noticing that fear has been disguised as practicality.
Seeing that constant responsibility can be a way to avoid desire, grief, rest, or risk.
Realizing that harsh self-criticism was learned and does not have to be mistaken for discipline.
Learning that maturity does not mean carrying everything alone.
Recognizing where ambition has been borrowed from family, culture, school, religion, or professional pressure.
Understanding that refusal to choose is still a choice with consequences.
Moving from 'I should' into 'I am willing to be responsible for this.'
greenFlags: The person becomes more honest without becoming cruel to themselves.
They simplify commitments instead of adding more obligations to prove they can cope.
They choose structure that supports life rather than structure that only performs competence.
They ask for help, mentorship, therapy, planning support, or practical guidance when needed.
They make decisions based on long-term reality rather than panic, shame, or outside approval.
They stop confusing delay with failure and start working with time.
redFlags: Making a fear-based decision just to relieve pressure.
Treating burnout as proof of maturity.
Staying in a role, relationship, or family pattern only because it is familiar.
Overcorrecting into rigidity, isolation, cynicism, or emotional shutdown.
Letting the inner critic run the return instead of turning Saturn into a steadier internal authority.

first: Like the costume of adulthood no longer fits.
Like the life built from other people's rules is asking for payment.
Like career, partnership, money, and family choices suddenly have consequences that cannot be postponed.
Like the person must decide what kind of adult they are becoming, not just what they are escaping.
second: Like the life already built is being audited for meaning, usefulness, and truth.
Like age and the body are no longer abstractions.
Like old definitions of productivity, success, beauty, responsibility, and usefulness need to be revised.
Like wisdom wants a form: mentoring, simplifying, teaching, legacy work, or a more honest next chapter.
third: Like the remaining structure of life asks for dignity, care, completion, and truth.
Like time becomes less theoretical and more sacred.
Like the person is asked to honor what endured and release what no longer needs to be carried.

examplesByHouse.1: Identity, body, autonomy, and how the person carries adulthood become the test. Expect questions around self-definition, health, visibility, and whether the person is living as the author of their own life.
examplesByHouse.2: Money, livelihood, values, possessions, and self-worth become the test. Expect budgeting, debt reality, earning strategy, pricing, material security, and the cost of under-valuing the self to become concrete.
examplesByHouse.3: Communication, learning, siblings, daily movement, writing, and mental discipline become the test. Expect pressure to say things clearly, study seriously, finish writing or teaching work, or repair daily communication habits.
examplesByHouse.4: Home, family, roots, parents, ancestry, privacy, and emotional foundations become the test. Expect family boundaries, housing decisions, caretaking roles, property, and the question of what home actually means.
examplesByHouse.5: Creativity, romance, children, joy, risk, and self-expression become the test. Expect the person to take pleasure seriously, structure creative work, mature around dating or children, and stop postponing joy until everything is perfect.
examplesByHouse.6: Work routines, labor, health, service, and maintenance become the test. Expect consequences around burnout, habits, employment conditions, body care, over-functioning, and whether daily life can sustain the person.
examplesByHouse.7: Partnership, marriage, clients, contracts, and open conflict become the test. Expect relationship definitions, commitment talks, boundaries, legal agreements, and whether both people can meet adult responsibility.
examplesByHouse.8: Shared resources, debt, taxes, intimacy, trust, grief, and power become the test. Expect serious conversations around money entanglement, vulnerability, inheritance, sex, therapy, control, or crisis repair.
examplesByHouse.9: Belief, faith, education, travel, publishing, law, and worldview become the test. Expect the person to examine what they believe, what they are willing to study, and whether their philosophy can hold real life.
examplesByHouse.10: Career, reputation, authority, public role, ambition, and legacy become the test. Expect professional consequences, leadership pressure, public accountability, parent/authority themes, and serious choices about contribution.
examplesByHouse.11: Friends, networks, community, audience, hopes, and long-range plans become the test. Expect pruning of social circles, responsibility to community, or the need to build future goals with structure instead of fantasy.
examplesByHouse.12: Solitude, hidden patterns, rest, endings, spirituality, and self-undoing become the test. Expect the person to confront avoidance, isolation, unconscious fear, secret burdens, and the need for disciplined retreat or healing.

examplesBySign.aries: The return asks the person to mature initiative. Expect lessons around starting, anger, courage, independence, and acting with discipline instead of impulse or paralysis.
examplesBySign.taurus: The return asks the person to mature stability. Expect lessons around worth, survival fears, resources, stubbornness, patience, and choosing what is actually worth building.
examplesBySign.gemini: The return asks the person to mature attention and communication. Expect lessons around scattered information, writing, teaching, nervous loops, and committing the mind to a useful long-term purpose.
examplesBySign.cancer: The return asks the person to mature emotional responsibility. Expect lessons around family, protection, caretaking, vulnerability, and creating structure for feeling instead of shutting feeling down.
examplesBySign.leo: The return asks the person to mature visibility and creative power. Expect lessons around joy, pride, performance, leadership, creative discipline, and expressing the self without needing applause to survive.
examplesBySign.virgo: The return asks the person to mature craft, health, and discernment. Expect lessons around perfectionism, daily systems, body feedback, analysis, service, and separating improvement from self-attack.
examplesBySign.libra: The return asks the person to mature relationship and fairness. Expect lessons around boundaries, equality, compromise, resentment, commitment, and standing in the self while staying in connection.
examplesBySign.scorpio: The return asks the person to mature trust and depth. Expect lessons around intimacy, secrecy, power, shared resources, control, and learning which bonds are safe enough to open inside.
examplesBySign.sagittarius: The return asks the person to mature belief and expansion. Expect lessons around faith, study, risk, travel, teaching, truth, and choosing a philosophy that can survive contact with reality.
examplesBySign.capricorn: The return asks the person to mature ambition and authority. Expect lessons around achievement, respect, competence, work, long-term goals, and choosing the right mountain instead of climbing every one.
examplesBySign.aquarius: The return asks the person to mature freedom and individuation. Expect lessons around belonging, rebellion, community, originality, and creating freedom with enough structure to last.
examplesBySign.pisces: The return asks the person to mature surrender and discernment. Expect lessons around fantasy, faith, avoidance, spiritual longing, porous boundaries, and committing to truth rather than escape.

timingMechanics.exactReturn: The exact return is transiting Saturn conjunct natal Saturn by degree.
timingMechanics.orb: Use a wider monitoring window for product messaging, but reserve exact language for close orb. Around 1 degree is strong; stations within about 1-2 degrees deserve special weight.

hitPatterns.singleHit: Saturn perfects the conjunction once. The return may feel concentrated.
hitPatterns.threeHit: Saturn crosses natal Saturn, retrogrades back, then crosses again direct. This often creates a beginning, review, and integration sequence.
hitPatterns.stationNearNatalSaturn: A station near natal Saturn lengthens the encounter and makes the theme harder to ignore.

retrogradeReturnLogic: First direct hit: Saturn names the work.
Retrograde pass or station: the person reviews why the pattern exists and where old authority models still run the show.
Final direct hit: the person commits to a more mature structure or faces the cost of avoiding it.

readingRules.natalSaturnHouse: The natal house of Saturn shows the life area where maturity, authority, discipline, fear, and durable skill are being developed.
readingRules.natalSaturnSign: The natal sign of Saturn shows the style and material of the lesson: how the person handles structure, limits, authority, and self-command.
readingRules.dignity: Dignity modifies how cleanly Saturn can do its work. Dignified Saturn can build with strength; debilitated Saturn may require more repair around fear, rigidity, avoidance, or harsh authority models.
readingRules.sect: Saturn is of the day sect. In day charts, Saturn is more constructive and legible. In night charts, Saturn can feel heavier or harsher and may need more conscious tempering.
readingRules.retrogradeNatalSaturn: Natal Saturn retrograde can point to internalized authority, delayed trust in one's own structure, or the need to reject borrowed definitions of maturity and build an inner authority.
readingRules.natalAspectsToSaturn: Natal aspects to Saturn show which parts of the psyche are pulled into the return. The return reactivates those relationships and asks Saturn to become a more useful advisor, not only a critic.
readingRules.timeLords: If Saturn is also activated by annual profection, zodiacal releasing, or another timing technique, weight the return up. If Saturn is not otherwise activated, still treat the exact return as significant because it is a life-cycle transit.

aspectThemes.sunSaturn: Identity, confidence, visibility, authority, and the right to take up space mature through Saturn.
aspectThemes.moonSaturn: Emotional safety, need, family patterns, and the body's memory of responsibility mature through Saturn.
aspectThemes.mercurySaturn: Thinking, communication, planning, study, writing, and the inner critic mature through Saturn.
aspectThemes.venusSaturn: Worth, love, money, pleasure, commitment, and relational standards mature through Saturn.
aspectThemes.marsSaturn: Action, anger, drive, stamina, boundaries, and the ability to pace effort mature through Saturn.
aspectThemes.jupiterSaturn: Faith, growth, risk, belief, and possibility mature through Saturn's demand for realism.
aspectThemes.uranusSaturn: Freedom and structure must learn to cooperate instead of treating each other as enemies.
aspectThemes.neptuneSaturn: Dreams, surrender, spirituality, and porousness need containers that do not kill the vision.
aspectThemes.plutoSaturn: Power, control, survival strategies, and authority patterns are pressured into deeper integrity.
aspectThemes.chironSaturn: Old wounds around authority, shame, competence, or not being ready can become places of steadier self-support.

voiceGuidance.tone: Direct, grounded, non-fatalistic, mature, compassionate without softening the accountability.
doSay: The old structure is being tested.
You are not being punished; you are being asked to get honest.
Fear is information, not a final answer.
The work is to build a life that can actually hold you.
avoid: Do not treat every hardship as cosmically required.
Do not tell the user what decision to make based on Saturn alone.
Do not romanticize suffering as proof of maturity.
Do not reduce the return to career only.

productSurfaces.overviewCard: Show age band, exact date range if calculated, natal Saturn sign and house, and the main life area being tested.
productSurfaces.timeline: Show first contact, retrograde contact, final contact, and station windows when present.
productSurfaces.interpretation: Blend natal Saturn sign, natal Saturn house, dignity, sect, retrograde condition, and natal Saturn aspects.
reflectionPrompts: Where am I still obeying an authority that no longer has authority over me?
What would become possible if I built a better structure?
What am I ready to take seriously without turning against myself?
What does maturity look like when it includes my actual needs?

prohibitions: Do not frame Saturn Return as guaranteed punishment, failure, divorce, job loss, or crisis.
Do not use Saturn Return alone to advise major life decisions.
Do not ignore natal Saturn house, sign, dignity, sect, retrograde condition, or aspects.
Do not treat second Saturn Return as simply a repeat of the first; it concerns age, wisdom, legacy, and the next chapter of usefulness.
Do not over-focus on career when the natal Saturn house points elsewhere.
weighting: Exact conjunction of transiting Saturn to natal Saturn is the core trigger.
Station within about 1-2 degrees of natal Saturn increases weight and duration.
Natal Saturn house and sign carry more interpretive weight than generic age-band text.
Sect and dignity modify tone: constructive, heavy, blocked, efficient, or strained.
Natal aspects to Saturn identify which psychological functions are tested and matured during the return.

orbs.monitoringWindow: Use a broad window around the return for user awareness, but avoid exact-return language until close orb.
orbs.strong: Within about 1 degree of natal Saturn.
orbs.station: A station within about 1-2 degrees of natal Saturn deserves special emphasis.
orbs.exact: Use ephemeris calculation for exact degree and minute when available.

modifiers.definition: Every chart belongs to one of two sects, day or night, set by whether the Sun is above or below the horizon. Each planet has its own sect affiliation, and a planet operates more comfortably when its sect matches the chart's.

chartSect.diurnal: Sun above the horizon (day chart). The Sun is the sect light.
chartSect.nocturnal: Sun below the horizon (night chart). The Moon is the sect light.

modifiers.mercuryRule: Mercury is common: diurnal when it rises before the Sun (oriental), nocturnal when it sets after the Sun (occidental).
modifiers.inSect: A planet in sect operates more constructively and is better able to deliver its significations.
modifiers.outOfSect: A planet out of sect is less stable. The out-of-sect malefic is the harsher of the two: Saturn is most difficult in a night chart, Mars most difficult in a day chart.
modifiers.paradox: The malefics are placed in the sect opposite their nature so they can be tempered: cold, heavy Saturn is warmed by the day sect; hot, volatile Mars is cooled by the night sect.
modifiers.testimony: Benefics regarding (aspecting) a malefic can moderate or restrain it; a malefic overcome by Jupiter or Venus does less damage.
modifiers.summary: Sect distinguishes day charts from night charts and determines which benefic or malefic is most constructive or difficult.
modifiers.body: Every chart belongs to one of two sects, day or night, set by whether the Sun is above or below the horizon. Each planet has its own sect affiliation, and a planet operates more comfortably when its sect matches the chart's.

modifiers.definition: A planet's condition relative to the Sun. Proximity to the Sun's rays weakens most planets by hiding them, except at the exact center, where the planet is strengthened.
modifiers.appUsage: Down-weight a transiting planet that is combust or under the beams (its signification is obscured). Up-weight a cazimi planet. Note orientality for Mercury's sect.

cazimi.effect: 'In the heart of the Sun'. Strengthened and clarified, the strongest condition.

combust.orb: within 8 degrees of the Sun (outside cazimi)
combust.effect: Burnt up and weakened; the planet's significations are hidden or overpowered.

underTheBeams.orb: within ~15 degrees of the Sun (outside combustion)
underTheBeams.effect: Obscured and diminished, though less severely than combust.

orientality.note: Determines Mercury's and other common planets' sect; also shades how a planet expresses (initiating vs reflective).

modifiers.summary: Solar phase describes whether a planet is strengthened, obscured, or hidden by proximity to the Sun.
modifiers.body: A planet's condition relative to the Sun. Proximity to the Sun's rays weakens most planets by hiding them, except at the exact center, where the planet is strengthened.

modifiers.summary: Stelliums concentrate three or more planetary drives into one sign, house, or tight conjunction pattern.
modifiers.body: A stellium is three or more planets clustered within about 30 degrees, falling in one sign, one house, or both. It concentrates and intensifies one area of life. Read the sign for style, the house for life area, and the planets for the drives packed together.
modifiers.definition: Three or more planets clustered within about 30 degrees, falling in one sign and/or one house. A triple conjunction is three planets in tight conjunction.
appUsage: Detect sign stelliums by counting three or more planets in the same sign.
Detect house stelliums by counting three or more planets in the same house when birth time is accurate.
Treat stelliums as chart-pattern emphasis, not as a replacement for Sun, Moon, Ascendant, chart ruler, sect, dignity, or house rulership.
Read generational-only stelliums as background unless they are angular or tied to a personal planet.
Use the opposite sign or house as a balancing prompt when the stellium area is over-emphasized.
modifiers.note: Imported from approved project stellium material. Source files and named-person examples were not copied into the repository.

definition.what: Three or more planets clustered within about 30 degrees, falling in one sign and/or one house. A triple conjunction is three planets in tight conjunction.
definition.twoKinds: By sign, where the planets share a sign, and by house, where the planets share a house. Often both are true at once.
definition.effect: A stellium concentrates and intensifies one area of life. It can become one of the defining features of a chart.

method: The sign sets the style of the concentrated energy.
The house sets the life area where it plays out.
The planets involved are the specific drives packed together; each one wants attention.
The challenge is integration: the planets compete like a room full of strong personalities, and the area can be over-emphasized while its opposite is neglected.
The growth is to mature the cluster into a concentrated strength, so the area becomes a major life theme and a source of mastery.
classes.polarityNote: The house and sign opposite the stellium are often underdeveloped and benefit from conscious attention.

bySign.plainTranslation: A stellium in Aries pours major energy into drive, initiative, and selfhood. Gift: tremendous force to start and lead. Watch: impatience, self-focus, and burning out from going too hard.
A stellium in Taurus concentrates on stability, resources, and the senses. Gift: persistence and the power to build something lasting. Watch: stubbornness and resistance to change.
A stellium in Gemini floods the mind with communication, curiosity, and learning. Gift: a fast, versatile, articulate mind. Watch: scattered focus and living in the head.
A stellium in Cancer concentrates on feeling, home, and care. Gift: deep emotional intelligence and a gift for nurturing. Watch: moodiness, over-attachment, and retreating.
A stellium in Leo pours energy into self-expression, creativity, and being seen. Gift: magnetism, warmth, and creative power. Watch: ego, drama, and needing the spotlight.
A stellium in Virgo concentrates on analysis, craft, and service. Gift: precision, skill, and genuine usefulness. Watch: perfectionism, criticism, and anxiety over details.
A stellium in Libra focuses on relationship, balance, and beauty. Gift: a talent for connection, fairness, and harmony. Watch: indecision, people-pleasing, and losing yourself in others.
A stellium in Scorpio concentrates on depth, intensity, and transformation. Gift: power, focus, and the ability to go where others won't. Watch: obsession, control, and all-or-nothing extremes.
A stellium in Sagittarius pours energy into meaning, freedom, and the big picture. Gift: vision, optimism, and a drive to grow. Watch: restlessness, overreach, and dodging the details.

A stellium in Capricorn concentrates on ambition, structure, and achievement. Gift: discipline and the capacity to build serious, lasting things. Watch: workaholism, coldness, and worth tied to output.
A stellium in Aquarius focuses on innovation, ideas, and the collective. Gift: originality and a vision ahead of its time. Watch: detachment, contrarianism, and living in theory.
A stellium in Pisces concentrates on imagination, sensitivity, and the unseen. Gift: deep empathy, creativity, and intuition. Watch: escapism, blurred boundaries, and overwhelm.

byHouse.plainTranslation: A stellium in the 1st house concentrates on identity and self; your presence is unusually strong and defining. Gift: a powerful sense of self. Watch: self-absorption and forgetting others exist.
A stellium in the 2nd house intensifies money, values, and self-worth; building security becomes a central theme. Gift: a talent for creating value. Watch: tying worth to what you own.

A stellium in the 3rd house floods communication, learning, and daily connection; the mind and immediate environment dominate. Gift: a sharp, communicative mind. Watch: mental overload and scattered energy.

A stellium in the 4th house concentrates on home, family, and roots; your foundation carries enormous weight. Gift: deep roots and a strong base. Watch: living in the past and difficulty leaving the nest.

A stellium in the 5th house pours energy into creativity, romance, and self-expression; play and creation are central. Gift: huge creative output and vitality. Watch: drama and chasing the next thrill.

A stellium in the 6th house intensifies work, health, and daily routine; being useful and refining your craft dominate. Gift: capacity for skilled, devoted work. Watch: overwork, worry, and self-criticism.

A stellium in the 7th house concentrates on partnership and one-to-one relationships; other people are a defining theme. Gift: a gift for relating and collaboration. Watch: losing yourself in others and dependence.

A stellium in the 8th house intensifies intimacy, shared resources, and transformation; depth, power, and merging are central. Gift: capacity for deep bonding and rebirth. Watch: power struggles, control, and crisis.

A stellium in the 9th house pours energy into meaning, learning, travel, and belief; the search for the bigger picture dominates. Gift: vision and a drive to expand. Watch: restlessness and chasing the horizon.

A stellium in the 10th house concentrates on career, status, and public role; your work in the world is a defining theme. Gift: ambition and the capacity to achieve. Watch: identity swallowed by career.

A stellium in the 11th house intensifies community, friendships, and future goals; the collective and your hopes dominate. Gift: a talent for networks and shared vision. Watch: losing the personal in the group.

A stellium in the 12th house concentrates on the inner, hidden, and spiritual; the unconscious carries great weight. Gift: a rich inner life and compassion. Watch: escapism, isolation, and self-undoing.

illustrativeExamples.note: Original demonstrations of the reading method, composed from planet, sign, and house meanings. Named-person sample charts are not included.
illustrativeExamples.howToRead: Name the planets, the sign, and the house, then state the integrated gift and the watch-out.
illustrativeExamples.generationalVsPersonal: A stellium made only of slow outer planets is shared by a whole generation. It becomes personal when it sits on an angle or aspects a personal planet: Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, or Mars.

examples.combo: Sun, Mercury, Venus in Gemini, 3rd house
examples.plainTranslation: Identity, thinking, and love all concentrated in communication. Gift: a magnetic communicator whose whole self runs through words and connection. Watch: living in the head and mistaking talking for relating.

examples.combo: Moon, Venus, Mars in the 5th house
examples.plainTranslation: Feeling, love, and drive packed into creativity and romance. Gift: enormous creative and romantic vitality. Watch: emotional drama and chasing the next thrill.
Drive, discipline, and intensity stacked in the most intense sign. Gift: formidable, unstoppable focus. Watch: control, all-or-nothing extremes, and burnout when it stays unintegrated.

examples.combo: Sun, Jupiter, Uranus in the 10th house
examples.plainTranslation: Identity, expansion, and innovation aimed at career and public role. Gift: a bold, original public path. Watch: career swallowing the rest of life, and restlessness with anything stable.

examples.combo: Mercury, Venus, Neptune in Pisces, 12th house
examples.plainTranslation: Mind, love, and imagination dissolved together in the hidden house. Gift: deep artistic and compassionate sensitivity. Watch: escapism and blurred boundaries between self and others.

prohibitions: Do not treat a stellium as automatically stronger than every other chart factor.
Do not ignore the individual planets involved.
Do not use house stelliums without accurate birth time.
Do not over-personalize a generational outer-planet cluster unless it contacts an angle or personal planet.
weighting: Weight up when the stellium includes Sun, Moon, Ascendant ruler, or multiple personal planets.
Weight up when the stellium is angular or tied to the chart ruler.
Weight down when the cluster is only slow outer planets and does not contact personal points.
Use the opposite sign or house as an integration prompt.

modifiers.summary: Synastry readings compare one chart against another with ordered interaspects, house overlays, and explicit ethical boundaries.
modifiers.body: Synastry shows relationship dynamics, pressure points, attraction patterns, and growth requirements. It does not decide whether someone should stay, leave, commit, or excuse harmful behavior.
modifiers.definition: Synastry is the comparison of Person A placements to Person B placements and houses.
appUsage: Use ordered keys because Person A to Person B can read differently than Person B to Person A.
Separate interaspect interpretation from house overlay interpretation.
Show strengths and challenges without deterministic language.
Escalate serious relationship safety concerns to non-astrological support language.
modifiers.note: Imported from the project policy bundle; source file was not copied into the repo.

interaspects.rationale: Two independent charts, not co-measured, so no elongation exclusions. Order matters for interpretation: A's Venus on B's Mars differs from B's Venus on A's Mars. 10x10 ordered pairs x 5 aspects = 500.

houseOverlays.rationale: One person's planet falls in the other's house, coloring that life area. Stored once as planet-in-house and applied in both directions (A-in-B and B-in-A) by the app.

principles: Descriptive, not deterministic. A chart shows tendencies and pressures, never fate or a compatibility verdict.
Hard aspects name areas of work and growth, never doom or proof of incompatibility.
Both people are free agents. Readings support choice, never obligation to stay or go.
prohibitedFramings: Predetermined-bond language that pressures someone to stay.
Framing jealousy, control, isolation, surveillance, or coercion as romantic, required, or owed.
Karmic-debt framing that casts suffering as deserved or unavoidable.
Clinical or diagnostic claims about either person's mind or health.
Any 'you'll never do better' or scarcity messaging.
requiredFramings: Name the dynamic, then offer something the people can actually do with it.
Treat difficulty as workable and optional, not a sentence.
ethics.safety: If a user describes abuse, control, or fear, the product surfaces support options rather than an astrological explanation. Astrology never rationalizes harm.
ethics.consent: Synastry uses a second person's birth data. Assume that person has not consented to being analyzed; keep output about the dynamic, not a verdict on them.
ethics.reviewGate: All relationship content stays DRAFT until reviewed against this policy. This policy itself needs human sign-off before any synastry content ships READY.

prohibitions: Do not call abusive dynamics soul work, required growth, or proof of a bond.
Do not tell a user to stay in or leave a relationship based on charts alone.
Do not use compatibility language that removes choice, agency, or context.

modifiers.summary: Synastry compares two natal charts to describe relationship dynamics without treating the chart as a verdict.
modifiers.body: Synastry compares two charts to read how two people interact and activate each other. It describes the connection and its dynamics; it does not decree the outcome. Read it as the meeting of two natal charts, not as a verdict.
modifiers.definition: Synastry compares two charts to read how two people interact and activate each other. It describes the connection and its dynamics; it does not decree the outcome. Read it as the meeting of two natal charts, not as a verdict.
appUsage: Read each natal chart first, then synastry, then composite.
Use synastry to describe activation, friction, support, and timing; do not present it as a fixed outcome or a compatibility score.
Prioritize personal planets, luminaries, angles, tight interaspects, and house overlays.
Downweight outer-planet, Chiron, and modern-point contacts between people of similar age unless they contact a personal planet or angle.
Keep relationship guidance choice-centered and avoid telling users to stay in or leave a relationship based on charts alone.
modifiers.note: Expanded from approved project relationship and synastry source material. Source files were not copied into the repository.

classes.synastryVsComposite: Synastry = how the two individuals interact (the initial connection and its push-pull). Composite = how the relationship itself behaves as its own entity. Order of reading: each natal chart first, then synastry, then composite.

method.name: Read each natal chart first
method.detail: Unresolved patterns in an individual chart get carried into every relationship, so read both charts alone before comparing. Key relational signals: the Moon (the needs a partner must meet), Venus (what the person seeks in love, by sign/house/aspect), the 7th house (partnership), houses 5 and 8 (romance, intimacy, shared life), and the Sun and Moon as the relational luminaries. No synastry can override an individual chart whose conflicts are unworked.

method.name: Check the relationship promise
method.detail: Before judging the comparison, identify what each chart is already asking for in partnership. Use the 1st/7th polarity, the ruler of the 7th, planets in or ruling the 7th, Venus, Mars, the Moon, and repeated natal aspect patterns. If the synastry gives a person something their own chart does not want or cannot receive, chemistry alone will not carry it.

method.name: Element balance
method.detail: Weigh the dominant element of each whole chart (not just the Suns). Fire-Fire stimulates but risks aggression; Fire-Air feeds and animates; Fire-Earth and Fire-Water need care; Earth-Earth steadies but can flatten; Air-Air connects mentally but drifts; Water-Water bonds deeply but can pool into moodiness; mixed pairs each ask the partners to lend what the other lacks.

method.name: Planet overlays
method.detail: Place each person's planets into the other's houses to see which life areas they activate. The house person feels the contact in that area of life.

planetInHouse.sun: illuminates and brings attention to that area
planetInHouse.moon: sensitizes it and creates needs there
planetInHouse.venus: brings pleasure and ease to that area
planetInHouse.mars: activates and energizes it (and can heat it up)
planetInHouse.jupiter: is where the partner helps you grow
planetInHouse.saturn: is where the bond steadies you and also where it can inhibit you
planetInHouse.uranus: brings surprise and openness to the new
planetInHouse.neptune: idealizes and spiritualizes it (watch for illusion)
planetInHouse.pluto: brings depth and the pressure to transform
planetInHouse.chiron: is where the partner can both wound and help heal

method.toTheAscendant: Benefic/personal contacts (Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter) to a partner's Ascendant tend to feel good; Mars, Saturn, and the outers/Chiron are heavier to carry.
method.overlayRule: Overlay meaning belongs first to the house person: the planet person brings a function, but the house person experiences where it lands. Read the overlay together with the planet's condition and aspects, because a planet in a partner's house can support, pressure, awaken, or irritate that house depending on the contact.

method.name: Interaspects
method.detail: The aspects formed between one person's planets and the other's. Harmonious contacts ease the bond; tense ones bring friction but can add depth and growth, and a relationship with only easy aspects tends to go flat. An aspect must actually form by degree, not merely share an element.
method.orbs: About 2 to 3 degrees for conjunction, sextile, square, trine, and opposition; allow 1 to 2 degrees more for the luminaries.

method.name: Cross-chart configurations
method.detail: Check whether one person's planets complete or activate a major pattern in the other's chart. A partner can close a T-square, supply a missing leg of a grand cross, activate a yod, or complete an easy-flow pattern. These contacts often feel consequential because the relationship turns on a natal pattern that was already waiting for activation.

patterns.tSquareCompletion: One person's planet completes the missing leg of another person's square/opposition pattern, increasing pressure and making the unresolved conflict impossible to ignore.
patterns.grandTrineCompletion: One person's planet completes an easy-flow triangle, bringing comfort and natural support, but sometimes reducing urgency to grow.
patterns.yodActivation: One person's planet touches the apex or release point of another person's yod-like pattern, making the bond feel like a turning point or specialized growth demand.
patterns.samePlanetAspects: Same-planet contacts are usually background rapport unless that planet rules a luminary, angle, or major relationship house.

method.name: Turning-point indicators
method.detail: Contacts sometimes read as karmic, ancestral, or turning-point material, but the product should keep this belief-neutral and describe the lived pattern instead of making literal claims about past lives.
indicators: one person's planet conjunct the other's lunar node
a node conjunct the partner's Ascendant
one person's Saturn conjunct or in tight aspect to the other's planets (duty, durability, a sense of test)
one person's planets falling in the other's 12th house
a planet or angle conjunct the partner's Vertex (a turning-point pull; Vertex-Ascendant is common)

method.name: The astrological moment
method.detail: Read current transits and the coming year for both people. Timing conditions whether a bond forms, deepens, or strains, independent of the static synastry.

relationshipPromise.definition: The natal chart describes what a person is wired to seek, repeat, resist, or negotiate in partnership before any second chart enters the room.
readFrom: planets in the 7th house and aspects to the 7th ruler
Venus for love language, pleasure, and attraction style
Mars for pursuit, desire, anger, and conflict style
Moon for attachment needs and daily emotional safety
Saturn contacts for fear, defense, commitment, and durability patterns
5th and 8th houses for romance, sex, shared resources, and psychological merging
relationshipPromise.use: Compare the synastry against each person's natal relationship promise. Strong contacts matter more when they answer a real natal need; they matter less when they only create temporary excitement.

highSignalHouses.1: Identity, embodiment, attraction, immediate recognition, and how the house person feels seen or altered by the planet person.
highSignalHouses.4: Home, family, memory, roots, emotional privacy, and whether the planet person feels safe or intrusive.
highSignalHouses.5: Romance, pleasure, play, creativity, fertility themes, and whether the planet person wakes up joy or performance pressure.
highSignalHouses.7: Partnership identity, commitment projection, open conflict, and the classic feeling of meeting the other half of an axis.
highSignalHouses.8: Intimacy, sex, shared resources, debt, trust, vulnerability, and power dynamics.
highSignalHouses.10: Public life, reputation, ambition, status, parent/authority themes, and life direction.

overlayPriority.interpretiveRule: Overlay houses are not compatibility scores. They show the stage where the partner's planet acts. A beautiful planet in a difficult house can still feel loaded; a difficult planet in a useful house can become productive if both people handle it consciously.

keyInteraspects.sun-sun: Shared core temperament. Harmonious aspects bring easy mutual respect and aligned goals; opposition attracts strongly; square and quincunx grate.
keyInteraspects.sun-moon: A classic compatibility contact, especially the conjunction: one person's core self meets the other's emotional nature. Hard aspects do not doom it.
keyInteraspects.sun-mercury: Good aspects bring mental rapport; hard ones, misunderstanding.
keyInteraspects.sun-mars: The Mars person energizes and initiates the Sun person, and can also irritate them.
keyInteraspects.sun-saturn: Can forge durability and commitment; poorly aspected, it may bind two people together more out of fear of change than desire.
keyInteraspects.moon-moon: Key for daily life together; even without an exact aspect, compatible elements ease the everyday exchange.
keyInteraspects.moon-mars: Stimulating but friction-prone; the Moon person's feelings bruise easily on hard contacts.
keyInteraspects.moon-saturn: A maturity test: the Moon can feel weighed down by duty while Saturn offers stability. It works when the Moon values Saturn's steadiness and Saturn softens toward the Moon's feelings.
keyInteraspects.moon-pluto: Intense emotional depth and attachment; on hard contacts it can tip into control or possessiveness.
keyInteraspects.venus-saturn: Loyalty and commitment when well-aspected, with Venus supplying the warmth Saturn struggles to show; hard contacts can withhold affection.
keyInteraspects.venus-uranus: Instant, electric attraction; exciting but not inherently durable, and can cool as fast as it sparked.
keyInteraspects.venus-neptune: Tenderness and idealization; lovely but needs grounding so it does not slide into illusion.
keyInteraspects.venus-pluto: Magnetic, deep, sometimes compulsive attraction and strong bonding.
keyInteraspects.mars-saturn: Drive meets restraint. It can build disciplined effort in practical or business bonds, but hard contacts can feel blocked, criticized, or sexually frustrated unless the couple has constructive outlets.
keyInteraspects.jupiter-uranus: Growth meets freedom. It can make the bond generous, exciting, and spacious, but needs grounding so the relationship does not become all possibility and no container.
keyInteraspects.jupiter-pluto: Expansion meets intensity. It can support shared ambition, business growth, or deep mutual transformation, but can also amplify control or excess.
keyInteraspects.saturn-saturn: A shared sense of responsibility; stabilizing for long bonds, while hard aspects test each other's security.

configurationLogic.principle: When two charts are combined, one person's planets can activate patterns that are quiet or incomplete in the other chart. Treat this as a major interpretive signal when the contact is tight and involves personal planets or angles.
readBeforeConclusion: Does the partner complete a missing leg of an existing natal pattern?
Does the partner's planet hit the apex, release point, or most stressed planet in the natal configuration?
Does the configuration repeat relationship themes already shown by the 7th house, Venus, Mars, Moon, or Saturn?
Is the pattern supported by easy contacts, or only intensified by pressure contacts?
configurationLogic.warning: A completed pattern can feel compelling without being healthy. Describe what gets activated and what skills are required; do not sell activation as proof of permanence.

nodesAndAngles.principle: Nodes, Vertex, angles, and 12th-house overlays can describe relationships that feel consequential, familiar, unfinished, or strangely timed. Keep the language experiential and belief-neutral.
useWhen: a node tightly contacts a partner's personal planet or angle
a partner's planet falls close to the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, or IC
several personal planets fall in the 12th house
the Vertex is tightly contacted by a personal planet or angle
nodesAndAngles.avoid: Do not promise a fixed outcome, past-life certainty, or spiritual obligation. The app should name the pull, the pattern, and the choices.

classes.ethicalBoundary: Synastry shows dynamics and potentials, not fixed outcomes. Do not frame abusive dynamics as lessons, ignore red flags, or create dependence on astrological validation.

houseOverlays.scope: Your planets in the other person's wheel: each planet is read through all 12 partner houses, with the house person treated as the one receiving the activation.
houseOverlays.use: Use overlays to locate where the relationship becomes personal: identity, money, communication, home, romance, daily life, partnership, intimacy, worldview, public life, community, or hidden material.
houseOverlays.caution: Do not read an overlay as automatically good or bad. The planet's condition, aspects, and the house person's natal relationship promise decide whether the activation feels supportive, intrusive, useful, exciting, or heavy.

interaspects.scope: Major contacts between Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, angles, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto.
priorities: Luminary contacts describe identity and emotional safety.
Mercury contacts describe whether the people can understand each other and keep talking.
Venus and Mars contacts describe affection, attraction, pursuit, desire, conflict, and chemistry.
Angle contacts make the relationship immediately embodied and hard to ignore.
Jupiter contacts describe growth, generosity, shared confidence, and the risk of excess.
Saturn contacts describe durability, duty, restraint, fear, maturity, and whether the bond can carry real life.
Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto contacts describe disruption, idealization, intensity, compulsion, and transformation; weight them most when they touch a personal planet or angle.
interaspects.caution: Exact contact matters. A sign-based affinity can support rapport, but it is not the same as a degree-based interaspect.

configurations.scope: T-squares, yods, grand trines, grand crosses, and other cross-chart patterns created when one person's planets activate the other's natal geometry.
configurations.use: After individual aspects are read, look for the larger pattern. A relationship can feel important because it completes a pattern, not because every contact is easy.
configurations.caution: A completed pattern can increase pressure as much as compatibility. Name the activation and the work it asks for.

nodes.scope: Lunar nodes in synastry, especially tight contacts to personal planets, angles, Saturn, or the 12th-house layer.
nodes.use: Use nodes for the relationship depth layer: familiarity, growth direction, old habits, timing, and the feeling that the connection opens a chapter.
nodes.caution: Keep the language belief-neutral. Do not promise past-life certainty, spiritual obligation, or a fixed outcome.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Natal relationship capacity
relationshipReadingChecklist.check: Read each person's Moon, Venus, Mars, Saturn, 1st/7th axis, 5th house, 8th house, and 7th ruler before comparing charts.
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: This shows what the person can receive, repeat, defend against, or ask for in relationship.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Partnership promise
relationshipReadingChecklist.check: Ask what each chart describes as partnership material before claiming compatibility.
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: A strong contact matters more when it answers a real natal partnership need.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Immediate recognition
relationshipReadingChecklist.check: Check Sun, Moon, Ascendant, Descendant, IC, MC, and planets on angles.
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: Angle and luminary contacts make the bond visible, embodied, and personally felt.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Emotional and daily fit
relationshipReadingChecklist.check: Prioritize Moon-Moon, Sun-Moon, Moon-Venus, Moon-Mars, Moon-Saturn, and Moon overlays.
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: Chemistry does not replace the daily emotional climate.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Communication capacity
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: A lasting bond needs enough shared language to repair misunderstanding.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Attraction and conflict
relationshipReadingChecklist.check: Read Venus, Mars, 5th-house overlays, and 8th-house overlays together.
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: This separates attraction, affection, sexual heat, and psychological merging.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Durability and strain
relationshipReadingChecklist.check: Read Saturn contacts, Saturn overlays, hard Mars-Saturn, and hard Venus-Saturn before promising longevity.
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: Saturn can hold a bond together, but it can also make the bond feel cold, blocked, or obligatory.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Growth and destabilizers
relationshipReadingChecklist.check: Read Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto only after the personal planet story is clear.
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: These contacts add expansion, freedom, fog, and intensity, but they should not carry the whole reading unless tied to personal planets or angles.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Configurations and nodes
relationshipReadingChecklist.check: Check whether the two charts create T-squares, yods, grand trines, grand crosses, nodal contacts, Vertex contacts, or repeated 12th-house themes.
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: These show why the relationship feels like a turning point or pressure point.

relationshipReadingChecklist.name: Composite synthesis
relationshipReadingChecklist.check: Read the composite only after the natal and synastry layers are clear.
relationshipReadingChecklist.reason: The composite describes the relationship field, not whether either person should stay in it.

interaspectFamilies.sun: Sun interaspects show how one person's identity, confidence, and life direction meet the other's planets or angles.
interaspectFamilies.moon: Moon interaspects show emotional safety, instinctive reaction, attachment patterns, and what daily life feels like together.
interaspectFamilies.mercury: Mercury interaspects show conversation, listening, learning, misunderstanding, repair, and whether the bond can stay mentally connected.
interaspectFamilies.venus: Venus interaspects show affection, ease, pleasure, attraction style, agreement, taste, and how love is offered or received.
interaspectFamilies.mars: Mars interaspects show pursuit, anger, desire, heat, competition, and whether action becomes teamwork or conflict.
interaspectFamilies.angles: Angle contacts show immediacy, embodiment, recognition, public/private impact, and the way one person alters the other's life direction or self-presentation.
interaspectFamilies.jupiter: Jupiter interaspects show growth, generosity, shared belief, humor, opportunity, and the risk of overpromising or excess.
interaspectFamilies.saturn: Saturn interaspects show commitment, tests, duty, restraint, maturity, endurance, fear, delay, and the bond's capacity to handle real life.
interaspectFamilies.uranus: Uranus interaspects show electricity, freedom, disruption, novelty, inconsistency, and the need for space or unconventional terms.
interaspectFamilies.neptune: Neptune interaspects show compassion, imagination, idealization, projection, confusion, spiritual longing, and the need for reality checks.
interaspectFamilies.pluto: Pluto interaspects show intensity, compulsion, power dynamics, psychological depth, transformation, and the need for clean boundaries.

weighting: Personal planets (Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars), the luminaries, and the angles carry the most weight.

Outer/transpersonal planets (Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) and Chiron should be discounted between people of similar age, since they will be near-conjunct for a whole generation. They matter mainly across significant age gaps, or when they land on a personal planet or an angle. This mirrors the modern-points policy: never let a generational contact carry a reading on its own.
Read both natal charts before the synastry; the synastry cannot fix an unresolved individual chart.
Use tight orbs and require the aspect to actually form; 'compatible by element' is not the same as an exact contact.
Some hard aspects are necessary; an all-harmonious synastry tends to be flat, and tension can carry the growth.
Percentage 'compatibility scores' are marketing, not signal; weigh the actual contacts.
An accurate birth time matters, since the Moon, angles, and house overlays depend on it.

orbs.majorAspects: Use about 2 to 3 degrees for conjunction, sextile, square, trine, and opposition; allow 1 to 2 degrees more for the luminaries when the contact is central.
orbs.exactness: Require the aspect to actually form by degree. Elemental compatibility alone is not an interaspect.

modifiers.definition: Time-lord systems answer 'why now' by dividing a life into chapters, each governed by a planet whose natal condition colors that span. Transits only matter when they activate the period's lord.

annualProfections.definition: Each year of life advances the focus one whole sign from the Ascendant. The ruler of the profected sign is the Lord of the Year.

computation.profectedSign: the sign that many whole signs from the natal Ascendant, counterclockwise
computation.lordOfYear: the domicile ruler of the profected sign (use dignity.domicile)
computation.monthly: from the annual profected sign, advance one sign per ~month (12 over the year) for the Lord of the Month
computation.daily: subdivide the month the same way for a Lord of the Day

interpretationRules: The year's topics are read from the profected house (see houseTopics).
The Lord of the Year's natal condition (house, sign, dignity, sect, aspects) sets the year's quality.
That year, transits TO or FROM the Lord of the Year and TO the profected sign are the ones that fire; others are background.
If the Lord of the Year is also currently transited by a malefic, weight the year's difficulty up; by a benefic, down.
A profection to a house activates the planets natally in that house and the planet ruling it.
The profected sign is active in both the natal chart and the Solar Return chart for that year.
Planets natally in the profected sign are activated, but only the traditional seven planets can become Lord of the Year.

The Lord of the Year is the first transit filter: prioritize transits to the natal Lord of the Year, transits to the Solar Return Lord of the Year, transits made by the Lord of the Year, and transits through the profected sign.
Angular profection years (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) are generally louder than cadent years, especially when the same sign or ruler is angular in the Solar Return.

method.rule: Each year of life, the focus advances one whole sign/house from the Ascendant. Age 0 = 1st house; the cycle repeats every 12 years (age mod 12 + 1 = the profected house).
method.timeLord: The ruler of the profected house is that year's time-lord. Watch where that planet sits by sign and house, and what transits it receives, for the year's dominant theme.
method.activation: The sign on the profected house and its ruler color the year; transits to the time-lord are emphasized.

zodiacalReleasing.definition: Releases time from a Lot through the signs, each sign lasting its ruler's period-years, producing nested life chapters (L1 major, L2 sub, L3, L4).

lots.spirit: career, action, mind, reputation, the volitional life

zodiacalReleasing.signPeriodNote: Each sign's L1 length equals its ruler's period-years (Cancer=Moon 25, Leo=Sun 19, etc.). L2 subdivides that span through all twelve signs in order.
mechanics: Start L1 at the sign of the Lot; advance through signs in order, each lasting its signPeriodYears.
Within each L1, run L2 through all twelve signs, each L2 lasting its own signPeriodYears, scaled into the L1 span.
'Loosing of the bond': when an L2 run completes the zodiac and would pass the sign opposite its start, it jumps to that opposite sign instead. Marks a major turning point.
Peak periods: L2 periods whose sign is angular (1st/4th/7th/10th) to the Lot of Fortune are high-activity 'peak' times; signs in aversion to the Lot are low/quiet.
interpretationRules: Read Spirit-based ZR for career and chosen action; Fortune-based for body, health, and circumstance.
The current L1/L2 ruling sign and its lord describe the chapter's theme; the lord's natal condition sets its quality.
Treat MVP use as advisory background ('what season of life'), not a daily trigger.
zodiacalReleasing.note: Advanced; structured here for later. Not required for the daily MVP, but the period numbers and peak rule are enough to compute chapters.

modifiers.summary: Selection and ranking guidance for deciding which active transits matter most before interpretation is looked up.
modifiers.body: Use this as the transit significance layer. It ranks active contacts before meaning is rendered. It does not interpret the transit itself; once a transit is selected, the app should look up the appropriate transit-to-natal, transit-house, or event-example content.
modifiers.definition: Transit significance is the weighting process that prioritizes active transits by transiting body, aspect, natal target, tightness, applying or separating motion, angularity, natal emphasis, and larger timing context.
appUsage: Compute candidate active transits first, then rank them by significance rather than tightest orb alone.
Use the numeric model as a tunable starting point, not a fixed doctrine.
Select top transits per product lane, such as Business, Creative, and Self.
Always interpret the selected transit through natal promise, house context, and broader timing testimony.
Do not let a high score become a deterministic event prediction.
modifiers.note: Imported from approved project transit-significance material. Source file was not copied into the repository.

scoringModel.note: Weights are a proposed starting model. Relative priority is meaningful; exact numbers should be calibrated against real app output.
scoringModel.formula: score = bodyWeight * aspectWeight * targetWeight * tightnessFactor * applyingFactor
scoringModel.natalEmphasisBonus: Multiply the target weight by about 1.3 when the natal point is heavily aspected, angular, close to an angle, chart-ruling, or otherwise repeated in the chart.

applyingFactor.note: Applying aspects are building and should rank above separating aspects with otherwise similar testimony.

priorityFlags.slowPlanetOnAngle: When Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, or Pluto conjoins Ascendant, IC, Descendant, or MC, flag the window around exact as a major period even if ordinary scoring would rank another transit higher.
priorityFlags.outerPlanetSignOrHouseChange: Flag when Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, or Pluto changes sign or enters a new natal house. Treat this as a shift of background theme, not one isolated event.

eclipseRules.countsWhen: Prioritize eclipses within about 4 degrees of conjunction, square, or opposition to the Sun, Moon, an angle, or a heavily emphasized natal planet.

nodeFlavor.northNode: Opening, appetite, increase, invitation, or directional pull.
nodeFlavor.southNode: Release, reduction, completion, letting go, or draining away.

eclipseRules.lunarVsSolar: Lunar eclipses often land emotionally and are felt most strongly in the days before exact. Solar eclipses are more likely to describe external or event-like shifts when the chart repeats the theme.

prohibitions: Do not interpret from the score alone.
Do not turn a high-ranking transit into a guaranteed event.
Do not let outer-planet background contacts dominate daily check-ins unless they are tight, angular, repeated, or hitting personal planets.
Do not rank eclipses as important unless they contact a meaningful natal point or house topic.
weighting: Angles, Sun, Moon, chart ruler, sect light, and activated time lords outrank background contacts.
Applying aspects rank higher than separating aspects when other factors are similar.
Tightness matters, but exactness alone is not enough if the natal target is low-relevance.
Slow planets on angles can describe major periods and deserve priority flags.
Daily lanes should select the strongest few transits rather than overloading the user with every active contact.

modifiers.summary: Ordered transit-to-natal contacts use every transiting planet against a fixed natal planet or point, without same-moment elongation exclusions.
modifiers.body: Use this policy for the app check-in layer. Same-moment aspect impossibilities do not apply here because the moving body can sweep the full zodiac against a natal placement fixed at birth.
modifiers.definition: Transit-to-natal aspects are ordered contacts from a current sky body to a natal body or sensitive point.
appUsage: Use ordered keys in the form transiting_natal_aspect.
Do not apply same-moment impossibility filters to transit-to-natal lookups.
For daily check-ins, gather in-orb contacts and prioritize tightness, speed, chart relevance, and user-facing weight.
Keep outer-planet contacts contextual unless they are tight, repeated, angular, or hitting a personal planet.
modifiers.note: Imported from the project policy bundle; source file was not copied into the repo.

classes.rationale: A transiting body sweeps the whole zodiac against a fixed natal point. The two are NOT co-measured, so the same-moment elongation exclusions do NOT apply. Every transiting->natal->aspect combination is valid.
classes.selection: For the daily check-in, gather all in-orb transit->natal contacts, then pick the tightest by |separation - aspectAngle|. Lane assignment (Business/Creative/Self) is downstream of selection.
classes.applyingSeparating: Compare transiting speed and direction to the aspect angle. Applying (tightening) reads as building; separating (loosening) reads as fading. Retrograde reverses the direction of approach.
cautions: Moon transits resolve in hours; treat as same-day texture, not multi-day themes.
Outer-planet transits (Saturn->Pluto) stay in orb for weeks to years; they are background, not daily weather.
Angle and node transits require an accurate birth time; degrade gracefully if time is unknown.

prohibitions: Do not filter transit-to-natal contacts through same-moment elongation impossibilities.

modifiers.summary: Uranus cycle milestones mark phases of individuation, disruption, freedom, reinvention, and changing relationship to the life script.
modifiers.body: Use Uranus cycle milestones as long-range life-cycle context. The first square, opposition, last square, and return can coincide with changes in freedom, identity, work, community, technology, and the need to stop living inside an inherited pattern. Because Uranus is a modern outer planet, treat this as a modern lens and do not use it in traditional dignity, sect, rulership, or time-lord logic.
modifiers.definition: Uranus takes about 84 years to return to its natal position, with major quarter-cycle checkpoints around ages 21, 42, 63, and 84.
appUsage: Compute exact Uranus contacts to natal Uranus by degree; do not rely on age alone.
Label this explicitly as a modern outer-planet life-cycle layer.
Use the cycle to contextualize life phases, not to predict sudden events by itself.
Check transits to angles, Sun, Moon, chart ruler, and time-lord context before surfacing event examples.
modifiers.note: Expanded from approved project outer-planet source material. Source files were not copied into the repository.

cycleFacts.segments: Four roughly 21-year phases: initiation, cultivation, review, adjustment.
cycleFacts.theme: A long story of dissatisfaction with the status quo and learning to value the eccentric, one-of-a-kind self. Upheaval (the Tower) asks you to improvise, innovate, and adapt.

milestones.plainTranslation: First Uranus square. Rebellion, throwing off inherited rules, claiming a life that's your own. Unsettling: you may not know who you are or what you want yet.
milestones.guidance: Experiment and break from what you inherited, but don't burn down everything that works.

milestones.plainTranslation: The Uranus opposition, the classic midlife awakening. Unlike at 21, you know who you are. The question now is whether you still want to be that person. It surfaces every way you don't fit.
milestones.guidance: Make the change you actually need, deliberately, not as a reactive blow-up.

milestones.plainTranslation: The last Uranus square, traditionally the threshold into retirement. New freedom can feel disorienting after a lifetime of structure.
milestones.guidance: Choose how you spend the freedom on purpose. Keep group and community ties; they matter now.

milestones.plainTranslation: The once-in-a-lifetime Uranus return. A final reinvention, and a rejection of society's script for old age.
milestones.guidance: Claim your independence on your own terms.

oppositionMidlife: Restlessness around the life already built, especially when old goals feel abandoned or unexpressed.
A return to school, training, creative practice, or an earlier dream that had been set aside for practical reasons.
A career pivot, leaving a role, exploring self-employment, or changing the structure of work so there is more autonomy.
Relationship reevaluation: changing roles inside the relationship, asking for more freedom, or ending patterns that have gone stagnant.
Impulsive purchases or lifestyle changes as a substitute for the deeper freedom question; treat these as signals, not solutions.
Small controlled changes to routine can discharge the pressure before it becomes a full life overhaul.
constructiveOutlets: Learn something outside the usual lane.
Change a daily routine in a low-risk way before making a major break.
Test a new work format, side project, or independent offer before quitting stable income.
Switch roles in a relationship conversation so each person sees the pattern from the other side.
Use the need for change to update habits, friendships, and thought patterns rather than shocking everyone around you.
cautionExamples: Do not present a new car, breakup, relocation, job exit, or sudden marriage as guaranteed from Uranus alone.
If the user feels urgent pressure to change everything, frame the urgency as information that needs pacing.
Name the difference between freedom and reactivity: freedom creates more agency; reactivity creates cleanup.

transitExamplesByHouse.1: Identity, body, style, and personal direction may feel ready for reinvention; unexpected incidents can force a new self-definition.
transitExamplesByHouse.2: Values, income, possessions, and security patterns may change; the person may need more financial independence or a less conventional resource strategy.
transitExamplesByHouse.3: Mental restlessness rises; new classes, skills, devices, writing, short trips, or sibling/neighborhood changes can become active.
transitExamplesByHouse.4: Home and family patterns get unsettled; repairs, moves, family disruptions, or a desire to change the living environment may surface.
transitExamplesByHouse.5: Romance, dating, creativity, hobbies, and children can become unpredictable; attraction to unusual people or unfamiliar pleasures may increase.
transitExamplesByHouse.6: Daily work, schedules, health habits, and service patterns need flexibility; freelancing, unusual hours, or sudden routine changes can appear.
transitExamplesByHouse.7: Close relationships ask for more room; fast attractions, sudden breaks, renegotiated commitments, or a less conventional partnership model can arise.
transitExamplesByHouse.8: Shared resources, debt, intimacy, trust, and dependency patterns shift; the person may need to stop relying on someone else financially or emotionally.
transitExamplesByHouse.9: Beliefs, travel, education, publishing, and cultural exposure open new doors; interest may spike quickly and need grounding to last.
transitExamplesByHouse.10: Career direction, reputation, and authority relationships can change suddenly; unusual work, public pivots, or self-directed ambition may call louder.
transitExamplesByHouse.11: Friendships, groups, networks, activism, and future plans change; the person may seek more unusual communities or detach from stale circles.
transitExamplesByHouse.12: Old habits, hidden anxieties, retreat, service, and unconscious patterns get interrupted; private liberation work matters before it becomes public.

prohibitions: Do not use Uranus as a traditional ruler in user-facing text.
Do not frame disruption as automatically liberating.
Do not predict divorce, job loss, relocation, or crisis from Uranus cycle alone.
weighting: Exact Uranus-to-Uranus contact is stronger than age estimate.
Angular Uranus or contacts to Sun, Moon, Ascendant, MC, Venus, Mars, or chart ruler increase relevance.
Repeated testimony from returns, progressions, profections, or transits is required before naming concrete events.
Use as modern lens context behind the scenes unless the app exposes modern life-cycle views.

chartRulers.tldr: Saturn rules the chart: a life steered by principle and detachment.
chartRulers.meaning: You move by system, ideals, and independence. The through-line is the group, the rule, and the reform.
chartRulers.modernLens: Traditional rulership names Saturn as Aquarius's ruler. Uranus is the modern lens: it adds themes of disruption, awakening, technology, rebellion, and sudden change, but it does not replace Saturn as the chart ruler.
chartRulers.business: Builds through structure aimed at change. Strong on systems and originality, weak on personal warmth.
chartRulers.readNext: Find this planet's sign, house, dignity, and aspects to see where and how well the life is steered.

chartRulers.tldr: Mars rules the chart: a life steered by drive and initiative.
chartRulers.meaning: You meet life head-on. The through-line is action, courage, and the fights you choose; you move first and lead.
chartRulers.business: Builds by initiating and pushing. Strongest when starting and leading, weakest when forced to wait.
chartRulers.readNext: Find this planet's sign, house, dignity, and aspects to see where and how well the life is steered.

chartRulers.tldr: The Moon rules the chart: a life steered by feeling and care.
chartRulers.meaning: You move by instinct and need, building security and belonging. The through-line is home, protection, and emotional tides.
chartRulers.business: Builds by nurturing and protecting. Strong on loyalty and timing, sensitive to mood and climate.
chartRulers.readNext: Find this planet's sign, house, dignity, and aspects to see where and how well the life is steered.

chartRulers.tldr: Saturn rules the chart: a life steered by structure and ambition.
chartRulers.meaning: You build slowly toward authority and mastery. The through-line is responsibility, the long climb, and earned standing.
chartRulers.business: Builds by disciplined, long-range effort. Strong on endurance, weak on speed and spontaneity.
chartRulers.readNext: Find this planet's sign, house, dignity, and aspects to see where and how well the life is steered.

chartRulers.tldr: Mercury rules the chart: a life steered by mind and exchange.
chartRulers.meaning: You navigate by curiosity, talk, and connection. The through-line is information, movement, and contact.
chartRulers.business: Builds by communicating and connecting. Strong on versatility, weak on staying with one thing.
chartRulers.readNext: Find this planet's sign, house, dignity, and aspects to see where and how well the life is steered.

chartRulers.tldr: The life steers toward the self.
chartRulers.meaning: Identity, body, and personal initiative are the main story. Self-driven and self-defining; the native is the project.
chartRulers.business: Work tends to be built around the person and their own brand or initiative.
chartRulers.advice: Put your energy where the chart ruler sits; this is the house your life is asking you to develop.

chartRulers.tldr: The life steers toward career and public standing.
chartRulers.meaning: Ambition, reputation, and visible achievement carry the life. The native is built to be seen and to lead.
chartRulers.business: Oriented to career, authority, and public reputation above all.

lunations.title: Full Moon in Aquarius
lunations.tldr: A culmination and release point for the Aquarius / Leo axis.
lunations.theme: This Full Moon illuminates future vision, community, individuation, innovation, and the courage to belong without disappearing through the Aquarius side of the axis, while the Sun in Leo asks for integration rather than extremes.
lunations.shadow: detachment disguised as enlightenment, rebellion without responsibility, or selling a version of yourself you do not believe in
lunations.integration: changing the system without abandoning your own aliveness

twoWeekArc.teaching: Your people want the real version, not the polished version built for approval.
twoWeekArc.appPrompt: Name what the last two weeks revealed. Release the pattern that blocks the Aquarius / Leo balance point.

sixMonthArc.appPrompt: Look back to the same-sign New Moon. What took root because you tended it, and what grew because the soil was left untended?

ritual.function: illumination, release, cleansing, integration, and completion
ritual.timing: Use after the exact Full Moon when possible. Keep eclipse lunations under the separate witness protocol, not ordinary release ritual.
