sections.heading: Elements
sections.body: Count how many planets are in each element. The dominant element shows how someone tends to navigate life. If one element is overemphasized and another is missing, the person may over-rely on one approach and need to bring in what is missing through environment, collaborators, or practices.

items.label: Fire Signs
items.body: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius. Fire emphasis indicates orientation toward initiative, creativity, and leadership. Strong fire tends to be energized by inspiring others, starting new projects, and taking independent action. Career applications often include entrepreneurship, entertainment, education, athletics, and fields where visibility and autonomous decision-making are valued.

items.label: Earth Signs
items.body: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn. Earth emphasis suggests practical approaches to goals and steady work habits. These individuals find satisfaction through tangible results and building useful things. Career applications often include business, healthcare, engineering, skilled trades, and fields with clear advancement paths and concrete outcomes.

items.label: Air Signs
items.body: Gemini, Libra, Aquarius. Air emphasis reveals mental agility and communication strengths. These people are energized by ideas, social connection, and problem-solving. Career applications often include writing, teaching, technology, law, consulting, and roles involving variety, intellectual stimulation, and human interaction.

items.label: Water Signs
items.body: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces. Water emphasis indicates emotional sensitivity and intuitive understanding. These individuals are drawn to helping others and creating emotional safety. Career applications often include counseling, healthcare, arts, spiritual work, and fields where empathy and emotional intelligence are valuable.

items.label: Element Imbalances
items.body: Earth-heavy charts might resist change. Fire-heavy charts may burn hot and fast. Air-dominant charts can feel ungrounded. Water-dominant charts may absorb too much from others.

sections.heading: Modes
sections.body: Count how many planets are in each mode. A lot of Cardinal may start projects but burn out. Too little Cardinal may struggle to begin. Fixed-heavy charts need consistency. Mutable-heavy charts need change and stimulation.

items.label: Cardinal Signs
items.body: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn. Cardinal emphasis suggests natural leadership abilities and comfort with starting projects. These individuals often thrive in roles where they can initiate new directions or take charge.

items.label: Fixed Signs
items.body: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius. Fixed emphasis indicates strength in sustaining effort and maintaining consistency. These people excel in roles requiring persistence, depth, and seeing projects through.

items.label: Mutable Signs
items.body: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces. Mutable emphasis reveals adaptability and learning orientation. These individuals often excel in teaching, consulting, or roles requiring flexibility and adjustment to changing circumstances.

sections.heading: Hemisphere and Quadrant Analysis
sections.body: Use house emphasis to identify orientation toward personal development, collective contribution, self-direction, or collaboration.

items.label: Northern Hemisphere
items.body: Houses 1-6. Emphasis suggests focus on personal development and individual achievement. Career satisfaction often comes through developing personal skills and expertise.

items.label: Southern Hemisphere
items.body: Houses 7-12. Emphasis indicates orientation toward social contribution and collective impact. Career fulfillment often involves serving others or contributing to larger social purposes.

items.label: Eastern Hemisphere
items.body: Houses 10-3. Emphasis suggests self-directed, initiating energy. These individuals often prefer to create their own opportunities rather than wait for others to provide them.

items.label: Western Hemisphere
items.body: Houses 4-9. Emphasis indicates others-oriented, responding energy. These people often work best in collaborative environments or in response to others' needs and initiatives.

sections.heading: Career Anchors
sections.body: Look at signs on the 10th, 6th, and 2nd house cusps and any planets inside for career themes.

items.label: 10th House / Midheaven
items.body: Represents how the world sees the person, how they want to be known professionally, and what kind of public impact they wish to make. The Midheaven sign and planets in the 10th reveal themes central to career expression.

items.label: 6th House
items.body: Shows natural work style, how the person prefers to serve others, and what daily routine supports productivity. The sign on the 6th cusp and planets here reveal ideal work environment.

items.label: 2nd House
items.body: Reveals relationship with money, material security, and values. Understanding the 2nd house helps align career choices with genuine values rather than paths that conflict with what is meaningful.

sections.heading: Sun, Moon, and Midheaven
sections.body: The Sun describes core identity and career satisfaction. The Moon describes emotional needs and productive work atmosphere. The Midheaven describes professional image and public role.

items.label: Fire Sun
items.body: Fire Suns typically display natural leadership and initiative. They find energy through creative projects and inspiring others. They need work that allows them to initiate rather than constantly respond to others' direction.

items.label: Earth Sun
items.body: Earth Suns demonstrate practical approaches to goals and steady work habits. They need practical results and tend to prefer stability over constant change.

items.label: Air Sun
items.body: Air Suns exhibit mental agility and communication strengths. They need mental challenge and social connection to feel engaged.

items.label: Water Sun
items.body: Water Suns show emotional sensitivity and intuitive understanding. They need work that feels personally meaningful rather than only financially rewarding.

items.label: Fire Moon
items.body: Needs excitement, autonomy, room for spontaneity, variety, and sometimes competitive elements. Rigid schedules or micromanagement can drain energy.

items.label: Earth Moon
items.body: Needs stability, clear expectations, practical outcomes, consistent schedules, and measurable progress. Chaotic environments can reduce productivity.

items.label: Air Moon
items.body: Needs intellectual stimulation, social interaction, collaborative environments, idea exchange, task variety, and freedom to communicate.

items.label: Water Moon
items.body: Needs emotional safety, meaningful connection, supportive atmospheres, and personally meaningful work. Harsh or competitive environments can be draining.

items.label: Fire Midheaven
items.body: Projects a public image as a dynamic leader or inspirational figure. Careers often involve innovation, creativity, teaching, or inspiring action.

items.label: Earth Midheaven
items.body: Projects a public image as a reliable expert or skilled professional. Careers often involve building, organizing, or practical services.

items.label: Air Midheaven
items.body: Projects a public image as communicator, connector, or advocate. Careers often involve ideas, networking, social causes, or facilitating understanding.

items.label: Water Midheaven
items.body: Projects a public image as nurturer, healer, or creative visionary. Careers often involve care, artistic expression, or emotional support.

sections.heading: North Node, Saturn, and Jupiter
sections.body: Use these placements to identify growth direction, mastery through challenge, and natural expansion.

items.label: North Node Cardinal
items.body: Learning to initiate and lead. Career growth often involves taking more responsibility and making independent decisions.

items.label: North Node Fixed
items.body: Learning to sustain effort and develop consistency. Career growth often involves deepening expertise and building lasting value.

items.label: North Node Mutable
items.body: Learning to adapt and teach others. Career growth often involves flexibility and sharing knowledge gained through experience.

items.label: Saturn
items.body: Represents consistent challenges that can become expertise and authority when worked through. The house placement shows where competence must be built through sustained effort.

items.label: Jupiter Fire
items.body: Finds meaning through inspiring others and expanding possibilities.

items.label: Jupiter Earth
items.body: Finds meaning through practical improvement and building useful things.

items.label: Jupiter Air
items.body: Finds meaning through sharing ideas and facilitating understanding.

items.label: Jupiter Water
items.body: Finds meaning through emotional healing and spiritual growth.

sections.heading: Common Career Patterns
sections.body: Use chart indicators to identify recurring vocational archetypes.

items.label: Executive Type
items.body: Indicators: strong Earth emphasis, planets in the 10th house, well-aspected Saturn, and often prominent Cardinal signs. Themes: management, business ownership, organizational structures, long-term planning, strategic implementation.

items.label: Helper Type
items.body: Indicators: strong Water emphasis, planets in the 6th or 12th houses, prominent Moon, and often Mutable signs. Themes: service, helping others navigate challenges, emotional needs, supportive assistance.

items.label: Communicator Type
items.body: Indicators: strong Air emphasis, prominent Mercury, planets in the 3rd or 9th houses, and often Mutable signs. Themes: sharing information, facilitating understanding, connecting perspectives.

items.label: Creator Type
items.body: Indicators: strong Fire emphasis, planets in the 5th house, prominent Sun or Leo energy, and often Fixed signs. Themes: creative expression, inspiration, innovation, motivating others.

items.label: Innovator Type
items.body: Indicators: prominent Uranus, strong Aquarius emphasis, planets in the 11th house, and often Air emphasis. Themes: cutting-edge fields, social reform, collective problem-solving, future possibilities.

sections.heading: Timing and Life Phases
sections.body: Use major cycles to contextualize career and life transitions.

items.label: Saturn Return
items.body: Ages 29-30 and 58-60. Major life restructuring. The first often involves choosing a serious career direction; the second may involve legacy and sharing wisdom.

items.label: Jupiter Return
items.body: Every 12 years. Brings opportunities for growth and expansion in the life area Jupiter occupies.

items.label: Uranus Transits
items.body: Every 7 years to different chart areas. When Uranus transits career houses such as the 6th or 10th, sudden changes, technological innovations, or breakthroughs may free limiting professional circumstances.

items.label: North Node Return
items.body: Every 18-19 years. Offers opportunities to align more closely with growth direction and integrate lessons.

sections.heading: What You'll Need
sections.body: Use exact birth date, time, and location. Use a free chart calculator such as mariesatori.com or astro.com. Keep a notebook for tracking insights.

sections.heading: Birth Time Accuracy Matters
sections.body: Even 4 minutes off can change your Rising sign. 2 hours off can shift house placements entirely. If unsure of time, request an official birth certificate from vital records.

sections.heading: If You Don't Have Birth Time
sections.body: Use a noon chart for planetary signs only. Avoid house-based interpretations. Focus on Sun, Moon, and planetary sign placements.

sections.heading: Secondary Layer
sections.body: Asteroids are a secondary synastry layer. They should never override the core relationship structure shown by natal capacity, Sun, Moon, Ascendant, Venus, Mars, Saturn, angles, house overlays, and the composite chart.

sections.heading: Use Tight Orbs
sections.body: Use tight orbs for asteroid contacts. Prioritize exact or near-exact conjunctions to personal planets, angles, nodes, or composite points. Treat wide asteroid contacts as symbolic background, not as primary evidence.

sections.heading: Asteroid Roles
sections.body: Asteroids can clarify a specific theme: commitment, longing, erotic charge, devotion, injury, repair, muse-like inspiration, or mythic patterning. They are best used to name nuance after the main relationship dynamics are already established.

sections.heading: Karmic Language Boundary
sections.body: Avoid deterministic language such as soul debt, required suffering, or proof of a past-life bond. If nodal, Saturn, Vertex, Chiron, or asteroid contacts feel consequential, phrase them as intensity, recognition, unfinished emotional pattern, or developmental pressure rather than proof that the relationship must continue.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Never use asteroid or karmic indicators to justify harm, obsession, coercion, or staying in a damaging relationship. If a contact describes pain, compulsion, or fixation, name the pattern and direct attention back to consent, boundaries, behavior, and support.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: Astrocartography projects the natal chart onto a world map. Each planet forms lines showing where it was angular at birth. Near a line, that planet's symbolism tends to be louder in the person's experience of that place.

sections.heading: Four Angles
sections.body: The Ascendant line emphasizes identity, body, vitality, and how the person shows up. The Midheaven line emphasizes career, public role, visibility, and reputation. The Descendant line emphasizes relationships, projection, and the people the person meets. The IC line emphasizes home, roots, privacy, family, and emotional foundation.

sections.heading: Proximity
sections.body: Effects are strongest close to the line and more diffuse with distance. Where two lines cross or closely overlap, both planets should be considered active. The app should compute distance and line intersections separately from this interpretive file.

sections.heading: Non-Deterministic Policy
sections.body: A line describes what a location may amplify; it does not guarantee events or define a fixed outcome. Heavier lines such as Mars, Saturn, Neptune, or Pluto should not be framed as places to avoid. They should be described as places that ask more of the person in a specific way.

sections.heading: App Policy
sections.body: Keep astrocartography behind a later optional feature. Do not surface this in the main chart, daily transits, synastry, or timing engine until map calculation and rendering are implemented. When released, require exact birth date, time, and location, and label the result as locational astrology.

sections.heading: Line Meanings
sections.body: Use these as short interpretive anchors for planet-angle combinations. The voice layer may expand or soften them later.

items.label: Sun Ascendant
items.body: Visibility, vitality, confidence, and self-expression are amplified. Strong for being seen and leading. Watch for inflated ego.

items.label: Sun Midheaven
items.body: Career, reputation, leadership, and recognition are emphasized. Strong for public visibility. Watch for tying identity too tightly to status.

items.label: Sun Descendant
items.body: Relationships bring visibility and may revolve around prominent or confident people. Watch for outshining or being outshone.

items.label: Sun IC
items.body: Home, roots, and belonging become central. Strong for building a base that feels personally affirming. Watch for making home the whole world.

items.label: Moon Ascendant
items.body: Feelings sit close to the surface, and people read the person more easily. Strong for familiarity and intuition. Watch for moods steering the day.

items.label: Moon Midheaven
items.body: Emotional life and public life intertwine. The person may be known for care, nurture, responsiveness, or feeling. Watch for managing emotions for appearances.

items.label: Moon Descendant
items.body: Relationships feel nurturing, familiar, and emotionally important. Strong for family-style bonds. Watch for dependency.

items.label: Moon IC

sections.heading: Scope And Safety
sections.body: Body astrology is a symbolic correspondence layer only. It is not health advice, not nutritional advice, not a remedy system, and not a way to identify or explain body concerns. Always use 'traditionally associated with' for the seven visible planets and sign correspondences, and 'modern overlay associated with' for Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto. For any body or health concern, direct the user to a licensed professional.

sections.heading: Excluded By Design
sections.body: Do not include supplement, vitamin, herb, flower essence, tea, diet, remedy, or protocol tables in the app. The knowledge base may store symbolic body correspondences, but it must not give instructions about what a user should consume, avoid, apply, or do for a body concern.

sections.heading: App Policy
sections.body: If shown in the app, label this as a symbolic body-correspondence layer. Do not display it in a way that implies a chart can determine, predict, or explain a person's health. Keep it separate from transit alerts, personal recommendations, and any feature that could be mistaken for care guidance.

sections.heading: Archetype
sections.body: Chiron describes a tender, old hurt and the wisdom that can develop around it. It points to an area where a person may feel different, inadequate, exposed, or unusually sensitive, and where honest integration can become a source of compassion, guidance, and skill.

sections.heading: Framing Rule
sections.body: Always pair the wound with the healing path. Never frame the person as broken, doomed, defective, or permanently defined by the wound. Chiron describes sensitivity and integration work, not a fixed outcome.

sections.heading: Houses Versus Signs
sections.body: Chiron by house is usually more personally specific because it shows where the wound gets lived: identity, money, voice, home, creativity, work, partnership, intimacy, meaning, public role, community, or hidden life. Chiron by sign is useful, but often more generational because Chiron spends uneven years in a sign. Weight sign text up when Chiron closely aspects a personal planet or angle.

sections.heading: Modern Point Policy
sections.body: Chiron is a modern point and should be secondary in weighting. Do not use it for dignity, sect, traditional rulership, time-lord logic, or primary chart-ruler logic. It becomes more important when it sits on an angle, aspects the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, or chart angles, or repeats a theme already shown elsewhere in the chart.

sections.heading: Symbolic Safety
sections.body: Chiron placements are descriptive and non-deterministic. Health-house or body-related placements must be emotional and symbolic only, never medical. Do not use Chiron to diagnose, explain symptoms, suggest treatment, or tell a user what will happen to their body.

sections.heading: Optional Evolutionary Lens
sections.body: Some users read Chiron through an evolutionary or past-life lens: an old wound carried into this life, with this lifetime offering a chance to face and integrate the pattern. Present this only as an optional interpretive lens, never as literal fact. It can be useful even when the user treats it metaphorically.

sections.heading: Evolutionary House Themes
sections.body: If the optional lens is enabled, keep the themes brief and belief-neutral. The 1st house suggests selfhood once denied; the 2nd, lack or worth; the 3rd, a silenced voice; the 4th, unsafe roots; the 5th, punished expression or love; the 6th, over-service or bodily hardship as symbolic material; the 7th, partnership betrayal or loss; the 8th, power, violation, trust, or loss; the 9th, broken faith or persecuted belief; the 10th, public shame or legitimacy; the 11th, exile from a group; the 12th, hidden or inherited sorrow. Do not present these as facts, memories, or proof.

sections.heading: App Display
sections.body: Show Chiron in an optional shadow and healing layer, with callouts when it touches personal planets or angles. Keep the language practical: what hurts, what pattern forms around it, what integration asks for, and what the person can offer others once the pattern is owned. Keep past-life or evolutionary framing behind an explicit optional lens.

sections.heading: Principle
sections.body: Synastry shows the attraction and friction between two individuals; the composite shows what the third thing they create is like to be inside. Always read both.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body: Use these as synthesis patterns, not verdicts.

items.label: Example 1
items.body: Easy synastry, hard composite: instant Venus-Mars chemistry between them, but a composite Moon square Saturn. Read it as: the attraction is real and personal, yet the relationship itself runs heavy and reserved. Chemistry is not the same as an easy relationship.

items.label: Example 2
items.body: Hard synastry, supportive composite: their Mars-Saturn synastry is full of friction, but the composite has Sun in the 7th and a Venus trine. Read it as: they rub each other the wrong way personally, yet the bond they build is steady and partnership-oriented. Worth the friction.

items.label: Example 3
items.body: Doubled theme: Pluto-heavy synastry and a Pluto-charged composite. Intensity and transformation define both the attraction and the relationship itself; the theme is unavoidable. Take it seriously and watch for control on both levels.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: Developmental age mapping is an optional lens that maps a life arc onto the natal chart so chart positions correspond to broad life periods. Treat it as a standalone interpretive method, not as a universal rule and not as the same thing as transits, progressions, returns, or time-lord timing.

sections.heading: Separate From Transits
sections.body: Do not merge this framework into daily check-ins, transit-to-natal lookup, current-sky transit work, synastry, or composite readings. Transits read current sky against the natal chart. This framework reads a fixed developmental map through the natal chart. They are different engines and should stay separate.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.body: The whole life arc, beginning before birth and continuing through later life, is mapped through the twelve houses on a compressed developmental scale. Early life receives more interpretive space, while later life compresses. The house gives the life period, the sign gives the quality of that period, and planets in the house describe catalytic people, pressures, or events associated with that age band.

sections.heading: Method Rules
sections.body: Use this only as conceptual guidance unless the app has a properly implemented calculator for the method. The Ascendant marks birth and the birth environment. The sign in a house sets the tone for that developmental period. Planets in a house intensify and complicate the period. More planets in a house can indicate a more eventful or layered period. Planetary symbolism can describe people present around that time, but should not be treated as literal certainty.

sections.heading: Octaves
sections.body: The framework can be organized into four broad octaves: gestation, childhood, maturity, and a transpersonal later-life octave. Gestation describes prenatal and inherited conditions. Childhood describes early development, family, learning, play, and rules. Maturity describes adult partnership, work, building, and social role. The transpersonal octave describes later-life consciousness beyond purely personal milestones.

sections.heading: Illustrative Anchors
sections.body: Illustrative anchors may be used only to explain the principle, not as a full timing table. Example: an early-life sign quality may be read around infancy, while a house associated with work, routine, learning, and bodily maintenance may describe adolescence into early adulthood. Do not publish exact age tables from these notes.

sections.heading: Calculator Warning
sections.body: Do not implement an age-map calculator from this framework alone. The precise age-to-house formula, tables, and calculation rules belong to the underlying method and are not reproduced here. If the app ever supports this feature, it needs a separate implementation task with verified calculation rules.

sections.heading: App Policy
sections.body: If surfaced, present this as an optional developmental reading, clearly separate from transits and current timing. Keep it non-deterministic: describe themes, developmental periods, and reflective questions. Do not claim one exact event must have happened at a given age, and do not use it for medical, legal, financial, or safety claims.

frameworks.title: Fixed Star And Lunar Mansion Framework

sections.heading: Stars Versus Planets
sections.body: Fixed stars should not be treated like fast-moving transits. Planets describe changing conditions because they move visibly through speed, brightness, station, retrograde, and aspect. Fixed stars are comparatively stable and work more like enduring points of potency, identity, and lineage. Use them as intensifiers and signature markers, not as ordinary daily-event triggers.

sections.heading: Stellar Timing
sections.body: The core timing rule for fixed-star work is the Moon conjoining the star while the star-Moon contact is elevated, ideally culminating or near the highest point in the local sky. A secondary timing layer is the star's own local cycle: heliacal rising, culmination, and setting. These moments are location-dependent and drift slowly through precession, so a fixed-star calendar must be calculated for the user's place and date rather than hard-coded globally.

sections.heading: Moon As Mediator
sections.body: The Moon is the primary carrier of stellar light into lived experience. For fixed-star timing, inspect the Moon's condition before using the star contact: phase, dignity, sect context, applying aspects, separation from malefics, void-of-course status, and angularity. A strong star contact carried by a damaged Moon should be down-weighted or treated as unstable.

sections.heading: Star Identity
sections.body: Do not reduce a star to a single keyword. A useful fixed-star profile should include visual quality, constellation placement, nearby sky figures, yearly visibility cycle, major cultural names or myths with attribution, and associated planetary tones. The star's associated planets approximate its flavor; they do not replace the star's own identity.

sections.heading: Lunar Mansions
sections.body: Lunar mansions divide the Moon's path into daily segments and are a bridge between lunar timing and stellar material. Use them as a timing and symbolic layer, especially for lunar electional work. Keep a caveat: tropical mansion positions can drift away from the actual stars they originally described, so any star-specific work should prefer direct Moon-star contact over mansion label alone.

sections.heading: Correspondence Use
sections.body: Traditional fixed-star lore often assigns stones, herbs, images, or sigils to major stars. Store those correspondences as optional support data when authored, but do not let correspondences stand in for interpretation. In the apps, fixed-star correspondences should support ritual or reflection features only after the astronomical contact and Moon condition are known.

sections.heading: Arc Doctrine
sections.body: Every New Moon plants seeds revealed six months later at the same-sign Full Moon. Track both the two-week immediate arc and the six-month maturation arc. Always name both.

sections.heading: Complete Axis Themes
sections.body: Use axis work to name shared themes, differences, shadows, integration point, and Full Moon opportunity.

items.label: Aries / Libra
items.body: Self vs. Others. Core tension: independence vs. partnership. Integration question: Can you stand fully in yourself while still making room for someone else? Shadow work includes times you kept the peace but lost yourself, or pushed people away in the name of independence.

items.label: Taurus / Scorpio
items.body: Security vs. Transformation. Core tension: stability vs. change. Integration question: Can you create stability in your life that also leaves room for change? Shadow work includes staying too long because it felt safe, or blowing everything up because stability felt suffocating.

items.label: Gemini / Sagittarius
items.body: Information vs. Wisdom. Core tension: details vs. big picture. Integration question: Can you stay curious without getting lost in details, and share insights without oversimplifying them? Shadow work includes avoiding decisions by asking endless questions, or clinging to a belief so tightly you stopped listening.

items.label: Cancer / Capricorn
items.body: Nurturing vs. Achievement. Core tension: emotional safety vs. public success. Integration question: Can you build success without sacrificing the people and peace that matter most, and care for home life without retreating from the world? Shadow work includes avoiding challenges in the name of self-care, or pursuing success at the expense of well-being.

items.label: Leo / Aquarius
items.body: Personal expression vs. collective good. Core tension: standing out vs. belonging. Integration question: Can you shine without making it all about you, and contribute to the group without disappearing in the crowd? Shadow work includes shaping yourself to be accepted, or withdrawing to prove you do not need anyone.

items.label: Virgo / Pisces
items.body: Precision vs. Flow. Core tension: control vs. surrender. Integration question: Can you give your all without losing yourself, and loosen your grip without letting go of the vision? Shadow work includes fixating on details to avoid uncertainty, or drifting into fantasy to avoid reality.

sections.heading: Double New Moon System
sections.body: When two New Moons occur in the same sign about 29.5 days apart, the lesson is emphasized as non-negotiable. First New Moon at 0-3 degrees: this is the first of two New Moons and a chance to go deeper. Second New Moon at 27-29 degrees: review what began four weeks ago and see how the attempt can grow into a higher expression or slip into shadow.

sections.heading: Eclipse Protocol
sections.body: Eclipse Witness: Stop. Put down candles, crystals, and kameas. If something must be done, light one white candle. Journal what is actually moving through you: what is ending, changing, or being removed. Eclipses take what is expired and give what is needed. The most powerful magick is knowing when not to interfere.

sections.heading: Major Aspect Patterns
sections.body: Use these patterns when writing major planetary aspects.

items.label: Conjunction
items.body: 0 degrees. Planet 1 meets Planet 2 in a sign. This is fusion: one planet's quality merges with the other's quality, creating something neither could achieve alone.

items.label: Square
items.body: 90 degrees. Planet 1 in Sign 1 squares Planet 2 in Sign 2. The tension shows competing approaches. Neither is wrong; both are necessary. The friction creates breakthrough through a third way.

items.label: Opposition
items.body: 180 degrees. Planet 1 opposes Planet 2. The person is pulled between two qualities. This is not about choosing sides; it is about finding the bridge and holding both.

items.label: Trine
items.body: 120 degrees. Planet 1 in Sign 1 trines Planet 2 in Sign 2. When signs align by element, quality flows with less effort. Notice what feels easier and do not overthink the gift.

sections.heading: Retrograde Daily Guidance Framework
sections.body: Use daily guidance to identify the pattern becoming visible, not to force action.

items.label: Mercury Retrograde
items.body: 21-24 days. Focus on communication patterns, mental loops, technology issues, travel delays, and unfinished conversations returning. Notice where communication patterns have been operating on autopilot.

items.label: Venus Retrograde
items.body: 40-43 days. Focus on worth patterns, relationship dynamics, financial decisions, beauty ideals, and self-care versus indulgence. Notice where undervaluing yourself or compromising too quickly shapes connection, spending, creation, and care.

items.label: Mars Retrograde
items.body: 58-81 days. Focus on anger patterns, energy management, action versus reaction, boundaries, and initiative versus force. Let anger be messenger, not driver.

sections.heading: Ritual Scope
sections.body: Electional and magick timing may be used for New Moon and Full Moon ritual support. Keep it out of ordinary daily guidance unless the user explicitly enters a ritual feature. The ritual layer should support reflection, intention, release, altar setup, journaling, tarot, and spiritual bath preparation.

sections.heading: New Moon Function
sections.body: New Moon ritual work emphasizes attraction, initiation, seed-setting, and calling in aligned change. Favor language of beginning, inviting, clarifying desire, preparing the space, and committing to small actions that can grow over the lunar cycle.

sections.heading: Full Moon Function
sections.body: Full Moon ritual work emphasizes illumination, culmination, release, cleansing, uncrossing, and integration. Favor language of seeing clearly, naming what has peaked, releasing what is complete, and restoring protection or steadiness after the release.

sections.heading: Six Month Altar Arc
sections.body: A New Moon can begin a six-month altar or intention arc that matures at the same-sign Full Moon. The app may help the user name the life house activated, choose a focus, track progress, and revisit the intention at the two-week Full Moon and six-month same-sign Full Moon.

sections.heading: Preparation Steps
sections.body: Ritual preparation should include cleansing the space, cleansing or bathing the body when appropriate, setting a clear intention or release statement, selecting a candle or simple object, creating a dedicated altar surface, journaling before and after, and closing the ritual cleanly.

sections.heading: Directional Actions
sections.body: Use clockwise motion for attraction, calling in, blessing, and building. Use counter-clockwise motion for release, clearing, uncrossing, and removing stagnant energy. Keep substitutions simple: a white candle, water, paper, and a quiet space are enough when the user lacks ritual materials.

sections.heading: Eclipse Exception
sections.body: Eclipses are not ordinary New or Full Moons. Do not recommend intention-setting or elaborate ritual during an eclipse. Use witness practice instead: one white candle if needed, journaling what is moving, grounding, and letting the eclipse reveal what is ending or changing.

sections.heading: Ethics And Accessibility
sections.body: Ritual guidance must remain non-coercive, non-medical, and accessible. Do not imply that materials are mandatory or that a ritual controls another person. Offer simple substitutions, safety reminders for candles and baths, and a clear statement that ritual supports intention and reflection rather than guarantees outcomes.

sections.heading: Principle
sections.body: Synthesis over enumeration. Instead of listing placements, name the two or three patterns the chart keeps producing. A through-line is only real when the chart says it more than one way; a single placement is a detail, not a pattern.

sections.heading: Philosophy
sections.body: Anchored to the house stance (see stance_chart_story.json): the chart speaks clearly about the shape of the story, less clearly about the choices made within it, least clearly about the exact scenes. Name the shape; hold the choices open; never predict the scene.

sections.heading: Factor Weights
sections.body: Proposed, tunable. Mirrors the transit_significance scoring idea, applied to the natal chart to find what carries the most weight.

items.label: dignityModifier
items.body: multiply a factor up for domicile/exaltation, down for detriment/fall.

sections.heading: Repetition Rule
sections.body: A through-line must be echoed by at least two independent signatures (for example a sign emphasis AND a house emphasis AND/OR an aspect). This is the guardrail against over-reading one placement, the same logic as 'a synastry bond needs multiple indicators' and the generational-vs-personal stellium check.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Use this order to turn many natal factors into two or three through-lines.

items.label: Step 1
items.body: Score every chart factor for emphasis using the weights above.

items.label: Step 2
items.body: Group the high-weight factors by shared theme (element, principle, life-area, or keyword).

items.label: Step 3
items.body: Keep only themes the chart states two or more ways; these are the through-lines.

items.label: Step 4
items.body: Name each plainly, in the second person, as a tendency.

items.label: Step 5
items.body: Pair each with its choice point so it reads as a pattern you can work with, not a verdict.

sections.heading: Output Shape
sections.body: Through-lines: 2 to 3 maximum. Each through-line should include a name, what it is, evidence, and a choice point.

items.label: name
items.body: a plain-language pattern, e.g. 'you keep depth and distance in the same hand'

items.label: whatItIs
items.body: the felt tendency in one or two sentences

items.label: evidence
items.body: the placements that say it (the repetition that makes it real)

items.label: choicePoint
items.body: the agency: what is learned and changeable here, and the decision it leaves you

sections.heading: Honesty Rules
sections.body: Keep natal synthesis descriptive and agency-forward.

items.label: shape_clear
items.body: State the pattern with confidence; this is what a chart can show.

items.label: choices_held_open
items.body: Always frame as a tendency plus a choice, never a fixed outcome.

items.label: scenes_not_predicted
items.body: Never name specific future events; the chart does not speak clearly there.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body: Use these as pattern examples, not fixed scripts.

items.label: Example 1
items.body: Depth through-line: a Scorpio Sun, an 8th-house stellium, and Moon square Pluto all say the same thing three ways. You go deep and don't do surface; intimacy is high-stakes. The shape is real; the choice is whether depth becomes connection or control.

items.label: Example 2
items.body: Freedom-versus-security through-line: Moon in Cancer (needs roots) opposed by Uranus (needs escape), with Aquarius rising. You're pulled between belonging and breaking free. The tension is built in; the work is holding both, not picking one.

items.label: Example 3
items.body: Visibility through-line: Sun conjunct the Midheaven, a Leo emphasis, and a 10th-house stellium. You're built to be seen and to lead. The drive is real; the choice is whether you lead for recognition or for the work.

sections.heading: Integration
sections.body: Pulls evidence from planet_in_sign, planet_in_house, the aspect corpora, stelliums, chiron, nodal, and lilith; scores with the transit_significance approach; frames with stance_chart_story. It is the layer that turns the data into two or three things worth saying.

sections.heading: Return Definition
sections.body: A planetary return occurs when a transiting planet returns to its natal position. Treat the return chart as a cycle map for that planet's topics: closure of one cycle, beginning of the next, and a concentrated preview of how that planet will operate until the next return.

sections.heading: Planet-Specific Scope
sections.body: Each return speaks through its planet. Solar returns emphasize vitality, identity, visibility, and annual direction. Lunar returns emphasize emotional climate and monthly movement. Mercury returns emphasize decisions, communication, study, commerce, travel, and logistics. Venus returns emphasize love, money, pleasure, aesthetics, and social ease. Mars returns emphasize action, conflict, stamina, risk, enterprise, and the body. Jupiter and Saturn returns describe larger multi-year developmental arcs.

sections.heading: Read Like A Chart
sections.body: Read the return chart as a chart, but keep the return planet central. Prioritize the return Ascendant, angular planets, the return planet's house and aspects, house rulers, repeated natal themes, and close contacts to natal planets or angles.

sections.heading: Timing With Transits
sections.body: The return chart describes the cycle; later transits to the return chart can time when its promises become active. This is especially useful for solar, lunar, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn return cycles.

sections.heading: Retrograde Return Series
sections.body: Retrograde planets can create more than one return in a short span. Treat a three-pass return as a sequence: first contact introduces the cycle issue, retrograde contact reviews or reverses it, final direct contact commits the outcome or direction.

sections.heading: Do Not Overpromise
sections.body: A return chart does not guarantee a single event. It gives a cycle field. Raise confidence only when the return chart repeats natal promise, progression, active transit, or time-lord testimony.

sections.heading: Solar Return Big Year Signals
sections.body: A Solar Return is more likely to describe a visible year when its Ascendant is close to a natal angle, when the Lord of the Year is prominent in the return, when return angles contact natal planets, or when the same planet and house topic repeat across natal chart, profection, return, and current transits.

sections.heading: Solar Return Plus Profection
sections.body: For annual work, start with the profection and Lord of the Year, then read the Solar Return through that lens. The return chart may be read as its own chart, but the Lord of the Year, profected sign, and activated natal planets determine which parts of the return deserve the most weight.

sections.heading: Necessity Before Perfect Timing
sections.body: Electional timing is a weighting layer, not a reason to sabotage practical life. If a real-world opportunity has a deadline, choose the best workable moment inside the available window rather than waiting for an ideal chart that arrives too late. The app should never advise delaying urgent health, legal, safety, financial, or career action solely because the astrology is imperfect.

sections.heading: Mundane Factors First
sections.body: Astrological support must be weighed against ordinary conditions: preparedness, skill, timing in the human calendar, social context, access, money, safety, and the actual requirements of the task. A strong election cannot compensate for avoidable neglect of the non-astrological work.

sections.heading: Direct Current Rule
sections.body: The more directly a working calls on a planet, star, lunar mansion, planetary hour, or talismanic image, the more strongly the astronomical condition matters. A general reflective practice may tolerate rougher sky weather. A planetary talisman, planetary petition, or star-specific ritual should require tighter electional standards.

sections.heading: Minimum Electional Checks
sections.body: For any elected moment, check the Moon first, then the significator. Avoid a severely afflicted or void-of-course Moon for beginnings. Prefer the significator dignified, direct, visible, angular or succedent, unafflicted by the out-of-sect malefic, and supported by benefic testimony or reception. Place malefics away from the angles when the goal is constructive or protective.

sections.heading: Mitigation
sections.body: When timing is imperfect but action cannot wait, mitigate rather than pretend the chart is clean. Choose the least damaged window available, strengthen the relevant planet through dignity or planetary day/hour where possible, use benefic support, avoid direct contact with the harshest testimony, and keep the practical action modest, specific, and well-prepared.

sections.heading: Ethical Boundary
sections.body: Electional and ritual guidance must not encourage coercion, harm, dependency, medical avoidance, legal avoidance, or unsafe delay. For consumer apps, phrase electional guidance as supportive timing and reflective practice, not as a guarantee of control over another person or outcome.

sections.heading: Natal Promise First
sections.body: Do not read a transit or progression as creating a life theme from nothing. Start with the natal chart: planet condition, house topics, rulership, aspects, angularity, sect, dignity, and repeated chart patterns. The timing technique activates what the natal chart can already describe.

sections.heading: Progressions Show Current Potential
sections.body: Secondary progressions describe the chapter currently developing from the natal chart. They are slower, more interior, and better for reading the background plot of a life phase. Progressed-to-natal and progressed-to-progressed contacts show the themes that are ready to be lived now.

sections.heading: Transits Trigger The Theme
sections.body: Transits are the timing pressure that can bring a progressed or natal theme into lived focus. A transit is louder when it repeats the same planetary pair, house topic, or life area already active by progression, return chart, profection, or natal promise.

sections.heading: Three Indicator Rule
sections.body: One indicator is not enough for a major event. Require multiple testimonies pointing in the same direction before the app treats a theme as high confidence. Useful agreement can come from natal promise, active progression, transit trigger, return chart emphasis, activated house ruler, angular planet, or repeated planetary pair.

sections.heading: Exactness And Orb
sections.body: The closer an aspect is to exact, the louder it is. Applying contacts build the trend; exact contacts peak it; separating contacts describe aftermath and integration. A wider contact can still manifest if another active planet triggers the same configuration or midpoint.

sections.heading: Priority Stack
sections.body: Prioritize angles, Sun, Moon, chart ruler, sect light, activated time lord, and planets already prominent in the natal chart. A planet is more prominent when angular, elevated, part of a stellium, heavily aspected, ruling an activated house, or repeating a current progressed or transit theme.

sections.heading: House Rulers Matter
sections.body: When a house ruler becomes active by progression, return, or transit, the house topics it rules become part of the story. For relationship timing, watch the 7th ruler along with Venus, Moon, Mercury, and relationship houses. For career timing, watch the 10th ruler along with Sun, Jupiter, Saturn, and public houses.

sections.heading: User-Facing Translation
sections.body: The app should not expose the full machinery unless the user asks for it. Translate agreement between techniques as plain confidence language: a background theme is active, a trigger is pressing it now, and the user's choices decide how consciously it is handled.

sections.heading: Events And Psychology Both Count
sections.body: A transit can describe an external event, an inner psychological shift, or both. The app should not force a false split between circumstances and inner process. Translate this as: the life area is activated, the pressure is real, and the visible form depends on context and choices.

sections.heading: Annual Context Before Daily Trigger
sections.body: Rank daily transits inside the yearly field. A transit is louder when it touches the Lord of the Year, the profected sign, a Solar Return angle, an angular natal planet, or a topic repeated by the Solar Return. A technically exact transit with no annual support should usually read as background.

sections.heading: Cycle Stage Language
sections.body: Read repeated contacts as a cycle: conjunction begins or fuses the topic, waxing square tests it, opposition brings culmination or confrontation, waning square forces revision, and the next conjunction resets the storyline. This helps avoid treating every exact hit as isolated.

sections.heading: Easy And Hard Transits
sections.body: Easy transits often require voluntary action or they pass quietly. Hard transits expose weak points, pressure stuck patterns, and force decisions where avoidance has built up. Do not call easy transits guaranteed blessings or hard transits guaranteed harm.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Use this as a question-led entry point for relationship readings. It maps common client concerns such as communication, conflict, affection, silence, withdrawal, stress, and support to the chart signatures that can explain the pattern. It complements bond-type and composite work by answering how the relationship functions in daily life.

sections.heading: Ethics
sections.body: Keep the reading agency-forward. The chart explains a tendency, not a verdict on the person. Silence and withdrawal should be read constructively and with nuance, never pathologized. Do not romanticize control, coercion, contempt, or repeated harm. This framework reads coping and support style, not mental health. It is not diagnostic, and style-matching is not a substitute for real support or professional help when someone is struggling.

sections.heading: Communication
sections.body: For questions like why the people do not understand each other or why talking goes wrong, read each person's Mercury by sign, element, and aspects; Mercury-to-Mercury contacts; Mercury-Saturn; Mercury-Mars; Mercury-Neptune; and 3rd-house overlays. Name the style difference as a mismatch to manage, not a fault.

items.label: Fire Mercury
items.body: Direct, fast, blunt, and enthusiastic. Says it as it comes, sometimes before thinking. Needs room to be direct without every direct statement being read as aggression.

items.label: Earth Mercury
items.body: Practical, concrete, measured, and specific. Slow to speak, means what is said, and wants useful conversation. Needs patience and clear examples.

items.label: Air Mercury
items.body: Verbal, social, idea-driven, and curious. Processes by talking, comparing, and debating. Can over-talk feelings and needs mental engagement.

items.label: Water Mercury
items.body: Emotional, intuitive, indirect, and tone-sensitive. Communicates through feeling as much as words. May hint or go quiet rather than state needs plainly, and needs emotional safety to open.

items.label: Mercury-Mercury
items.body: Harmonious contacts can show easy conversation and similar mental rhythm. Hard contacts can show different wavelengths, talking past each other, or needing translation before either person feels understood.

items.label: Mercury-Saturn
items.body: Saturn can sound critical, withholding, or shutting down, while Mercury may feel unheard or belittled. At its best, this contact supports serious listening and precise language.

items.label: Mercury-Mars
items.body: Stimulating, sharp, and fast. Conversation can become argument quickly. Useful for honesty and momentum, difficult when either person uses words as weapons.

items.label: Mercury-Neptune
items.body: Intuitive, gentle, imaginative, or confusing. People may hear what they hope was said instead of what was actually said, so clarity needs to be checked directly.

sections.heading: Conflict
sections.body: For repeating fights, read each person's Mars by sign, element, and aspects; Mars-to-Mars contacts; Mars-Mercury; Mars-Saturn; Mars-Pluto; and the hard aspects between the charts. Many recurring fights are style clashes rather than bad faith, but charts should never be used to excuse cruelty.

items.label: Fire Mars
items.body: Fights hot and fast: direct, loud, immediate, and often over quickly. Can intimidate cooler or slower conflict styles.

items.label: Earth Mars
items.body: Fights slowly and stubbornly: digs in, holds the position, and may resist moving until there is a practical reason. Watch stonewalling and grudges.

items.label: Air Mars
items.body: Fights through words, logic, and argument. Can detach, rationalize, or focus on winning the point while missing the emotional cost.

items.label: Water Mars
items.body: Fights indirectly or protectively: withdraws, goes quiet, absorbs hurt, or lets conflict move underground. Watch unspoken resentment and passive resistance.

items.label: Mars-Mars
items.body: Harmonious contacts can show compatible energy and conflict rhythm. Hard contacts can show friction, competition, impatience, and clashes of will.

items.label: Mars-Saturn
items.body: One person's drive meets the other's restraint, control, caution, or fear. This can build discipline, but it can also feel like constant blockage or suppression.

items.label: Mars-Pluto
items.body: Intense, magnetic, and forceful. Can show deep drive and transformation, but it must be watched for power struggles, control battles, or escalation.

sections.heading: Affection
sections.body: For questions about how someone shows love or why someone does not feel loved, read Venus for how love is offered, the Moon for what is needed to feel emotionally safe, and Mars for pursuit and desire. A Venus-Moon mismatch can create the feeling of being unloved even when affection is present.

items.label: Fire Venus
items.body: Shows love through pursuit, passion, enthusiasm, play, and bold gestures. Needs aliveness and visible desire.

items.label: Earth Venus
items.body: Shows love through reliability, touch, care, consistency, and practical support. Needs steadiness and embodied proof.

items.label: Air Venus
items.body: Shows love through words, wit, social connection, shared ideas, and playful exchange. Needs conversation and mental rapport.

items.label: Water Venus
items.body: Shows love through emotional attunement, nurturing, protection, devotion, and deep feeling. Needs safety and tenderness.

items.label: Venus-Moon
items.body: One person's way of loving meets, misses, or complicates the other's emotional needs. This is one of the clearest signatures for whether affection feels received.

items.label: Venus-Venus
items.body: Shows shared values, taste, affection style, and ease around pleasure. Hard contacts can still attract, but the people may want different expressions of love.

items.label: Venus-Mars
items.body: Shows chemistry, pursuit, desire, and attraction. Important for spark, but chemistry should not be treated as compatibility by itself.

items.label: Venus-Saturn
items.body: Love may be shown through commitment, duty, loyalty, or endurance rather than warmth. This can be stabilizing, but it can also feel withheld.

sections.heading: Silence And Avoidance
sections.body: For questions about silence or withdrawal, read Saturn contacts, especially Moon-Saturn and Mercury-Saturn; water Moon or Mars; fixed signs; 12th-house overlays; Neptune contacts; Moon-Uranus; and hard Moon-Saturn. Silence rarely means only one thing. Read the signature before assuming rejection.

items.label: Saturn-Heavy Silence
items.body: The person may go quiet under stress to self-protect, manage fear, or avoid vulnerability. This is often overwhelm or fear rather than indifference, though it still needs accountability.

items.label: Water Moon Or Mars
items.body: The person may process internally and withdraw in order to feel before speaking. Pressure can make the withdrawal stronger. Time and emotional safety matter.

items.label: Fixed Sign Silence
items.body: Fixed signs can hold a position for a long time. Taurus may shut down through stubbornness, while Scorpio may withdraw energy as protection or control.

items.label: 12th House Or Neptune
items.body: The person may retreat inward, become hard to reach, blur the issue, or disappear into avoidance. The reading should separate genuine sensitivity from evasion.

items.label: Avoidant Pattern
items.body: Moon-Uranus and hard Moon-Saturn can pull back precisely when closeness increases. Name the pattern without labeling the person as the pattern.

sections.heading: Work Stress
sections.body: For questions about how to support a partner or friend dealing with work pressure, read Saturn for responsibility and pressure, Mars for drive and burnout, the 6th house for daily work, the 10th house for career and ambition, and the Sun for how much identity is tied to achievement.

items.label: Fire Coping
items.body: Pressure makes the person want to act, push through, and regain momentum. Support works best when it helps them channel action rather than simply telling them to slow down.

items.label: Earth Coping
items.body: The person buckles down, gets practical, carries the load stoically, and may not say how heavy it feels. Support works best through practical help and noticing what they will not mention.

items.label: Air Coping
items.body: The person needs to talk it out, compare options, and understand the situation. Support works best through clear conversation and helping them stop spinning in analysis.

items.label: Water Coping
items.body: The person takes stress personally and feels it deeply. Support works best through reassurance first and problem-solving second.

items.label: Saturn-Strong Work Stress
items.body: Capricorn emphasis, 10th-house emphasis, or hard Saturn aspects can show high standards, fear of failure, and silent pressure. The person needs permission not to be perfect, not more pressure.

items.label: Mars-Stressed Work Stress
items.body: Hard Mars signatures can show overwork, burnout, irritability, and a body that needs to discharge pressure. Rest and movement both matter.

items.label: 6th-House Emphasis
items.body: The person may tie identity to usefulness and competence, so a work problem can feel like personal failure rather than a schedule issue.

items.label: Sun-10th Or Capricorn Sun
items.body: Achievement may sit close to the person's core identity. Career setbacks can hit the self, not just the calendar.

sections.heading: Stress And Coping
sections.body: For questions about how someone copes with stress and what actually helps, read the Moon for the real soothing language, dominant element for baseline coping, Saturn for internalized pressure, Mars for discharge, 12th-house or Neptune emphasis for retreat and escape patterns, and modality for how stress is held or moved.

items.label: Fire Stress
items.body: Stress is burned off through action and movement. A project, exercise, or physical outlet usually helps more than sitting still.

items.label: Earth Stress
items.body: Stress settles through routine, the body, and practical order. A walk, a meal, one concrete fix, or steady presence can help.

items.label: Air Stress
items.body: Stress moves through thinking, talking, and naming the problem. A good conversation and a wider perspective can help.

items.label: Water Stress
items.body: Stress needs to be felt through in safety. Gentle presence, no pressure, and permission to retreat and return can help.

items.label: Moon Language
items.body: The Moon shows how the person is actually soothed. Comfort the person in their language, not yours: a Cancer Moon may need care and home, a Capricorn Moon may need competence restored, and an Aquarius Moon may need space.

items.label: Saturn-Heavy Coping
items.body: The person may internalize stress, carry it alone, and ask for help late. Reassure them that support is not weakness.

items.label: Mars-Heavy Coping
items.body: Stress may show as irritability, urgency, or restlessness. Physical discharge helps before emotional processing can land.

items.label: 12th House Or Neptune Coping
items.body: The person may escape, numb out, disappear inward, or blur the problem. Gentle re-grounding matters more than force.

items.label: Modality
items.body: Fixed signs hold stress and release slowly. Mutable signs scatter, worry, and adapt. Cardinal signs want to act on the problem.

sections.heading: How To Support
sections.body: Before supporting someone, read what they need rather than projecting what would help you. The reliable move across every chart is to ask whether they want help thinking it through or whether they simply need to vent.

items.label: Solve
items.body: Fire, earth, and Mars-strong charts often want help fixing the problem. Offer ideas, action, and practical next steps.

items.label: Listen
items.body: Water, Moon-led, and water-Mercury charts often need to feel understood before advice will land. Reflect and validate first.

items.label: Space
items.body: Aquarius, Uranus-strong, and avoidant-pattern signatures may need room to handle the pressure alone. Check in lightly without crowding.

items.label: Presence
items.body: Cancer or Taurus Moons and earth-water charts may need someone simply there. Show up without making fixing the price of support.

sections.heading: Feedback And Advice
sections.body: For questions about how someone takes advice or criticism, read Mercury for how they process input, Saturn for sensitivity to criticism and authority, Mars for defensiveness, and fixed-sign emphasis for resistance. Match how input is given to how the person can actually receive it.

items.label: Saturn-Sensitive
items.body: Hard Saturn to the Sun, Moon, or Mercury can make criticism land loudly because the person is often already self-critical. Start with what is working.

items.label: Mars-Strong Or Fire
items.body: The person can become defensive or combative if feedback feels like an attack. Frame input as being on their side.

items.label: Fixed Signs
items.body: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius signatures may resist being told what to do. Offer, ask, and leave room for choice.

items.label: Mutable Or Air
items.body: The person may be open to input, sometimes too open. Help them filter advice rather than absorb every opinion.

items.label: Mercury-Saturn
items.body: The person may take ideas seriously but feel judged quickly. Be precise, kind, and specific.

sections.heading: App Usage
sections.body: Use this framework to route user-facing relationship questions into the right knowledge: communication to Mercury and 3rd-house overlays, conflict to Mars and hard aspects, affection to Venus-Moon-Mars, silence to Saturn, water signatures, fixed signatures, Neptune, Uranus, and 12th-house overlays, work stress to Saturn-Mars-6th-10th-Sun signatures, and support style to Moon, element, Saturn, and Mars. Phrase outputs as translation and choice, not diagnosis.

sections.heading: Free Will And Pattern
sections.body: The chart describes urges, patterns, inclinations, and developmental material. It does not remove choice. User-facing text should translate chart symbolism into awareness and agency: this is the pattern, this is how it can run unconsciously, and this is how the user can work with it.

sections.heading: Interpretation Order
sections.body: Begin with the whole chart before details: element and mode balance, hemispheres and quadrants, angular emphasis, chart shape, luminaries, Ascendant and chart ruler, house rulers, then major aspects. Do not let a single placement dominate the reading unless the chart repeats it.

sections.heading: Planet As Function
sections.body: Planets describe psychological functions: identity, emotion, thought, desire, action, growth, structure, change, imagination, and transformation. Signs describe style and temperament. Houses describe the life area. Aspects describe how functions cooperate, resist, pressure, or integrate.

sections.heading: Houses As Developmental Fields
sections.body: Houses should be read as fields of experience, not static labels. A planet in a house shows where that planetary function is being practiced, challenged, and made visible in life. Rulers connect one house topic to another and should be used for personalization.

sections.heading: Moon Phases And Nodes
sections.body: Natal Moon phase gives developmental tone: beginning, building, testing, culmination, sharing, revision, or release. The lunar nodes describe familiar patterns and growth direction. Do not make the nodes deterministic; use them to describe what is easy to repeat and what asks for development.

sections.heading: Comparison Before Synastry
sections.body: Before comparing charts, read each person's natal capacity for relationship. Then compare luminaries, Ascendant, personal planets, Saturn, nodes, house overlays, and repeated themes. A relationship reading should explain dynamics without assigning fate or obligation.

sections.heading: Plain-Language Spirituality
sections.body: Spiritual language should stay grounded. Translate symbolic material into lived questions: what pattern is being repeated, what skill is being developed, what responsibility belongs to the user, and what choice is available now.

sections.heading: Principle
sections.body: Name what the relationship is FOR, not a list of contacts. A bond type is only real when several signatures point to it; one aspect is not a bond. Most real relationships are a blend of two or three types.

sections.heading: Bond Types
sections.body: A bond type needs multiple signatures. Most relationships blend two or three types.

items.label: The Spark (chemistry)
items.body: Core signatures: Venus-Mars, Mars-Mars, Sun-Mars contacts; 5th-house overlays. What it is for: passion, attraction, feeling alive. The work: Chemistry is not compatibility. Enjoy it for what it is, or build something underneath it; heat alone says nothing about whether you can live together.

items.label: The Build (partnership)
items.body: Core signatures: supportive Saturn-Sun/Venus, Sun-Moon, 7th-house overlays. What it is for: lasting commitment and structure. The work: Durability over excitement. Keep warmth inside the structure so commitment doesn't curdle into duty.

items.label: The Mirror (recognition)
items.body: Core signatures: Sun-Moon, Moon-Moon, Sun-Ascendant, strong luminary overlays. What it is for: feeling deeply seen and at home. The work: Being recognized isn't the same as a workable relationship. Don't mistake familiarity for ease.

items.label: The Crucible (intense / transformative)
items.body: Core signatures: Pluto contacts (Pluto-Venus/Moon/Sun), 8th-house overlays. What it is for: depth, transformation, being changed by each other. The work: Intensity is not compatibility. The depth is real and high-stakes; watch for control, and let it transform you without dominating you.

items.label: The Fated (karmic)
items.body: Core signatures: Saturn, South Node, Vertex, and nodal contacts. What it is for: a sense of fated-feeling significance, recognition, unfinished business. The work: 'Fated' is a feeling, not a contract. Honor the pull; remember you still choose whether to stay.

items.label: The Teacher (growth)
items.body: Core signatures: Jupiter and Saturn contacts, 9th-house overlays, node links. What it is for: growth, expansion, maturing one another. The work: Peers, not pedestals. The lesson goes both ways or it becomes a power gap.

items.label: The Ease (friendship)
items.body: Core signatures: harmonious Mercury and Venus contacts, 11th-house overlays, shared air. What it is for: companionship and easy liking. The work: Ease can lack heat. Fine if that's what you both want; honest if it isn't.

items.label: The Grind (friction)
items.body: Core signatures: squares and oppositions, Mars-Saturn, Mercury-Mars. What it is for: challenge and growth through abrasion. The work: Friction can be generative or corrosive; the difference is mutual respect. If it's all wear and no spark, name it.

sections.heading: Attachment Lens
sections.body: A supplementary psychological lens, framed as analogues, not clinical diagnosis. Read the Moon, Venus, and Saturn contacts as the bond's attachment tone.

items.label: secure_analogue
items.body: harmonious Moon and Venus contacts; Saturn offering steady support rather than restriction. The bond feels safe and consistent.

items.label: anxious_analogue
items.body: Moon-Pluto, Moon-Mars, Venus-Saturn hard contacts. Craving closeness while fearing loss; push-pull and testing.

items.label: avoidant_analogue
items.body: Moon-Uranus, hard Moon-Saturn, distancing Saturn. Needing space, pulling back when things get close, discomfort with dependence.

sections.heading: Ethics
sections.body: Synastry describes the pull, not the outcome. A bond type needs multiple indicators, never one aspect. Intensity isn't compatibility; fated is a feeling, not a contract; never romanticize control or coercion. Every type carries its work, so the reading stays agency-forward.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body: Use these as synthesis patterns, not verdicts.

items.label: Example 1
items.body: Most bonds blend: Venus-Mars (spark) plus supportive Saturn-Sun (build) is a chemistry-and-commitment bond, the rarer combination that's both exciting and durable. Read both, not one.

items.label: Example 2
items.body: A Pluto-heavy, 8th-house-overlay bond is the Crucible type: it will change both people. That is not the same as easy or good. The work is keeping depth from turning into control.

items.label: Example 3
items.body: South Node plus Saturn contacts make a Fated bond: it feels like you've met before and can't quite leave. Honor the feeling, remember it's a feeling, and choose on purpose.

sections.heading: Integration
sections.body: Reads from synastry_aspects (and the marquee), synastry_house_overlays, synastry_features, and the composite work; the synthesisExamples in composite_chart_marquee show how to layer the composite on top.

sections.heading: Start With Natal Capacity
sections.body: Before comparing two charts, read each person's natal relationship pattern. Synastry cannot override a person's own Moon needs, Venus style, Mars pursuit pattern, Saturn defenses, attachment habits, or unresolved relational wounds. A good match on paper still has to pass through the people living it.

sections.heading: Relationship Coverage
sections.body: The relationship layer covers synastry house overlays, interaspects from Sun through Pluto plus angles, relationship-reading method, composite planets and aspects, cross-chart configurations, and lunar nodes. Use these as separate signals before synthesis; do not collapse them into a single compatibility score.

sections.heading: Relationship Promise
sections.body: Before asking whether two charts work together, identify what each chart is already seeking in partnership. Read the 1st/7th axis, the ruler of the 7th, planets in the 7th, Venus, Mars, the Moon, and Saturn. Synastry lands differently when it answers an actual natal need instead of only creating attraction.

sections.heading: Core Triad
sections.body: Begin comparison with Sun, Moon, and Ascendant. The Sun shows identity and life direction. The Moon shows emotional safety and instinctive needs. The Ascendant shows embodiment and immediate style. If these do not understand each other, later chemistry needs extra support.

sections.heading: Interaspects
sections.body: Prioritize close major aspects between one person's planets and the other's personal planets or angles. Conjunctions fuse and intensify. Oppositions polarize and reveal the other side. Squares create friction and action. Trines ease exchange. Sextiles offer cooperation that must be used.

sections.heading: House Overlays
sections.body: House overlays show where one person lands in the other's life. A partner's planets in your 1st affect identity and embodiment; 4th affects home and roots; 5th affects pleasure and romance; 7th affects partnership; 8th affects intimacy and shared resources; 10th affects reputation and life direction. The house person feels the life area; the planet person supplies the function.

sections.heading: Cross-Chart Configurations
sections.body: After reading individual aspects, check whether the two charts create a larger pattern together. One person's planet can complete a T-square, activate a yod-like pressure point, supply a missing grand-trine leg, or make an existing natal pattern impossible to ignore. These contacts are high signal when tight and tied to personal planets or angles.

sections.heading: Saturn And Durability
sections.body: Saturn contacts can indicate commitment, endurance, duty, and structure, but also inhibition, fear, coldness, delay, or burden. Do not romanticize Saturn as proof of longevity. Ask whether the Saturn person provides structure that supports the bond or pressure that makes affection go cold.

sections.heading: Nodes, Vertex, And 12th House
sections.body: Nodes, Vertex contacts, angle contacts, and 12th-house overlays can describe relationships that feel consequential, familiar, hidden, or unusually timed. Keep this language belief-neutral. Name the pull and the pattern; do not promise a fixed outcome, past-life certainty, or spiritual obligation.

sections.heading: Composite Chart
sections.body: Use the composite chart to describe the relationship as a third entity. Composite Sun describes purpose and identity of the bond. Composite Moon describes the daily emotional climate. Composite Venus describes affection and pleasure. Composite Mars describes conflict and desire. Composite Saturn describes tests, limits, and durability.

sections.heading: Order Of Reading
sections.body: Recommended order: each natal relationship pattern, shared Sun-Moon-Ascendant story, close interaspects, house overlays, Venus-Mars attraction, Saturn durability, nodal or turning-point contacts if used, composite chart, then a grounded summary of strengths, risks, and choices.

sections.heading: Significator Discipline
sections.body: Do not read every planet as equally relevant to every question. Identify the significator first: the planet ruling the relevant house, the planet occupying the house, the chart ruler, the Moon, or another specifically activated planet. Interpretation becomes clearer when the responsible planet is named.

sections.heading: Strength Before Story
sections.body: Before writing interpretation, inspect whether the significator can act. Dignity, angularity, sect, solar phase, speed, direction, reception, and maltreatment or bonification all describe the planet's condition. The same meaning changes tone depending on whether the planet is strong, weak, supported, or obstructed.

sections.heading: Houses Are Places
sections.body: House topics are not moods. They are life places and fields of manifestation. The house tells where the matter happens; the planet tells what agency or force is acting; the sign and dignity describe how that planet behaves; aspects describe help, conflict, or exchange.

sections.heading: Avoid Overpsychologizing
sections.body: Psychological language is useful, but it should not erase concrete topics. If the 2nd house is activated, include resources, income, possessions, livelihood, and value. If the 10th is activated, include career, reputation, authority, and visible action.

sections.heading: Modern Planets Boundary
sections.body: Use Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto as modern overlay factors, not as traditional rulers, time-lords, dignity rulers, sect participants, or primary significators in the traditional spine. If they are surfaced, label the layer as modern.

sections.heading: No Fatalism
sections.body: Traditional method can be concrete without being fatalistic. Name pressure, weakness, and risk plainly, but do not remove agency. Good interpretation shows the condition of the field and the likely forms of manifestation, then names the choices that remain.

sections.heading: Do Not Flatten Transits
sections.body: Do not treat a transit through a natal house as a simple planet-in-house event formula if the output is being labeled traditional. Four things tune a transit through a natal house: whole-sign houses, time-lord activation, sect, and dignity.

sections.heading: Whole-Sign Houses
sections.body: In whole-sign houses, a house is the entire sign counted from the rising sign. The 2nd house is the entire sign after the rising sign. A planet enters that house when it crosses the sign boundary, not when it crosses a quadrant degree cusp.

sections.heading: House System Policy
sections.body: Default transit framing uses whole-sign houses because it best fits the traditional spine and the interpretive data assumes one house equals one whole sign. Keep house-transit entries keyed only by house number so the meaning data stays system-agnostic. The calculation engine may also compute Placidus or another quadrant system as a user option, but that mapping choice belongs to the engine, not the authored entry.

sections.heading: Transits Are Activators
sections.body: A transiting planet lights up the topics of the place it occupies, but the volume comes from time-lord context. Annual profection and zodiacal releasing determine whether the transit is central or background. Mars crossing the 2nd in a year profected to the 2nd, or when Mars is the time-lord, is a real event. A routine pass in an unrelated year is background noise.

sections.heading: Sect Sets The Baseline
sections.body: Day chart means the Sun was above the horizon at birth. Night chart means the Sun was below the horizon. Sect changes the behavior of benefics and malefics. Mars is more constructive in a night chart and more difficult in a day chart. Venus is more constructive in a night chart and still benefic but less cleanly supportive in a day chart.

sections.heading: Dignity Sets The Strength
sections.body: The transiting planet's sign condition modifies the reading as much as sect does, and sect and dignity stack. Domicile and exaltation strengthen delivery. Detriment and fall weaken or distort delivery. A debilitated benefic underdelivers. A dignified malefic does its damage efficiently. The house tells the topic; sect and dignity together describe how it goes.

sections.heading: Modern Overlays
sections.body: There is no traditional Neptune in the seven-planet system. Neptune was discovered in 1846. A product may use Neptune, but Neptune transit content must be labeled as a modern overlay rather than traditional technique.

sections.heading: 6th House Place
sections.body: The 6th is the place of the health affliction itself: illness, injury, disease, accidents, bodily strain, toil, labor, and subordinates. It is cadent, weak, in aversion to the Ascendant, and associated with Bad Fortune. It is also the joy of Mars. Joy is a strength condition, not a softening; a planet in its joy does its job more, and Mars's job here includes sickness and strain. Do not confuse the 6th with the isolating experience around treatment or confinement; that belongs to the 12th.

sections.heading: 12th House Place
sections.body: The 12th describes isolation, retreat, confinement, hidden burdens, and being separated from ordinary life. In health-related timing, the 6th describes the illness, injury, or affliction itself, while the 12th describes the isolating experience that can surround hospitalization, quarantine, institutional care, or being kept apart from the usual world. Keep this distinction descriptive and non-diagnostic.

sections.heading: Transit Ranking Order
sections.body: For traditional timing, transits are last in the ranking stack: natal promise first, then time-lord context, then Solar Return or other annual chart, then real-time transit trigger. This does not make transits unimportant; it explains why some exact transits are loud and others are barely felt.

sections.heading: Traditional Seven Only For Time Lords
